revoke_existing_sessions.description: Applies to this change only and is not stored. When true, Proctor signs out active Sessions that used a sign-in method this change turns off. If this change starts requiring two-step verification for role holders, it also signs out their live Sessions that have not proved a second factor.

role_holder_mfa_required.description: Whether every role holder must use two-step verification. A role holder is any User with a current Role Binding at any scope, system administrators included. A role holder without a second factor who signs in on the web gets a Session that can only set up two-step verification, complete a challenge or sign out. Proctor Desktop refuses that sign-in with `authentication.mfa.enrollment_required`. While the server configuration turns two-step verification off, the requirement is paused and restricts or refuses nobody. Clients may label this switch "Two-step required for staff". It has nothing to do with the staff member Affiliation.

session_absolute_minutes.description: How long a Session may last from sign-in, in minutes. Null uses the deployment default. The value must be at least the deployment minimum, which is longer than the recent sign-in window and the idle minimum, and at most `session_absolute_minutes_maximum`. Shortening it moves running Sessions' deadlines and their credentials' expiry earlier. Lengthening it never extends a running Session.

session_idle_minutes.description: How long a Session may stay unused before it ends, in minutes. Null uses the deployment default. The value must be at least the deployment minimum, which is longer than an access credential lasts and longer than the delay before activity is recorded. It must be at most `session_idle_minutes_maximum` and never longer than the absolute Session length in force. Shortening it moves running Sessions' idle deadlines earlier. Lengthening it never extends a running Session.

expected_current_revision_id.description: The Exam Revision the client is showing. The request fails if another correction replaced it.

participation_id.description: The active Participation ID returned when the Attempt connected.

acknowledged_at.description: When the candidate acknowledged the correction.

current_revision_id.description: The Exam Revision the Sitting delivers now.

revision_id.description: The correction Revision that was acknowledged.

runtime_capabilities.description: What the candidate can do after this acknowledgement.

expected_revision.description: The Exam revision you last saw. If the Exam has changed since, the request fails with a conflict.

user_id.description: The User to make a Manager.

AdministrationCountsResponse.description: Counts for administration navigation. Each count is present only when the caller may list its resource, always with its lower-bound flag.

failed_jobs.description: Operator-visible Jobs that failed and were last updated in the last seven days.

failed_jobs_is_lower_bound.description: True when `failed_jobs` reached 1,000 and there may be more. Present with `failed_jobs`.

failed_mail_deliveries.description: Mail deliveries that ended in the `failed` state. Suppressed and canceled deliveries are not counted.

failed_mail_deliveries_is_lower_bound.description: True when `failed_mail_deliveries` reached 1,000 and there may be more. Present with `failed_mail_deliveries`.

open_onboarding_imports.description: Unexpired administrative onboarding imports not yet completed, canceled, or failed, within the caller's onboarding import visibility. Student progressions are not counted.

open_onboarding_imports_is_lower_bound.description: True when `open_onboarding_imports` reached 1,000 and there may be more. Present with `open_onboarding_imports`.

pending_invitations.description: Pending, unexpired Invitations within the caller's Invitation visibility.

pending_invitations_is_lower_bound.description: True when `pending_invitations` reached 1,000 and there may be more. Present with `pending_invitations`.

delivery_stream_id.description: The native delivery stream this admission opened. Desktop sends it as the security control's stream_id and as the native delivery watermark's source_id.

AffiliationKind.description: The kind of relationship a User has with the Institution. A User can hold several kinds at once, and an Affiliation grants no permissions by itself.

AffiliationListResponse.description: One page of Affiliations, in a fixed order.

items.description: The Affiliations on this page.

archived_at.description: When the Affiliation was archived. An archived Affiliation is never in effect. Omitted unless archived.

end_at.description: When the Affiliation stops being in effect. The Affiliation is no longer in effect at this instant. Omitted while it has no end.

kind.description: The kind of relationship this Affiliation records.

start_at.description: When the Affiliation takes effect. When the request gave no start, this is the time it was created.

updated_at.description: When the Affiliation last changed, for example when it was ended.

user_id.description: The User who holds the Affiliation.

ApplyExamSittingCorrectionRequest.description: The corrected content for one open or paused Sitting.

acknowledgement_required.description: Whether candidates must acknowledge the correction. While an acknowledgement is pending, the operations in `affected_capabilities` are blocked for that candidate.

browser_policy.description: A new Browser Policy. Leave it out to keep the current one. If you send it, it replaces the current policy together with the rest of the correction.

candidate_summary.description: Plain text that tells candidates what changed. No leading or trailing whitespace and no control characters: at most 500 characters and 2000 bytes.

expected_current_revision_id.description: The Exam Revision the Sitting delivers now. The request fails with a conflict if another correction replaced it first.

expected_revision.description: The Sitting's current revision, as last read. The request fails with a conflict if the Sitting has changed since.

instructions_markdown.description: New instructions in Markdown, at most 65536 bytes of UTF-8. Leave it out to keep the current instructions. Send an empty string to clear them. `null` is rejected.

reason.description: Why you are correcting the Exam. It is kept for audit and is never shown to candidates. Send valid UTF-8 with no leading or trailing whitespace: at most 1000 characters and 4000 bytes.

resources.description: Every resource the corrected Exam should have, in order. Resources you leave out are removed. Each `resource_id`, and each `stage_id` you send, must appear only once.

expected_revision.description: The `revision` from your last read of the resource. If the resource has changed since, nothing is archived. Null is rejected.
The Exam revision you last saw. If the Exam has changed since, the request fails with a conflict.

AssistantCall.description: One phase of a tool call: requested, decision (an approval answer), reserved (a command slot), completed, or applied (a Pair proposal matched by a candidate batch). A command's reservation names its assistant:N process tag before the process starts. Its completion carries the exit code; the Workspace journal names the call in the author of every change an Agent edit made.

arguments.description: The arguments as the model sent them, on the requested phase.

result.description: Bounded tool result text. On a completed propose_edit call with outcome proposed, this is a JSON object serialized as text, with path (workspace path), base_content_version (the expected current file version, or an empty string for a new file), sha256 (lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the full replacement), size_bytes (replacement UTF-8 byte count), and diff (a complete unified replacement diff). A matching ordinary candidate batch adds an applied phase to this call; the workspace write remains authored by the candidate. Other tools return text, and an applied phase contains a matching marker rather than the proposal object.

AssistantInventory.description: The transcript's record and byte counts, its gaps, and a SHA-256 digest chained over every record in order.

AssistantPolicy.description: Frozen assistant allowances. Instructions and avoided concepts are visible to managers only. Only Tutor is currently available.

profile_id.description: An assistant profile ID when enabled; empty when disabled.

AssistantProfileListResponse.description: One page of the collection in its stable order.

pseudonymize.description: Defaults to true when omitted or null. Candidate identity is never sent to a provider.

AssistantRecord.description: One transcript record, a turn or a tool call. Gap marks a record the server wrote for a turn that ended abnormally, such as at a seal or a provider failure.

next_cursor.description: Token for the next page. Send it back unchanged as `cursor`, and do not parse it. Omitted on the last page.

AssistantTurn.description: A candidate message, or part of a reply. A reply's text and its end are separate records; the final record carries the stop reason and the turn's usage, which includes any rewrite.

replayed.description: Whether this answers a retry of an earlier send.

AssistantUsage.description: Tokens a turn used. Estimated marks a figure the server estimated because the provider's count was lost.

session_inputs.description: Writes into assistant sessions. A poll does not count.

session_seconds.description: Total settled duration from the session-ended records, in whole seconds.

sessions.description: Assistant session reservations, also counted in commands.

AttemptConfigurationCandidate.description: Sent as `initial_configuration` when Proctor Desktop connects to an Exam Attempt over the WebSocket, so no HTTP operation uses it. A complete proposed Attempt Configuration, at most 16 KiB once encoded. At first admission the server checks the acknowledged User Settings revision, the exact Desktop build and target, the packaged settings registry and manifest, and that every item is safe for candidates. Values out of range are rejected, not adjusted. The digest of the fixed configuration covers this whole object, including where it came from.

approved_commands.description: IDs of approved commands from the Desktop settings catalog, sorted and without duplicates. Raw key chords are rejected.

approved_keybindings.description: IDs of approved keybindings from the Desktop settings catalog, sorted and without duplicates. Each keybinding must map to one of the approved commands. Raw key chords are rejected.

desktop_build.description: ID of the Desktop build. It must match the admitted build.

desktop_target.description: Target platform of the Desktop build. It must match the admitted build.

manifest_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the Attempt Configuration manifest packaged with the Desktop build, prefixed with sha256:. It must match the admitted build.

presentation.description: Presentation settings to fix for the Attempt.

registry_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the Desktop settings registry packaged with the build, prefixed with fnv1a64:. It must match the admitted build.

user_settings_revision.description: Revision of the User Settings Document the configuration was built from.

AttemptConfigurationPresentation.description: Presentation settings fixed for the Attempt. Stricter accessibility needs may change how they are applied at run time, never these stored values.

announcement_mode.description: How much detail the interface announces to assistive technology.

color_theme.description: Color theme. hcLight and hcDark are the high-contrast themes.

cursor_blinking.description: How the editor text cursor blinks. solid means it does not blink.

cursor_style.description: Shape of the editor text cursor.

editor_line_height_px.description: Editor line height, in pixels. Its limits don't depend on the font size.

prefer_high_contrast.description: Whether the candidate prefers high-contrast colors.

reduced_motion.description: Whether to reduce motion and animation.

screen_reader_mode.description: Whether the editor is optimized for screen readers. auto lets the client decide.

AttemptConnectionState.description: Whether a Connection is open or closed.

AttemptEnvironmentDesired.description: What the Attempt's facts ask the execution environment to be.

AttemptEnvironmentState.description: What the execution environment's machine is doing now.

detail.description: The author's own evidence object of at most 64 KiB, stored as given.

kind.description: `execution.process` is a slice of the command log, `execution.input` recorded terminal input, `execution.gap` missing coverage, `execution.overwritten` a guest change lost to a newer Workspace version, and `execution.refused` a guest change the Workspace refused.

observed_at.description: The author's observation time, never later than recorded_at.

sequence.description: The position of the record in its author's stream of this kind.

AttemptEvidenceInventory.description: The Attempt evidence the Submission seal fixed: kept records and their canonical bytes, how many are gaps, how many appends were refused over the per-Attempt bounds, and a digest chained over the kept records in order. Review finalization binds it.

AttemptParticipationState.description: Whether a Participation is still active or has ended.

AuditAction.description: Name of an audited action. Later versions may add values. Show your own label for each value, and a general message for one you don't recognize.

AuditEventResponse.description: One audit record you can see, without sensitive detail.

action.description: The action that was attempted, named like a permission, such as `class.members.manage`.

actor_id.description: The User who performed the action. Omitted for actions the system took on its own.

authentication_method.description: How the actor signed in, such as `password`. Omitted for Academic Unit auditors.

client_type.description: Kind of client the actor used, such as `web` or `desktop`. Omitted for Academic Unit auditors.

error_code.description: Error code of a failed action. Internal error details are never included.

ip_address.description: The client's IP address, when recorded. Omitted for Academic Unit auditors.

node_id.description: The server node that handled the action. Omitted for Academic Unit auditors.

reason.description: Reason given when an account was disabled. Present only on that Event, only when a reason was given, and only for Institution-wide audit readers.

request_id.description: ID of the request that caused the action, when it came in over HTTP or WebSocket. Omitted for Academic Unit auditors.

resource.description: The record the action was about.

scope_id.description: The scope the permission check used, when the action belongs to a scope.

scope_type.description: Kind of scope the permission check used, when the action belongs to a scope.

session_id.description: The Session the action was made in, when recorded. It is an ID, never a credential. Omitted for Academic Unit auditors.

status.description: Outcome of the action, `attempt` (not recorded yet), `success` or `fail`.

summary.description: One sentence describing the Event in the request's language, for display only. Programs should read the Event's codes instead. People and records appear by name only if you could see them now, and an unfinished or failed Event says so.

updated_at.description: Time the Event's outcome was last updated.

user_agent.description: The client's User-Agent header, up to 512 characters. Omitted for Academic Unit auditors.

AuditListResponse.description: One page of audit Events you can see.

items.description: The Events on this page.

next_cursor.description: Token for the next page. Send it back unchanged as `cursor`. Omitted on the last page.

total.description: Number of Events that match the filters and that you can see, across all pages. Sent on the first page only. Counting stops at 10,000, and then `total_is_lower_bound` is true.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when `total` reached 10,000 and there may be more. Sent with `total`.

password.description: Whether the User has a local password.

providers.description: The external identities linked to the User.

display_name.description: The provider's display name.

id.description: The ID of this linked external identity. Use it to unlink the identity.

provider_id.description: The ID of the configured provider this identity signs in through.

type.description: The provider's protocol, such as oidc or cas.

session.description: The Session that was created or refreshed.

tokens.description: The access and refresh tokens. Left out when the credentials were set as browser cookies instead.

user.description: The signed-in User's profile. Present after sign-in and left out after a refresh or Desktop code exchange.

access_expires_at.description: When the access token stops working.

access_token.description: The access token for API requests. Treat it as a secret.

refresh_expires_at.description: When the refresh token stops working.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token. Use it once to get a new token pair. Treat it as a secret.

token_type.description: The authorization scheme to send the tokens with. Bearer for CLI Sessions. DPoP for Desktop Sessions, which must also send a DPoP proof with each request.

chunk_sha256.description: The lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of every chunk, in order.

return_to.description: The path on this server to return to, such as /settings/authentication. It must start with a single slash and have no host or fragment. Defaults to /.

BootstrapAdministratorRequest.description: Profile of the first administrator account.

description.description: Optional free-text description of the Institution.

display_name.description: Name shown to people.

name.description: Short machine name for the Institution.

Each event digest covers only its own record, so it does not depend on how events are batched or sent.

events.description: The events, 1 to 64, in ascending sequence order.

generation.description: Participation Generation that started the source.

BrowserActivityDisclosure.description: Localized collection notice, not consent or history-read authority. Zero days means no configured automatic expiry. Holds, approval, grace and source reconciliation still apply; minimized integrity evidence can have a different period.

block_reason.description: Why the navigation was blocked. Null unless kind is blocked_top_level_navigation.

client_occurred_at.description: When the event happened, by the client clock.

generation.description: Participation Generation the source belonged to.

A successful navigation, or an HTTPS one the policy blocked, has an HTTPS host, a port only when it isn't the default, and a path. A blocked HTTP navigation has the same parts with the scheme http. Any other scheme that isn't allowed keeps only its lowercase scheme, with empty host and path. A block for invalid_url has empty scheme, host and path. Query strings, fragments, user information, local paths and scheme content are never kept. Null for browser_opened and browser_closed.

path.description: URL path. Empty when only the scheme is kept.

redirect_from_sequence.description: Sequence number of the earlier event in the same source that this redirect came from. Null when the event is not a redirect.

source_session_id.description: ID of the browser activity source that recorded the event.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Omitted on the last page. Send it back unchanged as cursor.

status.description: Status of the source after the declaration.

A redirect names an earlier successful navigation of the same source and policy. The server checks every record against the browser policy and rejects URLs that are not already in minimal form, unsafe integers, and times that are not UTC with millisecond precision.

client_occurred_at.description: When it happened by the Desktop's clock, in UTC with millisecond precision.

policy_revision_id.description: The Exam Revision whose browser policy was in force.

sequence.description: Position of the record in this browser source. Each record's number is higher than the last.

client_occurred_at.description: When it happened by the Desktop's clock, in UTC with millisecond precision.

policy_revision_id.description: The Exam Revision whose browser policy was in force.

sequence.description: Position of the record in this browser source. Each record's number is higher than the last.

client_occurred_at.description: When it happened by the Desktop's clock, in UTC with millisecond precision.

location.description: The page address with the query and fragment removed.

port.description: Port number. Omitted when it is the scheme's default port.

scheme.description: URL scheme in lowercase, such as `https`.

matched_rule_id.description: The browser policy rule that allowed the page.

policy_revision_id.description: The Exam Revision whose browser policy was in force.

sequence.description: Position of the record in this browser source. Each record's number is higher than the last.

client_occurred_at.description: When it happened by the Desktop's clock, in UTC with millisecond precision.

location.description: The page address with the query and fragment removed.

host.description: Host name in lowercase. Empty when the scheme has no host.

port.description: Port number. Omitted when it is the scheme's default port.

scheme.description: URL scheme in lowercase, such as `https`.

matched_rule_id.description: The browser policy rule that allowed the target page.

policy_revision_id.description: The Exam Revision whose browser policy was in force.

redirect_from_sequence.description: The `sequence` of the earlier navigation that redirected here.

sequence.description: Position of the record in this browser source. Each record's number is higher than the last.

client_occurred_at.description: When it happened by the Desktop's clock, in UTC with millisecond precision.

kind.description: The browser blocked a page the policy does not allow.

location.description: The page address with the query and fragment removed.

host.description: Host name in lowercase. Empty when the scheme has no host.

port.description: Port number. Omitted when it is the scheme's default port.

scheme.description: URL scheme in lowercase, such as `https`.

matched_rule_id.description: The browser policy rule that matched the page, when one did. Never sent for `scheme_not_allowed` or `invalid_url`.

policy_revision_id.description: The Exam Revision whose browser policy was in force.

redirect_from_sequence.description: The `sequence` of the earlier navigation that tried to redirect here. Required when `block_reason` is `redirect_not_allowed`.

sequence.description: Position of the record in this browser source. Each record's number is higher than the last.

BrowserDeliverySummaryResult.description: The recorded summary, with the source's current status.

status.description: Status of the source after the summary.

BrowserEventReceipt.description: Receipt for one stored browser activity event.

event_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the event record, prefixed with sha256:. It does not depend on how events were batched or sent.

received_at.description: When the server first stored the event.

sequence.description: Sequence number of the event in its source.

BrowserIntegrityEvidence.description: A copy of one blocked navigation, kept as evidence. It can't change, and it carries its own policy revision and digest, so it stays readable after ordinary browser activity is deleted.

event.description: The blocked navigation event, reduced to the minimum needed as evidence.

policy_digest.description: The digest of that Browser Policy, as `sha256:` followed by lowercase hex.

policy_revision_id.description: The Exam Revision whose Browser Policy was in force.

rule_id.description: The Browser Policy rule the blocked navigation matched.

source_session_id.description: The browser session that reported the event.

BrowserIntegrityGroup.description: The browser rule a `browser_navigation` Flag groups its evidence by, for one Participation and Browser Policy. The overflow times are left out while every matching event was kept. Counts do not include client summaries the server did not keep.

overflow_first_received_at.description: When the server received the first matching event that was not kept as evidence. Present only when some events were not kept, together with `overflow_last_received_at`.

overflow_last_received_at.description: When the server received the last matching event that was not kept as evidence. Present only when some events were not kept.

participation_id.description: The Participation in which the blocked navigations happened.

policy_revision_id.description: The Exam Revision whose Browser Policy contains the rule.

rule_id.description: The Browser Policy rule that the blocked navigations matched.

BrowserIntegrityOverflow.description: Valid browser events that were not kept because the Attempt already has 256 browser Flag groups. This is not another Flag, and the count is of events, not of the groups they would have formed.

first_received_at.description: When the server received the first event that was not kept.

last_received_at.description: When the server received the last event that was not kept.

reason.description: Why the events were not kept. `group_capacity` means the 256-group limit was reached.

validated_event_count.description: The number of valid events that were not kept.

display_name.description: The new account's display name.

handle.description: The `handle` returned when the browser acceptance started.

locale.description: The account's language, as a language tag such as `en`.

password.description: The password for the new account. It must meet the password policy.

timezone.description: The account's time zone, such as `Europe/Paris`. Omit it to use the time zone the inviter suggested.

username.description: The username for the new account.

handle.description: The `handle` returned when the browser acceptance started.

claim.description: The one-time claim from the Invitation email.

class_display_name.description: Display name of the Class a student Class Invitation enrolls the invitee in. Omitted for every other purpose.

email.description: The normalized address the Invitation was sent to. Account-creating acceptance gives the new account this address; no acceptance operation takes an address from the browser.

expires_at.description: When the browser handle stops working.

handle.description: The browser handle to send when accepting. It works only together with the proof cookie set on this response, and only until `expires_at`.

purpose.description: The purpose of the Invitation being accepted.

requirement.description: What accepting needs. `account` means the browser creates a new account, for student Class and teacher Academic Unit Invitations. `session` means the invitee must be signed in, for Role Invitations.

BrowserPolicy.description: The websites candidates may open in the Exam browser. A disabled policy has only enabled set to false. An enabled policy also names a start rule and lists up to 128 rules, within 32 KiB. When several rules match a page, Proctor picks the one with the longest path prefix, then an exact host over a subdomain match, then the longest hostname, then the alphabetically smallest rule ID. The order of the rules array never decides the match.

enabled.description: True to give candidates the Exam browser with these rules. False turns the Exam browser off.

rules.description: The allowed sites. Present only when enabled is true.

start_rule_id.description: The rule_id of the rule the Exam browser starts from. It must match one of the rules. Present only when enabled is true.

BrowserPolicyRule.description: One site, or part of a site, that candidates may open in the Exam browser.

allow_redirects.description: Whether the Exam browser may follow a redirect that this rule matches.

blocked_navigation_outcome.description: What happens when a candidate is blocked from opening a page under this rule. record only records it. integrity_evidence also creates Integrity Evidence for review.

host_match.description: exact matches only the origin's host. exact_and_subdomains also matches every subdomain of it.

institution_http_exception.description: Set to true only for an HTTP rule whose host and explicit port are the same as this installation's own HTTPS origin. It must be false for HTTPS rules. It never allows credentials to be sent over HTTP.

origin.description: The scheme, host and optional port of the site, in ASCII. Use HTTPS. HTTP is accepted only with institution_http_exception. Leave out the default port (443 for HTTPS, 80 for HTTP). The host must be DNS labels or an IPv4 address. Internationalized names, punycode, IPv6, a trailing dot, credentials, a query, a fragment and any path other than / are rejected. A port is a decimal number from 1 to 65535 with no leading zeros. An IP address works only with exact host matching.

path_prefix.description: The ASCII path the rule covers. It matches that exact path and anything below it at a slash boundary. One trailing slash is removed when you save, unless the path is just /. Dot segments, broken percent escapes and encoded slashes or backslashes are rejected. Repeated slashes, percent escapes of unreserved characters and the letter case of percent escapes are kept as written and compared exactly.

rule_id.description: Your name for this rule, unique within the policy. Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.

BrowserReceiptPage.description: One page of stored event receipts.

items.description: Receipts on this page, in ascending sequence order.

BrowserSourceList.description: Browser activity sources of one Participation, in start order.

items.description: Source statuses on this page.

BrowserSourceSessionID.description: Lowercase version 4 UUID that Proctor Desktop assigns to one browser source.

BrowserSourceStatus.description: Status of one browser activity source, at most 16 KiB. The policy and how the source started can't change. The server alone decides when it closes, and after that history can be uploaded only until a fixed deadline. The remaining-start counters cover the whole Participation, and neither retries nor retirement give starts back. The status grants no permission to navigate.

allocated_through_sequence.description: Highest sequence number reserved for the source so far.

budget_scope.description: Whether the Participation limit or the lifetime Attempt limit caused summary_only. Null while collecting.

closure.description: Whether and how the server closed the source.

declaration_revision.description: Number of gap and final declarations recorded for the source. Send it as expected_revision in the next declaration.

detail_mode.description: collecting while individual events are kept. summary_only after a delivery limit was reached or detailed delivery was stopped, when only summary counts are kept.

generation.description: Participation Generation that started the source.

highest_contiguous_sequence.description: Highest sequence number such that every event from 1 up to it has been received.

highest_seen_sequence.description: Highest sequence number the server has received.

missing_ranges.description: Up to the first 32 ranges of positions that are neither received nor declared missing, in ascending order.

missing_ranges_truncated.description: True when there are more missing ranges than missing_ranges lists.

participation_id.description: ID of the Attempt Participation that started the source.

policy_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of that Browser Policy, prefixed with sha256:.

policy_revision_id.description: ID of the Exam Revision whose Browser Policy the source uses.

predecessor_source_session_id.description: ID of the source this one replaced. Null when start_transition is initial.

remaining_correction_starts.description: How many more sources this Participation may start after a policy correction. It starts at 32.

remaining_runtime_reset_starts.description: How many more sources this Participation may start after a runtime reset. It starts at 16.

runtime_reset_reason.description: Why the browser runtime was reset. Present only when start_transition is runtime_reset, otherwise null.

server_time.description: Server time when the status was read.

settled_through_sequence.description: Highest sequence number such that every position up to it has been received or declared missing.

source_session_id.description: ID of the browser activity source.

start_transition.description: Why the source started. initial for the first source, policy_correction after a live correction to the Browser Policy, and runtime_reset after the browser runtime was reset.

summary.description: The latest summary of undelivered events. Null until the client sends one.

first_unretained_at.description: When the first undelivered event was produced, by the client clock. Omitted when unknown.

last_unretained_at.description: When the most recent undelivered event was produced, by the client clock. Omitted when unknown.

summary_sequence.description: Number of this summary. Each changed summary uses a higher number.

unretained_record_count.description: Total number of events produced but not delivered so far.

summary_only_reason.description: Which limit was reached, or local_loss_inventory_exhausted when the client stopped detailed delivery. Null while collecting.

terminal_missing_through_sequence.description: Positions up to this one that were not received are permanently missing, for example after the upload deadline passed. Zero when there is no such cutoff.

BrowserSubmissionSettlement.description: The server's summary of browser activity across every source and Participation in the Attempt. Activity that arrives late but is still accepted updates this summary. It never changes the submitted work.

incomplete_source_count.description: The number of sources with missing or unretained activity. At most `source_count`. A source can be both pending and incomplete.

inventory_revision.description: Starts at 1 and goes up each time the server updates this summary.

pending_source_count.description: The number of sources that can still deliver activity. At most `source_count`.

source_count.description: The number of browser activity sources across all Participations in the Attempt.

state.description: `not_applicable` when the Attempt has no browser sources. Otherwise `pending` while any source can still deliver, then `incomplete` if any source is missing data, or `settled` when every source is complete.

BuildInfoResponse.description: Version and build details of the server binary that answered.

build_time.description: When the binary was built, as recorded at build time.

commit.description: Source commit the binary was built from.

go_version.description: Version of Go used to build the binary.

version.description: Proctor release version, or a development version string.

CancelExamSittingRequest.description: The Sitting revision you last read and a private reason for canceling.

expected_revision.description: The Sitting's current revision, as last read. The request fails with a conflict if the Sitting has changed since.

reason.description: Why you are canceling. It is kept for audit and is never shown to candidates. Send valid UTF-8 with no leading or trailing whitespace: 1 to 1000 characters and at most 4000 bytes.

CandidateAttemptConfiguration.description: The presentation settings and approved command IDs the candidate interface uses for this Attempt. The revision and digest identify the configuration, which was fixed at admission. Where it came from (the Desktop build, settings catalog and User Settings) is sent only to the Desktop that owns the Attempt.

approved_commands.description: IDs of approved commands from the Desktop settings catalog, sorted and without duplicates. Raw key chords are rejected.

approved_keybindings.description: IDs of approved keybindings from the Desktop settings catalog, sorted and without duplicates. Each keybinding must map to one of the approved commands. Raw key chords are rejected.

attempt_configuration_revision.description: Server-assigned revision of the Attempt Configuration.

digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the full Attempt Configuration, prefixed with sha256:.

CandidateBrowserCapability.description: Whether the integrated browser can be used right now. Policy details are left out when the browser is disabled.

policy_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the Browser Policy that applies, prefixed with sha256:. Omitted when state is disabled.

policy_revision_id.description: ID of the Exam Revision whose Browser Policy applies. Omitted when state is disabled.

state.description: disabled means the Exam has no integrated browser. available means it can be used. sitting_paused means the Sitting is paused. acknowledgement_required means a live correction to the Browser Policy must be acknowledged first. temporarily_unavailable means the server could not start a new browser activity source after the browser was reset, for example because a limit was reached.

CandidateBrowserPolicy.description: The current Browser Policy and its collection notice, which has its own revision. The revision number only goes up. The digest, prefixed with sha256:, covers only the policy itself, not its revision details or the notice. A disabled policy has no start_rule_id or rules.

browser_activity_disclosure.description: Notice to show the candidate about what browser activity is collected and how long it is kept.

enabled.description: Whether the integrated browser is turned on for this Exam.

policy_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the Browser Policy, prefixed with sha256:.

policy_revision_id.description: ID of the Exam Revision this Browser Policy comes from, which is the current Revision of the Sitting.

policy_revision_number.description: Number of the Exam Revision this Browser Policy comes from. It only goes up.

rules.description: Rules that list where the browser may go. Present only when enabled is true.

start_rule_id.description: ID of the rule the browser starts from. Present only when enabled is true.

CandidateCapability.description: A group of candidate operations that a live correction can hold back until it is acknowledged. `browser` covers the exam browser, `submission` covers submitting the Attempt, and `workspace` covers changing the Workspace.

CandidateDepartureCapability.description: Whether the candidate may leave the Attempt now.

allowed.description: Always false while the Attempt is in progress.

reason.description: Why the candidate may not leave.

For ignored, what ignored it: .proctorignore, default (the default patterns, while the Workspace has no .proctorignore that parses) or parent_not_synced. For refused, the Workspace's public error code, such as exam.attempt.workspace.size_limit or exam.attempt.workspace.content_conflict.

status.description: ignored stays on the machine; refused was not accepted by the Workspace.

paths.description: The guest paths that are not in the Attempt Workspace, oldest first.

projection_cursor.description: The Workspace journal cursor the machine holds.

waiting_since.description: When the current wait for an execution host with room began.

CandidateExamAccessState.description: Whether the candidate can enter now, and if not, why. `joinable` and `resumable` mean they can start or continue. `sitting_paused` means the Sitting is paused, and `await_reallow` means the Attempt is suspended until a manager lets the candidate back in. `blocked_by_other_attempt` means another unfinished Attempt is in the way, and `not_eligible` means the candidate can't take part, for example because they left the Class or manage the Exam. `not_open`, `submitted`, `result_available` and `ended` follow the Sitting and Submission.

suspension_reason_code.description: Why the Attempt is suspended, or null when it is not suspended.

allowed_actions.description: The action to offer now, if any. `enter` and `resume` appear only for a Session from a registered Proctor Desktop.

attempt.description: The candidate's Attempt, or null if they have none.

class.description: The Class the Sitting is for.

result.description: The released result, or null until it is released.

sitting_reason_code.description: The reason code recorded with the Sitting's current state, or null when there is none.

submission.description: The candidate's Submission, or null if there is none yet.

display_name.description: Name shown to people.

released_at.description: Time the result was released to the candidate.

CandidateExamAllowedAction.description: An action the client can offer now: start the Attempt (`enter`), continue it (`resume`), or open the released result (`view_result`).

browser_policy.description: The current Browser Policy and its collection notice. Null while the candidate still has to acknowledge a live correction that changes the Browser Policy.

candidate_runtime_capabilities.description: What the candidate may do right now, such as change the Workspace or submit.

exam_sitting_id.description: ID of the Exam Sitting the Attempt belongs to.

instructions_markdown.description: Exam Instructions from the current Exam Revision of the Sitting, in Markdown.

live_corrections.description: Live corrections published to the Sitting after the Attempt was admitted.

resources.description: Exam Resources from the current Exam Revision, in position order.

CandidateExamResourceResponse.description: One Exam Resource the candidate can open during the Attempt.

description_markdown.description: Description of the resource written by the Exam author, in Markdown. Empty when the author gave none.

display_name.description: Name of the resource to show the candidate.

id.description: ID of the Exam Resource. Use it to fetch the resource content.

media_type.description: Media type of the resource content.

position.description: Zero-based place of the resource in the list. Resources are returned in this order.

size.description: Size of the resource content in bytes.

CandidateExamRevisionCapability.description: The Exam Revisions that apply to the Attempt.

acknowledgement_required.description: True when at least one live correction still needs the candidate to acknowledge it.

admission_revision_id.description: ID of the Exam Revision the Attempt was admitted with. Capacity limits come from this Revision.

current_revision_id.description: ID of the current Exam Revision of the Sitting. Instructions, resources and the Browser Policy come from this Revision.

CandidateExamWorkspaceItemResponse.description: One file or directory in the Attempt Workspace. File-only members are omitted for directories.

content_version.description: Workspace Content Version of the current file content. Present only for files. Send it back unchanged when you replace or delete the file.

id.description: ID of the Workspace Entry. It stays the same when the entry is renamed or moved.

kind.description: Whether the entry is a file or a directory.

media_type.description: Media type declared for the file. Present only for files.

path.description: Current Workspace Path of the entry.

sha256.description: Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the file content. Present only for files.

size.description: File size in bytes. Present only for files.

items.description: Files and directories on this page, in ascending path order. Empty when refresh_required is true.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Omitted on the last page. Send it back unchanged as cursor. It holds no Workspace path.

refresh_required.description: True when the Workspace changed after the first page was read. The page is then empty, and you must start again from the first page.

workspace_cursor.description: Workspace Cursor this page reflects. Use it as workspace_cursor when you list changes made after this listing.

acknowledged_at.description: When the candidate acknowledged the correction. Present only when acknowledgement_state is acknowledged.

acknowledgement_required.description: Whether the candidate must acknowledge the correction before using the affected capabilities again.

affected_capabilities.description: Capabilities the correction affects. When acknowledgement is required, they stay blocked until the candidate acknowledges it.

changed_areas.description: Which parts of the Exam the correction changed.

revision_number.description: Number of the Exam Revision that carries the correction.

connection_limit.description: The maximum concurrent connections for this Attempt on one node.

attempt_configuration.description: The Attempt Configuration fixed when the candidate was admitted.

browser.description: Whether the integrated browser can be used now.

departure.description: Whether the candidate may leave the Attempt now.

exam_revision.description: The Exam Revision the Attempt was admitted with, and the current one.

focus_loss_collection_enabled.description: Whether the Exam collects Focus Loss observations from the client.

interaction_state.description: interactive while the Sitting is Open. sitting_paused while it is Paused, when Workspace changes and submission are blocked.

pending_correction_capabilities.description: Capabilities blocked by live corrections that still need acknowledgement, sorted and without duplicates. Empty when nothing is waiting.

schema_version.description: Version of this object's layout. Currently always 1.

server_time.description: Server time when these capabilities were worked out.

submission_allowed.description: Whether the candidate may submit now. False while the Sitting is paused or a correction that affects submission awaits acknowledgement.

workspace_mutation_allowed.description: Whether the candidate may change the Workspace now. False while the Sitting is paused or a correction that affects the Workspace awaits acknowledgement.

exit_code.description: The exit status of a terminal that exited on its own.

exit_signal.description: The signal that ended a terminal that exited by one.

input_offset.description: How many bytes of input the terminal has taken; the next INPUT is written at it.

number.description: The terminal's number on the current machine, which addresses it in the terminal routes.

expected_workspace_cursor.description: Required exactly when a mutation deletes a directory recursively; the Workspace Cursor the batch starts from.

content.description: One body per create_file and replace_file mutation, in manifest order.

A create names its entry by path only: the server chooses its entry_id, returned in the change.

changes.description: One journal change per mutation, in batch order, at consecutive cursors.

CandidateWorkspaceJournalEntryResponse.description: One change the server accepted in the Attempt Workspace.

content_version.description: Workspace Content Version of the file after the change. Present when a file is created, replaced or moved. Omitted for directories and deletions.

cursor.description: Workspace Cursor of this change. Cursors go up by one with each change, with no gaps.

entry_id.description: ID of the Workspace Entry that changed.

kind.description: Whether the changed entry is a file or a directory.

new_path.description: Path of the entry after the change. Present for create_file, create_directory, replace_file and move_entry. Omitted for delete_entry.

old_path.description: Path of the entry before the change. Present for replace_file, move_entry and delete_entry. For replace_file it equals new_path.

recursive.description: True when this deletion removes the directory at old_path and everything inside it, meaning every path that starts with old_path followed by a slash. Apply the whole removal at this one cursor.

current_cursor.description: Latest Workspace Cursor of the Workspace when the server read this page.

items.description: Changes in ascending cursor order. Empty when refresh_required is true.

password.description: The new local password. It must meet the password rules and must not contain the username, the part of the email address before the @, or the person's name. When the server keeps a password history, it must not match a recent password.

email.description: The new address. It must be a valid email address that no other User has.

previous.description: The student's earlier enrollment in the same Academic Period that this request ended, for a transfer or progression. Omitted when there was none.
