redirect_url.description: The provider's sign-in address. Send the browser there to sign in again.

expires_at.description: The verification deadline.

provider_display_name.description: The provider that confirmed the first factor.

purpose.description: The sign-in that needs a second factor.

user_display_name.description: The account confirmed by the provider.

FocusLossPolicy.description: When leaving the Exam window counts against a candidate. Each time focus is lost for at least the minimum duration is one incident. Reaching the incident count within the window triggers the outcome.

enabled.description: True to apply this rule during Attempts.

incident_count.description: How many incidents within the window trigger the outcome.

minimum_duration_milliseconds.description: The shortest focus loss that counts as an incident, in milliseconds.

outcome.description: What happens when the threshold is reached. flag marks the Attempt for review. flag_and_warn also warns the candidate. flag_and_suspend also suspends the Attempt.

window_milliseconds.description: The rolling time window in which incidents are counted, in milliseconds.

approved_commands.description: Sorted unique approved catalog IDs; keybindings must resolve to selected commands. Raw key chords are rejected.

approved_keybindings.description: Sorted unique approved catalog IDs; keybindings must resolve to selected commands. Raw key chords are rejected.

status.description: The successful health state. Readiness answers `degraded` when an enabled plugin has failed: the node still serves, without that plugin. The server log and the `proctor_plugin_state` metric name the plugin.

ID.description: A Proctor identifier, 26 lowercase z-base-32 characters. Compare it as an exact string.

InitialAccessPolicyResponse.description: The first Access Policy, which controls how people sign in and join.

desktop_authorization_enabled.description: Whether Proctor Desktop can sign in through the browser. True after bootstrap.

invitation_admission_enabled.description: Whether Invitations can admit people. True after bootstrap.

invitation_local_credential_enabled.description: Whether accepting an Invitation can set a Proctor password. True after bootstrap.

local_login_enabled.description: Whether people can sign in with a Proctor password. True after bootstrap.

public_registration_enabled.description: Whether people can sign themselves up. False after bootstrap.

revision.description: Version number of the policy. It is 1 after bootstrap.

InstallationBootstrapResult.description: Everything bootstrap created. A successful response always has every member.

role_binding.description: The grant of the System Administrator Role to the first administrator, at the Institution.

InstallationStateResponse.description: When setup happened and the IDs it created.

InstallationStatusResponse.description: Whether the installation has been set up.

archived_at.description: Time the Institution was archived. Omitted while it is active.

description.description: Free-text description. It can be empty.

display_name.description: Name shown to people.

name.description: Short machine name of the Institution.

updated_at.description: Time of the latest change to the Institution.

InvitationAcceptanceResponse.description: The account and the relationships that accepting the Invitation created.

academic_unit_member_id.description: The Academic Unit membership acceptance created. Present for teacher Academic Unit Invitations.

affiliation_id.description: The Affiliation acceptance created. Present for student Class and teacher Academic Unit Invitations.

class_member_id.description: The Class enrollment acceptance created. Present for student Class Invitations.

replayed.description: True when this request repeated an acceptance that had already succeeded, and the stored outcome was returned.

role_binding_id.description: The Role Binding acceptance created. Present for teacher Academic Unit, Academic Unit Role and Institution Role Invitations.

user_id.description: The User who accepted. For a student or teacher Invitation, this is the new account.

InvitationAdministrationListResponse.description: One page of Invitations. Only the first page carries `total`.

items.description: The Invitations on this page.

total.description: How many Invitations match the filters and your visibility across all pages. Present only on the first page. Counting stops at 10,000, and then `total_is_lower_bound` is true.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when counting stopped at 10,000 and there may be more. Present with `total`.

InvitationAdministrationResponse.description: An Invitation as administrators see it, with its recipient, lifecycle and latest delivery. It never includes the claim, the rendered email or mail provider details.

academic_period_id.description: The Academic Period of that Class. Present only for `student_class`.

academic_unit_id.description: The Academic Unit a teacher or Academic Unit Role Invitation applies to. Present only for those purposes.

accepted_user_id.description: The User who accepted the Invitation. Present only once accepted.

class_id.description: The Class a student Class Invitation enrolls the student in. Present only for `student_class`.

delivery.description: The latest email delivery of the Invitation. Omitted when there is none.

email.description: The address the Invitation was sent to.

end_at.description: When the relationship the Invitation grants ends. Omitted when it has no end.

expires_at.description: When the Invitation can no longer be accepted.

inviter_user_id.description: The User who issued the Invitation.

purpose.description: What accepting the Invitation does. `student_class` creates a student account and Class enrollment, and `teacher_academic_unit` creates a teacher account with an Academic Unit membership and Role. `academic_unit_role` and `institution_role` give an existing User a Role at that scope.

revision.description: The Invitation's revision, which goes up each time it changes. Send it as `expected_revision` to resend, revoke or replace the Invitation.

role_actions.description: The actions the Role allowed when the Invitation was issued, as recorded in the Invitation.

role_id.description: The Role the Invitation grants. Present for every purpose except `student_class`.

start_at.description: When the relationship the Invitation grants starts. When the issuer gave no start, a student Class Invitation starts with its Academic Period and every other Invitation starts when it was issued.

state.description: `pending` until the Invitation is accepted, revoked, expires, or is replaced by a new one (`superseded`).

updated_at.description: When the Invitation last changed.

InvitationBatchErrorCode.description: Why one Invitation batch item failed. New codes may be added later, so show an unknown code as a generic failure.

email.description: The address to invite. Required for the `.create` operations, and not allowed for `resend` and `revoke`.

end_at.description: When the relationship the Invitation grants ends, for the `.create` operations. It must be after the start. Omit it for no end.

expected_revision.description: The Invitation's current `revision`. Required for `resend` and `revoke`, and not allowed otherwise.

invitation_id.description: The Invitation to resend or revoke. Required for `resend` and `revoke`, and not allowed otherwise.

key.description: Your key for this item, unique within the request. Together with the request's Idempotency-Key it lets you retry the item safely.

role_id.description: The Role the Invitation grants. Required for `teacher_academic_unit.create`, `academic_unit_role.create` and `institution_role.create`, and not allowed for other operations.

start_at.description: When the relationship the Invitation grants starts, for the `.create` operations. Omit it for that kind of Invitation's default start.

suggested_display_name.description: The name used to greet the invitee in the Invitation email. Only for `student_class.create` and `teacher_academic_unit.create`.

suggested_first_name.description: A first name to suggest for the new account. Only for `student_class.create` and `teacher_academic_unit.create`.

suggested_last_name.description: A last name to suggest for the new account. Only for `student_class.create` and `teacher_academic_unit.create`.

suggested_locale.description: The language of the Invitation email, as a language tag such as `en`. Only for `student_class.create` and `teacher_academic_unit.create`.

suggested_timezone.description: The time zone the new account gets if the invitee gives none when accepting, such as `Europe/Paris`. Only for `student_class.create` and `teacher_academic_unit.create`.

suggested_username.description: A username to suggest; the invitee chooses their own when accepting. Only for `student_class.create` and `teacher_academic_unit.create`.

error_code.description: Why the item failed. Present only when `status` is `failed`.

index.description: The item's position in the request, starting at 0.

invitation_id.description: The Invitation the item issued, resent or revoked. Omitted when the item failed.

status.description: `succeeded` when the item made its change, `no_op` when its outcome was already recorded, for example by an earlier request with the same keys, and `failed` when it could not be applied.

items.description: The items to process, from 1 to 200.

operation.description: The one Invitation operation applied to every item.

scope_id.description: The Institution, Academic Unit or Class the batch runs in.

scope_type.description: The kind of scope the batch is authorized at: `class` for `student_class.create`, `academic_unit` for `teacher_academic_unit.create` and `academic_unit_role.create`, `institution` for `institution_role.create`, and any of the three for `resend` and `revoke`.

items.description: One outcome for each request item, in request order.

no_op.description: How many items changed nothing because their outcome was already recorded.

InvitationDeliveryResponse.description: The latest email delivery of an Invitation. The recipient address is shown only masked.

accepted_at.description: When the mail server accepted the message. Present only once accepted.

deadline.description: The time after which the delivery is no longer attempted.

masked_recipient.description: The recipient address with most of its local part hidden, such as `s***@example.edu`.

public_failure_code.description: Why the latest attempt failed. Present after a failed attempt, including while the delivery is retried.

state.description: Where the delivery stands: `queued` or `sending` while it is being sent, `accepted` once the mail server took the message, `failed` when it gave up, `suppressed` when the message was deliberately not sent, or `canceled`.

template_key.description: The email template used, such as `access.student_class_invitation`.

updated_at.description: When the delivery last changed.

expected_revision.description: The Invitation's `revision` as you last read it.

InvitationResponse.description: A newly issued Invitation. It never includes the claim or the recipient's mailbox details.

academic_period_id.description: The Academic Period of that Class. Present only for `student_class`.

academic_unit_id.description: The Academic Unit a teacher or Academic Unit Role Invitation applies to. Present only for those purposes.

class_id.description: The Class a student Class Invitation enrolls the student in. Present only for `student_class`.

end_at.description: When the relationship the Invitation grants ends. Omitted when it has no end.

expires_at.description: When the Invitation can no longer be accepted.

purpose.description: What accepting the Invitation does. `student_class` creates a student account and Class enrollment, and `teacher_academic_unit` creates a teacher account with an Academic Unit membership and Role. `academic_unit_role` and `institution_role` give an existing User a Role at that scope.

role_actions.description: The actions the Role allowed when the Invitation was issued, as recorded in the Invitation.

role_id.description: The Role the Invitation grants. Present for every purpose except `student_class`.

start_at.description: When the relationship the Invitation grants starts. When the issuer gave no start, a student Class Invitation starts with its Academic Period and every other Invitation starts when it was issued.

state.description: `pending` until the Invitation is accepted, revoked, expires, or is replaced by a new one (`superseded`).

email.description: The email address of the existing User to invite.

end_at.description: When the Role Binding ends; it must be after the start. Omit it for no end.

expires_in_days.description: How many whole days the Invitation can be accepted for, from 1 to 30. Omit it or send null for 7 days. A value outside the range is refused with invitation.invalid.

role_id.description: The Role the Invitation grants. You must be allowed to delegate it at this scope.

start_at.description: When the Role Binding starts once accepted. Omit it to start when the Invitation is issued.

email.description: The address to send the Invitation to. An account created on acceptance gets this address.

end_at.description: When the enrollment ends; it must be after the start. Omit it for no end.

expires_in_days.description: How many whole days the Invitation can be accepted for, from 1 to 30. Omit it or send null for 7 days. A value outside the range is refused with invitation.invalid.

start_at.description: When the enrollment starts once accepted. Omit it to start with the Class's Academic Period.

suggested_display_name.description: The name used to greet the invitee in the Invitation email.

suggested_first_name.description: A first name to suggest for the new account.

suggested_last_name.description: A last name to suggest for the new account.

suggested_locale.description: The language of the Invitation email, as a language tag such as `en`.

suggested_timezone.description: The time zone the new account gets if the invitee gives none when accepting, such as `Europe/Paris`.

suggested_username.description: A username to suggest. The invitee chooses their own username when accepting.

email.description: The address to send the Invitation to. An account created on acceptance gets this address.

end_at.description: When the membership and Role end; it must be after the start. Omit it for no end.

expires_in_days.description: How many whole days the Invitation can be accepted for, from 1 to 30. Omit it or send null for 7 days. A value outside the range is refused with invitation.invalid.

role_id.description: The Role the teacher gets in the Academic Unit. You must be allowed to delegate it.

start_at.description: When the teacher's membership and Role start once accepted. Omit it to start when the Invitation is issued.

suggested_display_name.description: The name used to greet the invitee in the Invitation email.

suggested_first_name.description: A first name to suggest for the new account.

suggested_last_name.description: A last name to suggest for the new account.

suggested_locale.description: The language of the Invitation email, as a language tag such as `en`.

suggested_timezone.description: The time zone the new account gets if the invitee gives none when accepting, such as `Europe/Paris`.

suggested_username.description: A username to suggest. The invitee chooses their own username when accepting.

JobAttemptListResponse.description: One page of a Job's execution Attempts.

items.description: Attempts on this page, highest attempt number first.

next_cursor.description: Token to pass as `cursor` to read the next page. Treat it as unreadable. Omitted on the last page.

JobAttemptResponse.description: One execution Attempt of a Job.

completed_at.description: Time the Attempt finished. Omitted while it is still running.

heartbeat_at.description: Time the worker last reported that it was still running the Attempt.

lease_expires_at.description: Time the worker's hold on the Job runs out. If the worker hasn't reported again by then, the Attempt is treated as abandoned.

number.description: Position of this Attempt within its Job. The first Attempt is 1 and each new one goes up by one.

public_error_code.description: Public reason the Attempt failed. Internal error detail is never returned. Omitted when there is no failure to report.

status.description: Where the Attempt is in its lifecycle.

JobAttemptStatus.description: State of one execution Attempt. `lease_expired` means the worker stopped reporting before it finished. `incompatible` means the worker that picked up the Job could not run it and handed it back to the queue.

JobErrorCode.description: Public reason a Job or Job Attempt failed. It never carries internal error detail. The server only uses the values listed here, but later releases may add more. Clients choose their own labels and should show an unknown value in a generic way.

items.description: Jobs on this page, in the requested order.

next_cursor.description: Token to pass as `cursor` to read the next page. Treat it as unreadable. Omitted on the last page.

total.description: Number of Jobs, across all pages, that match the filters and that the caller may see. Present only on the first page. Counting stops at 10,000, and then `total_is_lower_bound` is true.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when `total` reached the 10,000 limit and there may be more Jobs. Present whenever `total` is.

JobProgressResponse.description: Approximate progress a running Job reports for its current stage.

current.description: Number of work units finished in the current stage.

stage.description: Name of the stage the Job is in.

total.description: Number of work units the current stage expects to process.

JobResponse.description: State of a background Job whose type the public API exposes. Private payloads, worker details and internal errors are never included.

attempt_count.description: Number of execution Attempts made so far.

available_at.description: Earliest time a worker may pick up the Job while it is queued.

completed_at.description: Time the Job finished, whether it succeeded, failed or was canceled. Omitted while it has not finished.

created_at.description: Time when the Job was created.

created_by_display_name.description: Display name of the User who started the Job, or their username when they have none. Omitted with created_by_user_id, and while that User is archived.

created_by_user_id.description: User whose request started the Job. Omitted for recurring and system work, and after that User is deleted.

maximum_attempts.description: Most execution Attempts this Job's retry policy allows.

progress.description: Latest progress the Job reported. Omitted when it has reported none.

public_error_code.description: Public reason for the Job's most recent failure. Worker and infrastructure errors are never returned. Omitted when no failure is recorded.

revision.description: Version number of the Job's state. It goes up with every change, so a client can tell a newer state from an older one.

started_at.description: Time the current or most recent Attempt started. Omitted until the first Attempt starts.

status.description: Where the Job is in its lifecycle. `cancel_requested` means cancellation was asked for but the running work has not stopped yet.

subject.description: What the Job is about, for the Job types that say: an Examination Export build names the title of the Exam revision its Sitting runs. Omitted for every other type.

type.description: What kind of work the Job does.

updated_at.description: Time of the most recent change to the Job.

JobStage.description: Name of a stage a Job works through. The server only uses the values listed here, but later releases may add more. Clients choose their own labels and should show an unknown value in a generic way.

JobStatus.description: State of a background Job: waiting to run (`queued`), running, asked to stop (`cancel_requested`), or finished as `succeeded`, `failed` or `canceled`.

JobType.description: Type of a background Job. The server only uses the values listed here, but later releases may add more. Clients choose their own labels and should show an unknown value in a generic way.

client_type.description: The kind of client the new Session is for. It decides whether credentials come back as cookies (web, desktop) or in the body (cli).

device_id.description: An identifier the client chooses for its device and keeps the same across sign-ins, up to 128 bytes. It is shown in Session management.

device_name.description: A readable device name shown in Session management, up to 128 characters.

login_id.description: The username or email address of the local account. Case and surrounding spaces are ignored.

mfa_code.description: A current six-digit authenticator code, or one unused recovery code. Required when the account has two-step verification turned on.

password.description: The account's local password. Treat it as a secret and keep it out of traces and logs.

recovery_codes.description: The recovery codes for the new setup, each usable once in place of an authenticator code. Proctor never shows these codes again.

code.description: A current six-digit authenticator code, or one unused recovery code where the operation accepts it. Hyphens and spaces in a recovery code are ignored.

MFAKeyStateResponse.description: The MFA key IDs, the required primary key and how many live secrets each key encrypts.

active.description: The keys that encrypt at least one live authenticator secret, sorted by key ID.

active_rekey_job_id.description: The ID of the MFA rekey Job that is queued or running. Left out when there is none.

primary_key_id.description: The ID of the key this node uses to encrypt new authenticator secrets.

required_primary_key_id.description: The primary key the last rekey made required. Every node must encrypt new secrets with it. Left out before the first rekey.

recovery_codes.description: The new recovery codes, each usable once in place of an authenticator code. Earlier codes no longer work. Proctor never shows these codes again.

MFARekeyProgress.description: Rough progress while live authenticator secrets are re-encrypted.

current.description: How many secrets the Job has checked so far.

stage.description: The step the Job is on. resealing means it is re-encrypting secrets.

total.description: How many secrets the Job expects to check in total.

MFARekeyProof.description: The final counts of live secrets that show whether the retiring key can be removed.

non_primary_references.description: How many live authenticator secrets still use any key other than the primary key after the Job finished.

retirement_safe.description: True only when the final counts prove that the retiring key can be removed.

retiring_references.description: How many live authenticator secrets still use the retiring key.

MFARekeyRequest.description: Which key a new MFA key rotation Job retires.

retiring_key_id.description: The ID of the configured MFA key to retire. It must not be the primary key.

MFARekeyResponse.description: The Job and keys of an accepted MFA key rotation.

created_at.description: When the rekey Job was created.

job_id.description: The ID of the rekey Job. Use it to follow progress.

primary_key_id.description: The ID of the key that secrets are re-encrypted with.

retiring_key_id.description: The ID of the key being retired.

MFARekeyStatusResponse.description: The rekey Job's status, its progress and, once it succeeds, the key retirement proof.

attempt_count.description: How many times the Job has started running.

completed_at.description: When the Job finished. Left out while it is still queued or running.

job_id.description: The ID of the rekey Job.

maximum_attempts.description: How many times the Job may run before it gives up.

primary_key_id.description: The ID of the key that secrets are re-encrypted with.

processed.description: How many secrets the Job has checked so far.

progress.description: The progress the Job last saved. Left out until the Job has saved progress.

proof.description: The key retirement proof. Present only after the Job succeeds.

public_error_code.description: A code saying why the Job's last run failed, such as mfa.rekey.incomplete. Left out when there is no failure to report.

resealed.description: How many of the checked secrets the Job re-encrypted. A secret that changed while the Job was working is counted as checked but not re-encrypted.

retiring_key_id.description: The ID of the key being retired.

updated_at.description: When the Job last changed.

MFASecretKeyUsage.description: How many live authenticator secrets one MFA key encrypts.

configured.description: Whether this server node has the key in its MFA key configuration.

credentials.description: How many live authenticator secrets this key encrypts.

key_id.description: The key's ID, 128 bits written as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. It is not secret.

expires_at.description: When this pending setup expires. Activate it before then.

provisioning_uri.description: An otpauth URI with the same secret, usually shown as a QR code for the authenticator app to scan.

secret.description: The authenticator secret in base32, for typing into an authenticator app by hand. Treat it as a secret.

authentication_method.description: How this Session was signed in.

authentication_provider_id.description: The ID of the provider an external Session signed in through. Left out for a password Session.

authentication_strength.description: multi_factor when this Session has passed two-step verification, otherwise single_factor.

can_raise_strength.description: Whether this single-factor Session can be upgraded using the User's active Proctor factor. It is false when the service is disabled or MFA recovery is required.

enabled.description: Whether two-step verification is on for the User.

enabled_at.description: When two-step verification was turned on. Present only while enabled.

method.description: The second factor in use. Present while two-step verification is on or a setup is pending. More methods may be added later.

mfa_enrollment_required.description: Whether the Access Policy limits this Web Session until its User sets up or completes two-step verification. While it is true, the Session can only set up two-step verification, answer the two-step verification challenge, reauthenticate, read the security status and sign out.

mfa_recovery_required.description: Whether this Session is limited, after an administrator reset two-step verification, to reauthenticating and setting up a new authenticator app.

password_changed_at.description: When the User's current password was set or last changed. Left out for an account without a password.

pending.description: Whether an authenticator app setup has been started but not yet activated.

pending_expires_at.description: When the pending setup expires. Present only while pending is true.

recent_authentication_minutes.description: The length of the recent sign-in window, in whole minutes rounded down. It comes from the `Authentication.RecentAuthenticationTTL` setting.

recently_authenticated.description: Whether this Session signed in or reauthenticated within the recent sign-in window, so actions that need a recent sign-in are allowed.

recently_authenticated_until.description: When this Session's recent sign-in window ends. Present only while `recently_authenticated` is true.

recovery_codes_generated_at.description: When the current recovery codes were issued. Left out when there are none.

recovery_codes_remaining.description: How many of the current recovery codes are still unused. 0 when two-step verification is off.

recovery_codes_total.description: How many recovery codes the User was given in the current set, used ones included. It stays correct even if the configured count changes later. 0 when two-step verification is off.

service_enabled.description: Whether this server currently offers authenticator app setup and two-step verification.

items.description: Deliveries on this page, in the requested order.

next_cursor.description: Token to pass as `cursor` to read the next page. Treat it as unreadable. Omitted on the last page.

total.description: Number of deliveries, across all pages, that match the filters and that the caller may see. Present only on the first page. Counting stops at 10,000, and then `total_is_lower_bound` is true.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when `total` reached the 10,000 limit and there may be more deliveries. Present whenever `total` is.

MailDeliveryMetricResponse.description: Totals for one template, state and outcome, counted since this server process started.

attempt_count.description: Number of send attempts started. Only the `mail.attempt_started` group counts attempts, and its `count` is 0. Every other group reports 0.

count.description: Number of times a delivery of this template reached this state with this outcome.

maximum_processing_latency_millis.description: Longest time, in milliseconds, any one delivery in the group took from creation to reaching its state.

outcome_code.description: Outcome this group counts: `mail.accepted` for messages the SMTP server accepted, a mail failure code for deliveries that failed, were suppressed, expired or will be retried, or `mail.attempt_started` for the group that counts send attempts.

processing_latency_millis.description: Sum, in milliseconds, of the time each delivery in the group took from creation to reaching its state. Divide by `count` for the average.

state.description: State the deliveries in this group reached.

template_key.description: Template of the deliveries in this group.

MailDeliveryResponse.description: Status and routing details of one mail delivery. The recipient address is masked and the message content is never included.

accepted_at.description: Time the SMTP server accepted the message. Omitted until then.

attempt_count.description: Number of send attempts made so far.

created_at.description: Time when the delivery was created.

deadline.description: Time after which the message is no longer worth sending. A delivery still unsent by then expires.

failed_at.description: Time the delivery failed for good. Omitted unless it failed.

masked_recipient.description: Recipient address with the local part hidden, such as `a***@example.edu`. Safe to show to administrators.

message_date.description: Time written in the message's `Date` header.

message_id.description: The message's `Message-ID` header, for matching the delivery with mail server logs. It isn't a secret.

occurrence_id.description: ID of the notification this delivery belongs to. When one notification goes to several recipients, each of their deliveries carries the same value.

public_failure_code.description: Public reason the delivery failed, was suppressed or canceled, or was retried by an operator. Raw SMTP and infrastructure errors are never returned. Omitted when there is no such reason.

recipient_display_name.description: Current display name of the User in `target_user_id`. Present only when the delivery is listed or fetched by ID, and only while the caller can see that User in the User directory (`user.view` or `class.members.view`). `mail.view` alone doesn't reveal it. Omitted for Invitation mail, for a User the caller can't see, and in the responses to sending a test, canceling or retrying. It is the account's name, not the address the mail went to, which stays masked.

state.description: Where the delivery is in its lifecycle.

target_invitation_id.description: Invitation the mail is addressed to. Present instead of `target_user_id` for Invitation mail.

target_user_id.description: User the mail is addressed to. Each delivery has exactly one of `target_user_id` and `target_invitation_id`. Invitation mail uses the second, because the invitee has no account yet.

template_digest.description: SHA-256 hash, in lowercase hexadecimal, of the exact template version used to write the message.

template_key.description: Template the message was written from.

updated_at.description: Time of the delivery's most recent change.

MailDeliveryState.description: Where one mail delivery is in its lifecycle. `accepted` means the SMTP server took the message. It doesn't prove the message reached the inbox.

MailFailureCode.description: Public reason a mail delivery failed, was suppressed or canceled, or was retried by an operator. The server only uses the values listed here, but later releases may add more. Clients choose their own labels and should show an unknown value in a generic way.

MailKeyStateResponse.description: Which keys encrypt mail payloads, and how many payloads each key still covers.

active.description: Keys that still encrypt at least one stored payload, at most nine.

primary_key_id.description: ID of the key this server uses to encrypt new payloads.

required_primary_key_id.description: ID of the primary key that the most recent key rotation recorded. New payloads must be encrypted with it, so a configured primary key that differs has to be resolved. Omitted before the first rotation.

MailMetricsResponse.description: Mail delivery totals and queue health for the server that answered the request.

deliveries.description: Delivery totals since this server process started, one entry per template, state and outcome.

health_code.description: Overall mail health on this server. `mail.disabled` means mail is turned off in configuration. Empty when the monitor hasn't reported yet.

queues.description: Queue figures from the monitor's most recent check, one entry per template, state and outcome.

MailPayloadKeyUsage.description: How many stored encrypted mail payloads use one configured key.

active_references.description: Number of stored encrypted mail payloads that are still encrypted with this key.

key_id.description: ID of the key, a 128-bit value in lowercase hexadecimal. It isn't secret.

MailQueueMetricResponse.description: Size and age of the stored deliveries of one template, state and outcome, as the mail maintenance monitor last saw them.

count.description: Number of deliveries in the group when the monitor last checked.

health_code.description: Overall mail health the monitor decided during the same check. `mail.queue_delayed` means queued mail has waited too long. `mail.smtp_outage` means the SMTP server can't be reached.

oldest_age_millis.description: Age, in milliseconds, of the oldest delivery in the group when the monitor last checked.

outcome_code.description: Public failure code the deliveries in this group carry. Empty when they carry none.

state.description: State of the deliveries in this group.

template_key.description: Template of the deliveries in this group.

truncated.description: True when the monitor's check stopped at its size limit, so these figures may not cover every delivery.

MailRekeyProgress.description: Approximate progress while stored payloads are re-encrypted. Omitted until the Job has saved its first progress.

current.description: Number of payloads checked so far.

stage.description: Name of the stage the rotation is in.

total.description: Number of payloads the rotation expects to check.

MailRekeyProof.description: Final counts that show whether the retiring key can be removed. Present only after the rotation succeeds.

non_primary_references.description: Number of stored payloads still encrypted with any key other than the primary, after the rotation.

retirement_safe.description: True only when the final counts show that no payload uses the retiring key, so it can be removed.

retiring_references.description: Number of stored payloads still encrypted with the retiring key.

retiring_key_id.description: ID of the configured key to retire, in lowercase hexadecimal. It must not be the primary key.

job_id.description: ID of the rotation Job. Use it to check progress.

primary_key_id.description: ID of the primary key that payloads are re-encrypted with.

retiring_key_id.description: ID of the key being retired.

MailRekeyStatusResponse.description: Status and progress of a mail key rotation Job, with its final counts once it succeeds.

attempt_count.description: Number of execution Attempts made so far.

completed_at.description: Time the rotation Job finished. Omitted while it has not finished.

created_at.description: Time when the rotation Job was created.

maximum_attempts.description: Most execution Attempts the Job's retry policy allows.

primary_key_id.description: ID of the primary key that payloads are re-encrypted with.

processed.description: Number of stored payloads the rotation has checked so far.

progress.description: Progress of the re-encryption. Omitted until the Job has saved its first progress.

proof.description: Final counts that show whether the retiring key can be removed. Present only after the Job succeeds.

public_error_code.description: Public reason for the Job's most recent failure, from the Job error codes. Omitted when there is none.

reencrypted.description: Number of checked payloads that the rotation re-encrypted. It is never more than `processed`.

retiring_key_id.description: ID of the key being retired.

status.description: Where the rotation Job is in its lifecycle.

updated_at.description: Time of the rotation Job's most recent change.

MailTemplateKey.description: Key of one of the server's built-in transactional mail templates. The server only uses the values listed here, but later releases may add more. Clients choose their own labels and should show an unknown value in a generic way.

expected_revision.description: The Draft revision you last saw. If the Draft has changed since, the request fails with a conflict.

path.description: The entry's new path. Its parent directory must already exist.

categories.description: The sub-categories the capability runs; empty means every registered one.

NativeCapabilityFact.description: One activated capability's full minimized state as Desktop observed it, with its envelope. Desktop sends a fact whenever the state or the envelope changes; the server checks it against the capability's published schemas and evaluates the policy's rules on it again. A fact no newer than the latest of its source instance changes nothing.

observed_at.description: The device time of the observation, in whole milliseconds.

state.description: The full state, valid against its published state schema. State and summary are at most 16 KiB together.

summary.description: The counts derived from the state, valid against its published summary schema.

sequence.description: The sequence the capability's event stream continues from.

state.description: The capability's minimized full state, valid against its published state schema, at most 16 KiB. It never holds what must not leave the device. A field named "<capability>.<name>" is read from state.<name>.

summary.description: The counts Desktop derives from the state, valid against its published summary schema, at most 16 KiB. A field named "<capability>.summary.<name>" is read from summary.<name>.

catalog_app_ids.description: Catalog application IDs in ASCII order.

NativeCondition.description: Exactly one of a comparison of a registered field with a typed value, a combination of conditions, or an application condition matched on the device. Nesting is at most three deep.

value.description: A whole number, one of an enumerated field's values, a boolean, or a list of them for in and not_in.

NativeConditionInventory.description: A running count and digest of the native condition records kept for the Attempt.

digest.description: A digest that changes with every record added, as `sha256:` followed by lowercase hex. Compare it to detect any change in the records.

records.description: The number of native condition records kept.

NativeParticipationConfirmed.description: Where the exam begins on the stream: Desktop sends it once, when the candidate window mounts after admission. Before it the server applies the policy's readiness rules; from it, the participation rules, on the latest facts. Send the mounted candidate window's fact before it, in the same or an earlier batch; otherwise the window rule is evaluated on the window Desktop reported at Start and fails.

NativeRule.description: One requirement, in the rule grammar Desktop publishes.

reason.description: A reason registered for the capability; Desktop owns its localized text.

unknown_cause.description: Why the rule is unknown; present only when status is unknown.

NativeRuleStatusReport.description: Desktop's own status for one participation rule and whether it is containing the candidate window because of it. The server's status is authoritative; a disagreement is counted, never applied.

unknown_cause.description: Why the rule is unknown; present only when status is unknown.

at.description: The device time of the change; it never moves backwards within a Participation.

occurrence.description: The rule's occurrence this change opened or closed, counted from 1 per Participation.

reason.description: The reason ID Desktop's registry publishes for the rule; Desktop owns its wording.

NativeScreenRecordingPolicy.description: Whether Desktop records the candidate's screen on the device for the whole session, uploading only the ranges the server requests. Off by default; the candidate is told before the Attempt starts. When on, the policy activates the screen_recording capability with the readiness rule screen_recording.free_space: Start is refused unless the recorder is permitted and the device has at least 3072 MiB free.

NativeSecurityPolicy.description: Complete native selection with an invariant baseline and exactly ten families in the documented order. Complete canonical ExamPolicySet bytes are limited to 64 KiB.

families.description: Exactly one family in this order: process_application, interactive_session, clipboard, printing, removable_storage, virtualization, network_configuration, camera, microphone, external_capture.

allowed_application_ids.description: The only catalog applications the candidate may run, sorted and unique: IDs from the Desktop release's application catalog, each one it marks allowable. Empty adds no allowlist. When the family is on, the catalog's never-allowable applications are always blocked.

outcome.description: What an enforce occurrence of this family leads to; flag unless mode is enforce.
What an enforce occurrence of this family leads to; flag unless mode is enforce.

What an enforce occurrence of this family leads to; flag unless mode is enforce.

NativeSecuritySummary.description: The candidate's live native standing: how many rule status changes are kept, whether the live Participation's native delivery is open, each enforce rule's status as the server evaluates it, whether Desktop is containing the candidate window, and the Attempt's screen clips by state. It contains no facts, source-instance or application identities, and an application outside the catalog is never named. A rule that is not met is not a misconduct finding; its Flag is reviewed like any other.

contained.description: Whether Desktop reports it is containing the candidate window right now.

live_coverage_available.description: Whether the live Participation's native delivery is open, so rule statuses are current.

retained_condition_records.description: Number of native condition records kept for the Attempt. Zero once its integrity data has been retired.

rules.description: The live Participation's enforce rules, by rule ID; empty when nothing is live.

open_occurrence.description: The occurrence open now, counted from 1 in this Participation; absent when none is open.

reason.description: The registry's reason ID for the rule, such as display.single_display_required.

capability.description: The activated capability whose source this names.
The activated capability whose source this names.

NextCursor.description: Token for the next page. Send it back unchanged as `cursor`, and do not parse it. Omitted on the last page.

OnboardingImportCommitRequest.description: The revision and SHA-256 digest of the preview you reviewed, and how to treat invalid rows.

expected_revision.description: The import's `revision` when you reviewed it.

policy.description: `require_all_valid` refuses the commit if any row is invalid. `valid_rows_only` commits the valid rows and skips the invalid ones.

preview_digest.description: The import's `preview_digest`, a SHA-256 digest in lowercase hexadecimal.

OnboardingImportFailureCode.description: Why an onboarding import, student progression or academic administration preview failed as a whole. Examples are lost credentials or permissions, an unreadable file, a target that is no longer valid, or a preview filter that matched too many Users. Later versions may add values. Show your own label for each value, and a general message for one you don't recognize.

OnboardingImportListResponse.description: One page of onboarding import summaries, without rows.

items.description: The imports on this page.

OnboardingImportPreviewCode.description: Why a preview row is invalid, a duplicate, or carries a note. Examples are a malformed or repeated CSV row, a target that can't be found, a student who can't progress or is already enrolled in the destination, or an academic administration row that will be skipped or changes nothing. Later versions may add values. Show your own label for each value, and a general message for one you don't recognize.

OnboardingImportResponse.description: A CSV onboarding import, a student progression or an academic administration preview. The server parses it into rows you can review, then runs the rows when you commit it.

commit_policy.description: How the import was committed: `require_all_valid` runs only if every row is valid, and `valid_rows_only` runs the valid rows and skips the rest. Present after commit.

destination_class_id.description: Class students progress into. Student progressions only.

destination_class_name.description: Display name of the destination Class, present only on student progression reads and listings.

destination_period_id.description: Academic Period students progress into. Student progressions only.

effective_at.description: Time the student progression takes effect. Omitted for other modes.

execution_job_id.description: The background Job that runs the rows. Present after commit.

expires_at.description: Time after which the import can no longer be read, seven days after it was created.

failure_code.description: Why the import failed. Present only when `state` is `failed`.

file_name.description: Base name of the uploaded file as the uploader gave it, omitted when none was given and for student progressions.

ignored_headers.description: CSV column names the import did not recognize and ignored, in lowercase and sorted.

mode.description: What kind of import this is, which decides the CSV columns and the operations its rows run.

parse_job_id.description: The background Job that parses the file.

preview_digest.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the parsed preview, as 64 hexadecimal characters. Send it back when you commit, to confirm you reviewed this exact preview. Present once parsing has finished.

revision.description: Version number that goes up with each change. Send it as `expected_revision` when you commit.

role_id.description: The Role the import grants, for modes that grant one.

rows.description: Every row of the import. Present only when you read one import, not in listings.

scope_id.description: The Class, Academic Unit or Institution the import works in.

scope_type.description: Kind of scope the import works in.

skipped_rows.description: Rows that did not run, because they were left out at commit or the import was canceled.

source_class_id.description: Class students progress from. Student progressions only.

source_class_name.description: Display name of the source Class, present only on student progression reads and listings.

source_period_id.description: Academic Period students progress from. Student progressions only.

state.description: Progress of the import. It goes from `uploading` and `parsing` to `preview_ready`, then `executing` after commit, and ends as `completed`, `completed_with_errors`, `canceled` or `failed`.

succeeded_rows.description: Rows that ran and made their change.

total_rows.description: Number of data rows in the import.

updated_at.description: Time of the latest change to the import.

OnboardingImportRowCode.description: Why a row failed when an onboarding import, student progression or academic administration preview ran. It is the code the Invitation or academic administration operation for that row returned, or `academic_administration_preview.system_administrator` when the row's User became a System Administrator after the preview was taken. Later versions may add values. Show your own label for each value, and a general message for one you don't recognize.

OnboardingImportRowResponse.description: One row of an import: where it sits, what it does and how it ended. It never repeats the email address or names the row holds.

invitation_id.description: The Invitation the row created, for rows that invite someone.

operation.description: The change the row makes when the import runs.

preview_code.description: Why the preview marked the row invalid or duplicate, or a note about it. Omitted when there is none.

public_code.description: Why the row failed when the import ran. Present only on a `failed` row.

reference.description: Your label for the row: the value of the CSV `reference` column, or the row number when that column is empty or longer than 128 characters. For a student progression or an academic administration preview, it is the ID of the Class membership or User the row is about.

resource_id.description: The ID of the record the row created or changed, when the operation reports one.

row.description: Row number, starting at 1 for the first data row after the header.

status.description: Where the row stands. Before commit it is `valid`, `invalid` or `duplicate`. On commit, valid rows become `pending`, rows that would change nothing become `no_op`, and the rest are `skipped`. A pending row ends as `succeeded` or `failed`, or `canceled` if the import is canceled first.

password.description: The current User's password. Never log or store it.

The new local password. It must meet the password rules and must not contain the username, the part of the email address before the @, or the person's name. When the server keeps a password history, it must not match a recent password.

token.description: The reset token from the link in the password-reset email, as 43 URL-safe base64 characters.

email.description: The email address of the account whose password should be reset.

PermissionArea.description: A group of permissions. The server owns the grouping.

title.description: The area's title in the request's language.

PermissionCatalogueResponse.description: Every permission a custom Role can hold, and the areas that group them.

areas.description: Every area, in the order a role editor shows them.

PermissionResponse.description: One permission a custom Role can hold.

description.description: One sentence on what the permission allows, in the request's language.

name.description: The permission's name, as a Role's `permissions` lists it.

override_of.description: For an override permission, the permission it widens through the audited administrator path. Omitted otherwise.

scope_types.description: The scopes a Role Binding can grant this permission at. A Binding at an Academic Unit also covers the Exams, Sittings, Programmes and Classes under it.

title.description: A short title in the request's language.

PersonRef.description: A person a record refers to, such as who granted a Role or who paused a Sitting. Anyone who can read the record gets the person's presented name: their display name, or their username when it is empty. The username and profile picture are included only when the reader can see that User in the directory.

display_name.description: The person's presented name. Omitted when the account has been removed.

id.description: The User's ID. It is kept after the account is removed.

profile_picture_url.description: Same-origin path of the User's profile picture. Omitted unless the reader can see this User.

username.description: The username. Omitted unless the reader can see this User in the directory.

credential.description: The secret token value to send as a Bearer token. Store it safely now, because Proctor never shows it again.

display_name.description: The Academic Unit's display name.

academic_unit_ids.description: The listed `academic_units` where the scope can be granted. It can also be granted at any unit below them.

description.description: One sentence, in the request's language, explaining what the scope allows.

institution_wide.description: True when the scope can be granted without an Academic Unit limit, or limited to any Academic Unit.

name.description: The scope name to send in scopes when creating a token. A newer server may send a name this contract does not list yet.

resource_types.description: The resource types the action applies to.

title.description: A short title in the request's language.

academic_units.description: Up to 50 top Academic Units where at least one scope can be granted, sorted by display name.

academic_units_has_more.description: True when there are more such Academic Units than are listed.

scopes.description: The scopes the current User may grant somewhere. Scopes they can't grant anywhere are left out.

PersonalAccessTokenListResponse.description: One page of the collection in its stable order.

items.description: The tokens on this page, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass this back as cursor to get the next page. Left out on the last page.

academic_unit_id.description: The Academic Unit the token is limited to, including the units below it. Left out for a token that works across the Institution.

archived_at.description: When the token record was archived. Left out when it has not been archived.

description.description: What the token is for, as its owner described it.

disabled_at.description: When the token was disabled. Left out while it is enabled.

expires_at.description: When the token stops working.

id.description: The Personal Access Token ID. It is not the secret token value.

last_used_at.description: When a request last used the token. Use is recorded at most once per update interval, five minutes by default, so it can trail the latest request. Left out when the token has never been used.

revoked_at.description: When the token was revoked. Left out unless it has been revoked.

scopes.description: The actions the token may perform.

updated_at.description: When the token record last changed.

user_id.description: The ID of the User who owns the token.

PersonalAccessTokenScope.description: An action a Personal Access Token may carry. The grantable-scopes operation reports which of them the current User may grant.

PluginListResponse.description: One page of the collection in its stable order.

PluginResponse.description: One compiled-in plugin as an administrator sees it.

enabled.description: Whether the plugin should run, from its saved settings or its default.

enabled_by_default.description: Whether the plugin runs when nobody has configured it.

revision.description: The saved settings revision, 0 when nothing is saved.

settings.description: The saved settings document as JSON text, or "{}" when nothing is saved.

settings_schema.description: The JSON Schema of the plugin's settings as JSON text, absent when the plugin has none.

state.description: The plugin's state on the serving node.

enabled.description: Whether the plugin should run. A required plugin cannot be turned off.

expected_revision.description: The settings revision the editor read, 0 when nothing is saved. A stale revision cannot overwrite newer settings.

settings.description: The plugin's settings document as JSON text, a JSON object of at most 64 KiB, as its settings_schema describes.

ProblemDetails.description: The RFC 9457 error body returned by every failed request. Use `code` to decide what to do. `title` and `detail` are text for people, in the request's language.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, such as `request.invalid`. Base your error handling on this.

control_metadata_bytes.description: Bytes of delivery control data already stored. Present only with `exam.delivery.metadata_capacity`.

control_metadata_limit_bytes.description: Most bytes of delivery control data that can be stored. Present only with `exam.delivery.metadata_capacity`.

delivery.description: Current delivery progress and budget, sent with some Exam delivery errors.

detail.description: Longer explanation of this occurrence for people. Omitted when there is nothing to add.

fields.description: For validation errors, the request fields that were wrong, each mapped to a short reason.

instance.description: The request path that failed, when the server includes it.

remaining_reservable_bytes.description: Bytes that can still be reserved. Present only with `exam.delivery.metadata_capacity`.

request_id.description: The server's ID for the request. Quote it when you report a problem.

required_reservation_bytes.description: Bytes the refused request needed to reserve. Present only with `exam.delivery.metadata_capacity`.

status.description: The HTTP status code of the response.

title.description: Short summary of the error for people.

type.description: Link to this error's page on the installation's documentation site, such as `https://docs.example.edu/problems/request.invalid`, or `about:blank` when the installation has not configured one. Use `code`, not `type`, to decide what to do.

ProfilePictureKind.description: Which picture the profile picture route serves: the User's own upload (custom), which can be removed, or the picture generated for every User (default).

ProgrammeLevelListResponse.description: One page of Programme Levels, ordered by name and then by identifier. Only the first page carries the total.

items.description: The Programme Levels on this page.

total.description: How many Programme Levels match the filters across every page. Present only on the first page. Counting stops at 10,000, and then `total_is_lower_bound` is true.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when `total` reached 10,000 and there may be more. Present with `total`.

archived_at.description: When the Programme Level was archived. Omitted while it is active.

created_at.description: When the Programme Level was created.

description.description: Longer text shown to people, up to 1,024 characters. Empty when none was given.

display_name.description: Name shown to people, up to 128 characters.

name.description: Machine name: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, at most 64 characters. Unique among the Programme's active Programme Levels.

programme_id.description: The Programme that owns the Programme Level. It can't change.

revision.description: Starts at 1 and goes up with every change. Send it as `expected_revision` on an update or archive so the change fails if someone else changed the Programme Level first.

updated_at.description: When the Programme Level last changed.

ProgrammeListResponse.description: One page of Programmes, ordered by name and then by identifier. Only the first page carries the total.

items.description: The Programmes on this page.

total.description: How many Programmes match the filters across every page. Present only on the first page. Counting stops at 10,000, and then `total_is_lower_bound` is true.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when `total` reached 10,000 and there may be more. Present with `total`.

academic_unit_id.description: The Academic Unit that owns the Programme. It can't change.

archived_at.description: When the Programme was archived. Omitted while it is active.

description.description: Longer text shown to people, up to 1,024 characters. Empty when none was given.

display_name.description: Name shown to people, up to 128 characters.

name.description: Machine name: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, at most 64 characters. Unique among the Academic Unit's active Programmes.

revision.description: Starts at 1 and goes up with every change. Send it as `expected_revision` on an update or archive so the change fails if someone else changed the Programme first.

updated_at.description: When the Programme last changed.

ProviderAdmissionMode.description: How a configured external sign-in provider lets people in once it has proved who they are. `linked_only` signs in only identities already linked to a User. `invitation_required` also lets a new identity in by accepting an Invitation. `auto_provision` also creates a User for a new identity, when the provider supports it. A provider with no entry can't be used to sign in.

expires_at.description: When this connection attempt expires. Finish the provider sign-in before then.

redirect_url.description: The provider's sign-in address. Send the browser there to connect the identity.

PublicAccessCapabilitiesResponse.description: Which ways in the Access Policy currently allows, so a client can offer the right sign-in or registration flow. All are false until the installation is set up.

desktop_authorization.description: Whether Proctor Desktop may sign in through the browser authorization flow.

invitation_admission.description: Whether pending Invitations can be accepted.

local_login.description: Whether people may sign in with a local password.

public_registration.description: Whether anyone may create their own local account.

PublicAccessDiscoveryResponse.description: What a client needs before sign-in to choose how to register or sign in.

canonical_origin.description: The installation's public origin. Clients must use exactly this origin when they check browser requests and redirects.

discovery_version.description: The format version of this document. Always 1 in this API version.

initialized.description: True once the installation has been set up. Setup happens once.

installation_id.description: The installation identifier, the same as the Institution's. Omitted until the installation is set up.

institution.description: The Institution to show on sign-in pages. Omitted until the installation is set up.

password_minimum_length.description: The fewest characters a new local password may have, set by `Authentication.Password.MinimumLength`. Other password rules still apply and are reported when a password is rejected.

policy_revision.description: The current Access Policy revision. Omitted until the installation is set up.

providers.description: The external sign-in providers to offer: those configured on this deployment that the Access Policy turns on, sorted by ID. Empty until the installation is set up.

support_address.description: The help mailbox, set by the operator in `Mail.SupportAddress`, that hosted pages offer as a contact. Omitted when none is set.

PublicInstitutionPresentationResponse.description: The Institution's identity, safe to show on sign-in pages before anyone signs in.

display_name.description: The Institution's name as shown to people.

name.description: The Institution's machine name.

email.description: The account email address. It is stored in lower case, and the verification link is sent to it.

first_name.description: The person's first name, shown on the profile. Surrounding spaces are removed, and it can't be blank.

last_name.description: The person's last name, shown on the profile. Surrounding spaces are removed, and it can't be blank.

password.description: The new local password. It must meet the password rules and must not contain the username, the part of the email address before the @, or the person's name.

username.description: The sign-in name for the new account. No other account may already use it.

expected_revision.description: The Draft revision you expect to publish. If the Draft has changed since, the request fails with a conflict.

ReadinessDigest.description: Identifies what the readiness overview shows and Desktop enforces: the activations and rules, family selections, recorder switch, and the registry, matrix and catalogs they rest on. Unlike the policy content digest it leaves out the policy's own identity, so the overview and the preflight prepared at Start carry the same value exactly when nothing that matters changed. It is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON object {activations, rules, capabilities, screen_recording, focus_loss_mode, connection_loss_mode, registry_digest, capability_matrix_digest, catalog_bindings}, taken from the policy and its resolution.

suspension_id.description: ID of the active Suspension to close.

submission_id.description: Submission the hold was created on, if any.

device_name.description: The new name. Surrounding whitespace is removed before the length is checked.
