end_at.description: When that relationship ends; it must be after the start. Omit it for no end.

expected_revision.description: The pending Invitation's current `revision`.

expires_in_days.description: How many whole days the new Invitation can be accepted for, from 1 to 30. Omit it or send null to keep the replaced Invitation's own lifetime, rounded to whole days. A value outside the range is refused with invitation.invalid.

purpose.description: The purpose of the new Invitation.

role_id.description: The Role the new Invitation grants, for every purpose except `student_class`.

start_at.description: When the relationship the new Invitation grants starts. Omit it for the default: the Academic Period's start for a student Class Invitation, otherwise the time of issue.

suggested_display_name.description: The name used to greet the invitee in the Invitation email.

suggested_first_name.description: A first name to suggest for the new account.

suggested_last_name.description: A last name to suggest for the new account.

suggested_locale.description: The language of the Invitation email, as a language tag such as `en`.

suggested_timezone.description: The time zone the new account gets if the invitee gives none when accepting, such as `Europe/Paris`.

suggested_username.description: A username to suggest. The invitee chooses their own username when accepting.

end.description: The range's end, at most ten minutes after the request.

from_session_start.description: True for a range from the moment the candidate window opened; start is then omitted.

reason.description: The manager's private reason. It is stored with the request and never returned.

start.description: The range's start, required unless from_session_start is true, and omitted then.

identity_verified.description: Confirms that the Institution has finished checking the User's identity. Must be true.

reason.description: Why the reset is needed, in up to 512 characters. Don't include passwords, secrets, recovery codes or identity documents.

verification_reference.description: A reference to the Institution's record of the identity check, such as a case number. Don't include the evidence itself.

ResourceType.description: Type of a resource in permission checks and audit records. Later versions may add values. Show your own label for each value, and a general message for one you don't recognize.

RetentionControlRequest.description: A change to the cleanup control.

expected_policy_revision.description: The policy revision you reviewed. The request fails if the policy changed since.

expected_revision.description: The control revision you read. The request fails if the control changed since.

preview_id.description: Retention Preview to approve cleanup with. Required to enable, omitted when pausing.

state.description: `enabled` turns recurring cleanup on. `paused` stops new scheduling.

RetentionControlResponse.description: Whether recurring cleanup is approved, and for which policy revision.

approved_policy_revision.description: Policy revision the approval applies to. Omitted while `disabled`.

approved_preview_id.description: Retention Preview the approval was based on. Omitted while `disabled`.

revision.description: Current control revision. Send it as `expected_revision` when you change the control.

state.description: `disabled` means no cleanup approval exists. `enabled` means cleanup runs for the approved policy revision. `paused` means an approval exists but scheduling is stopped.

updated_at.description: Time the control last changed.

RetentionExpiryCounts.description: Counts for audit records or retirement receipts. Each record is counted once, under the first reason that applies, so the other counts add up to `total`.

awaiting_deadline.description: Records whose retention period hasn't ended yet.

held.description: Records protected by a Retention Hold.

purge_pending.description: Receipts whose retired files are still waiting to be removed from storage.

referenced.description: Records that other records still refer to.

source_protected.description: Records protected because an export that relies on them is being built.

unconfigured.description: Records with no audit retention period configured.

unfinished.description: Records whose audited work hasn't finished.

items.description: Holds on this page.

next_cursor.description: Token to pass as `cursor` to read the next page. Treat it as unreadable. Omitted on the last page.

RetentionHoldResponse.description: A Retention Hold on an Exam, a Sitting or a Submission.

exam_id.description: Exam the hold is on, or that contains the held Sitting or Submission.

exam_sitting_id.description: Held Sitting, or the Sitting of the held Submission. Omitted for an Exam hold.

integrity_retired_submission_count.description: Number of Submissions in the hold's scope whose integrity records were already retired when the hold was created. The hold can't restore them.

private_reason.description: Private reason from the Institution, with no leading or trailing spaces. At most 4,000 UTF-8 bytes. It is never written to the ordinary audit log.

reason_code.description: Reason code for the audit log. Put case details only in the matching private reason field.

release_private_reason.description: Private reason from the Institution, with no leading or trailing spaces. At most 4,000 UTF-8 bytes. It is never written to the ordinary audit log.

release_reason_code.description: Reason code for the audit log. Put case details only in the matching private reason field.

released_at.description: Time the hold was released. Omitted while it is active.

released_by_user_id.description: User who released the hold. Omitted while it is active.

revision.description: Revision of the hold. Send it as `expected_revision` to release it.

submission_id.description: Held Submission. Present only for a Submission hold.

work_retired_submission_count.description: Number of Submissions in the hold's scope whose work was already retired when the hold was created. The hold can't restore them.

RetentionNoticeResponse.description: A notice that one category of a Submission's records has entered deletion grace.

canceled_at.description: Time the notice was canceled. Omitted unless it was canceled.

category.description: Which records are due to be retired: the work, the integrity evidence, the Browser Activity or the security operational data of the Submission.

delivery_error_code.description: Public reason the notice email failed or was suppressed. Omitted when there is none.

delivery_state.description: Status of the notice email. `pending` means the email hasn't been queued yet. The other values are mail delivery states. Delivery doesn't mean the recipient read it.

exam_title.description: Title of the Exam revision the Sitting delivered. It can't change. Every recipient of the notice sees it, even one who no longer has access to the Exam.

retire_after.description: Earliest time the records may be retired. It no longer applies once the retirement is canceled.

retirement_id.description: ID of the scheduled Record Retirement the notice is about. Pages are ordered by this ID.

sitting_end_at.description: Scheduled end of the Sitting whose records the notice covers.

sitting_start_at.description: Scheduled start of the Sitting whose records the notice covers.

state.description: `grace` means retirement is scheduled and waits for `retire_after`. `canceled` means the scheduled retirement was called off. `retired` means the records were removed.

submission_id.description: Submission whose records are due to be retired.

items.description: Notices on this page, in retirement ID order.

next_cursor.description: Token to pass as `cursor` to read the next page. Treat it as unreadable. Omitted on the last page.

audit_retention_days.description: Days to keep each completed audit or receipt event, counted from that event. Zero keeps them with no expiry. Unfinished work and records that still refer to them keep them longer.

browser_activity_retention_days.description: Days to keep Browser Activity after the current Sitting Records Completion. Zero means no expiry is configured. Deletion still needs approval, a grace period, completion and no Retention Hold.

candidate_notices.description: Also notify candidates when their records enter grace. Exam Managers and operators are always notified.

deletion_grace_days.description: Days each record waits in grace before cleanup may retire it. Cleanup can only be approved when this is above zero. Zero means not configured and never allows immediate deletion. Seven days is the suggested starting value.

expected_revision.description: The policy revision you read before editing. If the policy changed since, the request fails instead of overwriting newer settings.

export_retention_days.description: Days a temporary export archive is kept. Creating an export needs a value from 1 to 7, so with 0 no export can be created. An existing archive keeps the expiry set when it was requested.

integrity_retention_days.description: Days to keep integrity evidence, Reviews and released remarks after the current Sitting Records Completion. Zero keeps them with no expiry. Unresolved Reviews block completion.

security_operational_retention_days.description: Days to keep security operational data after the current Sitting Records Completion. Zero means no expiry is configured. Deletion still needs approval, a grace period, completion and no Retention Hold.

submission_retention_days.description: Days to keep Submission work after the current Sitting Records Completion. Zero keeps it with no expiry. Supporting integrity evidence, Retention Holds and source protections can keep it longer.

audit_retention_days.description: Days to keep completed audit and receipt events, counted from each event. Unfinished work and records that still refer to them keep them longer. Zero keeps them with no expiry.

automatic_deletion_enabled.description: True only when a separate cleanup approval is active for this exact policy revision and the grace period is above zero. It can't be set directly.

browser_activity_retention_days.description: Days to keep Browser Activity after the current Sitting Records Completion. Zero means no expiry is configured. Deletion still needs approval, a grace period, completion and no Retention Hold.

candidate_notices.description: Whether candidates are notified too. Exam Managers and operators are always notified.

created_at.description: Time the policy was first created.

deletion_grace_days.description: Days each record waits in grace before it is retired. Zero means not configured, and then cleanup can't be approved.

export_retention_days.description: Days a temporary export archive is kept. Creating an export needs 1 to 7 days. An existing archive keeps the expiry set when it was requested.

integrity_retention_days.description: Days to keep integrity evidence, Reviews and released remarks after the current Sitting Records Completion. Zero keeps them with no expiry.

revision.description: Current policy revision. Send it as `expected_revision` when you replace the policy.

security_operational_retention_days.description: Days to keep security operational data after the current Sitting Records Completion. Zero means no expiry is configured. Deletion still needs approval, a grace period, completion and no Retention Hold.

submission_retention_days.description: Days to keep Submission work after the current Sitting Records Completion. Zero keeps it with no expiry. Integrity evidence it supports and Retention Holds still protect it.

updated_at.description: Time the policy last changed.

RetentionPreviewCounts.description: Counts for one record category. Each record is counted once, under the first reason that applies, so the other counts add up to `total`.

awaiting_deadline.description: Records whose retention period hasn't ended yet.

eligible.description: Records that cleanup could retire now.

export_protected.description: Records protected because an export that includes them is being built.

held.description: Records protected by a Retention Hold.

incomplete.description: Records whose Sitting has no current Sitting Records Completion.

supporting_work.description: Work kept because it supports integrity evidence that has no expiry.

total.description: Number of records in the category.

unconfigured.description: Records whose category has no retention period configured.

RetentionPreviewRequest.description: Which policy revision a new Retention Preview assesses.

expected_revision.description: The current policy revision to assess. The request fails if the policy changed since.

RetentionPreviewResponse.description: A one-hour Retention Preview of one policy revision. It holds counts only, never content.

expires_at.description: Time after which the preview can no longer be used to approve cleanup.

id.description: ID of the preview. Send it as `preview_id` to approve cleanup.

integrity.description: Counts for integrity evidence and Reviews.

RetentionRecord.description: Retention status of one category of one Submission's records. It contains no content.

blocker.description: First reason the records can't be retired yet. Empty when they are eligible now. `retention_period` means the period hasn't ended. `export_in_progress` means an export is being built from them. `supporting_integrity` means the work supports integrity evidence with no expiry.

category.description: Which of the Submission's records this item covers.

completed_at.description: Time the Sitting's records were last completed. Omitted if they were never completed.

completion_current.description: True when the Sitting's records completion is current. A stale or missing completion blocks retention.

completion_revision.description: Revision of the Sitting's records completion.

eligible_at.description: Time the retention period ends and the records become eligible. Omitted when no period applies.

export_protected_until.description: Time until which an export being built protects these records. Omitted when no export protects them.

has_integrity.description: True when the Submission has integrity evidence.

held.description: True when a Retention Hold covers these records.

retired_at.description: Time these records were retired. Omitted until then.

retirement.description: The scheduled or completed retirement of these records. Omitted when there is none.

shared_published_objects.description: Number of shared published files the work refers to. They survive work retirement, which only releases the Submission's reference to them.

as_of.description: Time the statuses were worked out.

items.description: Records on this page, four per Submission, in the order work, integrity, Browser Activity, security operational.

next_cursor.description: Token to pass as `cursor` to read the next page. Treat it as unreadable. Omitted on the last page.

policy_revision.description: Policy revision the statuses were worked out with.

RetentionRetirement.description: The scheduled or completed retirement of one category of a Submission's records. After retirement it remains as a short receipt with no content.

completion_revision.description: Sitting Records Completion revision the retirement was based on.

control_revision.description: Cleanup control revision that approved the retirement.

policy_revision.description: Policy revision in force when the retirement was scheduled.

purge_pending.description: Number of stored objects of the retired records still waiting to be removed from storage.

purge_verified.description: Number of stored objects confirmed gone from current storage. This doesn't cover backups or earlier object versions.

retire_after.description: Earliest time the records may be retired.

retired_at.description: Time the records were retired. Omitted unless `state` is `retired`.

state.description: `grace` means retirement is scheduled and waits for `retire_after`. `canceled` means it was called off. `retired` means the records were removed.

RevokeOtherSessionsResponse.description: How many of the current User's other Sessions this request revoked.

revoked_session_count.description: How many other Sessions this request revoked. 0 when no other Session was active.

session_id.description: The ID of the Session to revoke. It must belong to the current User.

RoleBindingListResponse.description: A page of current and past Role Bindings you can see.

items.description: The Role Bindings on this page.

total.description: Number of Role Bindings that match the filters, across all pages. Sent on the first page only. Counting stops at 10,000, and then `total_is_lower_bound` is true.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when `total` reached 10,000 and there may be more. Sent with `total`.

RoleBindingResponse.description: A grant of one Role to one User at one scope: the Institution, an Academic Unit or a Class. It is in effect from `start_at` until `end_at`, if set.

archived_at.description: Time the Role Binding was archived. Omitted while it is not archived.

created_at.description: Time the Role Binding was created.

end_at.description: Time the grant stops. Omitted for a grant with no end.

granted_by.description: Who granted the Role: the person who made a manual grant, or the inviter of an invitation, who is the importer for an imported invitation. Omitted only for the grant made at installation.

granted_via.description: How the grant was made: by a person directly (`manual`), by accepting an invitation (`invitation`), or at installation (`bootstrap`).

display_name.description: The Role's display name, localized for the protected System Administrator role. Omitted for an archived Role.

scope.description: The scope the grant applies to, named.

name.description: The Institution, Academic Unit or Class display name. Omitted when it is archived.

scope_id.description: The Institution, Academic Unit or Class the grant applies to.

scope_type.description: Kind of scope the grant applies to, `institution`, `academic_unit` or `class`.

start_at.description: Time the grant takes effect.

updated_at.description: Time of the latest change, such as ending the Binding.

user_id.description: The User who receives the Role.

RoleHolders.description: Who holds a Role now, counting only the Role Bindings you can see. A Binding counts when it is in effect at the time of the request, its scope is not archived, and it sits inside your role_binding.view scopes. Sent on Role reads only, and only if you hold role_binding.view somewhere. Counting stops at 10,000 Bindings. `users` and `scopes` are counted from those Bindings, so when `bindings` reaches 10,000 all three numbers are minimums.

bindings.description: Number of current Role Bindings of this Role that you can see.

bindings_is_lower_bound.description: True when `bindings` reached 10,000 and there may be more.

scopes.description: Number of different scopes (scope type and ID) those Bindings are at.

scopes_is_lower_bound.description: True when `scopes` may be higher than reported, because counting stopped at 10,000 Bindings.

users.description: Number of different Users who hold those Bindings.

users_is_lower_bound.description: True when `users` may be higher than reported, because counting stopped at 10,000 Bindings.

RoleListResponse.description: A page of Roles you can see.

items.description: The Roles on this page, sorted by `name` and then `id`.

RoleResponse.description: A named set of permissions. A Role grants nothing by itself. A User gets its permissions only through a Role Binding at a scope.

archived_at.description: Time the Role was archived. Omitted while it is active.

built_in.description: True for a Role that ships with Proctor. Built-in Roles can't be edited or deleted.

description.description: What the Role is for, in plain text.

display_name.description: Name shown to people.

holders.description: Who holds the Role now. Present only if you hold role_binding.view somewhere.

name.description: Machine name of the Role. It can't change after creation.

permissions.description: The permissions the Role grants, such as `class.view`. Each appears once.

updated_at.description: Time of the latest change to the Role.

SHA256.description: A SHA-256 digest as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

SaveExamIntegrityDecisionRequest.description: A new or replacement decision for one integrity Flag.

expected_review_revision.description: 0 when this decision creates the Review; otherwise the Review's current revision.

expected_revision.description: 0 for the first decision on this Flag; otherwise the decision's current revision.

outcome.description: Your conclusion about the Flag: `confirmed`, `dismissed` or `inconclusive`. It is about integrity only, never a grade or a verdict of guilt.

private_rationale.description: Why you reached this outcome. Only managers can see it. Send valid UTF-8 with no leading or trailing whitespace: at most 1000 characters and 4000 bytes.

submission_review_id.description: The Review's ID. Required once the Review exists. Leave it out only when this decision creates the Review.

ScheduleExamSittingRequest.description: The Exam Revision, Class and time window for a new Sitting.

class_id.description: The Class whose members can take the Sitting.

exam_revision_id.description: The published Exam Revision to deliver. It must belong to this Exam.

scheduled_end_at.description: The Sitting's deadline. It must be after the start and inside the Class's Academic Period.

scheduled_start_at.description: When the Sitting opens. It must be in the future and inside the Class's Academic Period.

ScreenClipListResponse.description: One page of the collection in its stable order.

failure.description: Why the clip failed; present only when state is failed.

chunk_bytes.description: The size of every chunk but the last.

content_digest.description: The SHA-256 of the clip's manifest: "proctor-screen-clip-v1", the media type, size, chunk size and every chunk hash in order, each followed by a line feed.

received_chunks.description: The numbers, from 1, of the chunks that arrived, in order.

ScreenRecordingDisclosure.description: Localized recorder notice, not consent or playback authority. Zero days means no configured automatic expiry; holds still apply.

audience.description: Who may play an uploaded clip.

clip_retention_days.description: Uploaded clips are integrity evidence and follow its retention period.

local_recording.description: Desktop records the whole session on the device and deletes it at submission.

uploads.description: Only ranges the Sitting's Exam Managers ask for, or the minute either side of a Flag, leave the device.

SearchClassItem.description: An unarchived Class within the caller's class.view scope.

display_name.description: The Class name shown to people.

programme_level_id.description: The Programme Level the Class belongs to.

SearchExamItem.description: An Exam the caller may see in the Exam catalog, titled by its current Draft.

academic_unit_id.description: The Academic Unit that owns the Exam.

title.description: The title of the Exam's current Draft.

SearchItem.description: One search match, discriminated by type.

SearchResponse.description: Up to `limit` matches of each requested type, grouped by type. Search never continues, so `next_cursor` is always omitted.

items.description: The matches, Exams first, then Classes, then Users.

next_cursor.description: Never present. Search does not continue past its single page.

SearchUserItem.description: A User visible in the caller's User directory. The email address is never included.

display_name.description: The User's name as shown to people.

SecurityControlResult.description: How the server processed Desktop's latest security control: the lease renewal and its delivery watermarks. A renewal never changes whether the candidate may interact; only closing native delivery does.

capability_matrix_digest.description: SHA-256 of the exact signed bytes of the release's certification document.

screen_recording_disclosure.description: The recorder notice to show before Start; null when the Exam does not record the screen.

SecurityPolicyResponse.description: Privileged registered-Desktop response bounded to 128 KiB. Catalog bindings are unique and sorted by kind then catalog_id. First admission returns null configuration; Ready rejoin returns the original immutable configuration.

capability_matrix_digest.description: SHA-256 of the exact signed bytes of the release's certification document.

screen_recording_disclosure.description: The recorder notice to show before Start; null when the Exam does not record the screen.

SecurityPreflightReport.description: What Desktop observed at Start, at most 128 KiB: one fresh fact for each activated capability and its own status for each readiness rule. No inventories, media, clipboard bytes, OS errors or arbitrary details are accepted. The server evaluates the readiness rules on these facts and its result decides admission. The server computes the report digest. Client reported_at is provenance; server time controls challenge expiry and admission freshness.

capabilities.description: One fresh fact for every activated capability at Start, in the policy's activation order.

rules.description: Desktop's own status for every readiness rule.
The server's own status for every readiness rule, evaluated on the reported state. Where it differs from Desktop's, the server's decides admission.

SelfAuditEvent.description: The name of one event in the account history. The list is fixed but can grow in later releases. Clients write their own labels and should show an unknown name in a generic way.

SelfAuditEventResponse.description: One event in the current User's own account history.

actor.description: Who performed the event. It never identifies another person.

kind.description: Who performed the event: the User, another person with authority over the account, or work with no signed-in actor such as a background Job, offline recovery, or an emailed link.

client_type.description: Kind of client the event came from, when recorded.

error_code.description: A code for why a failed event failed. It holds no private details, and the values don't change between releases.

event.description: The name of the event, such as password.changed. A newer server may send a name this contract does not list yet, so show an unknown name in a generic way.

ip_address.description: The IP address of the User's own action. Left out for anyone else's.

relation.description: `subject` when the event is about the User's account, or `actor` when the User performed it on anything else.

resource.description: What the event was recorded against.

id.description: The resource ID. Present only when the resource is the User, the Institution, or an Academic Unit or Class where the User has or had a membership or Role Binding.

type.description: The type of the resource the event was recorded against, such as user or class. The values don't change between releases.

summary.description: One sentence describing the event in the language chosen for the request. It is for display only, so clients that need to act on the event should read its codes. It never names who acted on the User. It names a User the User acted on only while the User can see them now, and a failed event says so.

user_agent.description: The user agent of the User's own action. Left out for anyone else's.

SelfAuditListResponse.description: One page of the current User's own account history, with at most 200 items.

items.description: The events on this page, in the requested order.

next_cursor.description: Pass this back as cursor to get the next page. Treat it as a token and don't read or change it. Left out on the last page.

runs.description: Stretches of two or more consecutive items on this page that read as one line, in page order and never overlapping. Omitted when the page has none.

total.description: Events matching the filters across every page, present only on the first page. At 10,000 counting stops and `total_is_lower_bound` is true.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when `total` reached the 10,000 limit and the history may be longer. Present with `total`.

SelfAuditRun.description: Consecutive items on one page with the same actor kind, event, recorded operation, status, and relation.

length.description: Number of items the run covers, starting at `start`.

start.description: Index in `items` of the run's first item.

summary.description: One plural sentence for the whole run in the negotiated language, counted by its items, such as "You changed 5 profile pictures". It names no person or resource, and a failed run says so.

text.description: The message; line breaks and tabs are its only control characters.

SessionAdministrationListResponse.description: One page of a User's Sessions, newest first.

items.description: The User's Sessions on this page, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass this back as cursor to get the next page. Treat it as a token and don't read or change it. Left out on the last page.

archived_at.description: When the Session record was archived. Left out when it has not been archived.

authenticated_at.description: When the Session was first signed in.

authentication_method.description: How the Session was signed in: password for a local password, or the external provider's protocol, such as oidc or cas.

authentication_strength.description: single_factor when the Session was signed in with one factor, or multi_factor when it also passed two-step verification.

client_type.description: The kind of client the Session was created for.

desktop_architecture.description: The processor architecture the Desktop was built for. Present only for a desktop Session.

desktop_build_id.description: The Desktop build identifier recorded when the Session was created. Present only for a desktop Session.

desktop_platform.description: The operating system the Desktop runs on. Present only for a desktop Session.

desktop_realtime_protocol.description: The realtime protocol version the Desktop speaks. Present only for a desktop Session.

desktop_registration_id.description: The ID of the Desktop Registration the Session is bound to. Present only for a desktop Session.

desktop_release.description: The Desktop release version recorded when the Session was created. Present only for a desktop Session.

device_id.description: The device identifier the client sent when it signed in. Left out when it sent none.

device_name.description: The readable device name the client sent when it signed in. Left out when it sent none.

expires_at.description: When the Session ends no matter how often it is used.

idle_expires_at.description: When the Session ends if it stays unused. Each recorded use of the Session moves this later.

last_activity_at.description: When the Session was last used. Proctor records use at most once per activity update interval, so this can trail the latest request.

mfa_completed_at.description: When the Session last passed two-step verification. Left out when it never has.

mfa_enrollment_required.description: Whether the Access Policy limits this Web Session until its User sets up or completes two-step verification. While it is true, the Session can only set up two-step verification, answer the two-step verification challenge, reauthenticate, read the security status and sign out.

mfa_recovery_required.description: Whether this Session is limited, after an administrator reset two-step verification, until its User sets up a new authenticator app.

reauthenticated_at.description: When the User last proved who they are again on this Session, with the same method they signed in with. It does not change authenticated_at or mfa_completed_at. Left out when the Session has never reauthenticated.

revocation_reason.description: A readable explanation of revocation_reason_code in the request's language. Present only when the Session was revoked.

revocation_reason_code.description: Why the Session was revoked. Present only when revoked_at is set.

revoked_at.description: When the Session was revoked. Left out while it is still active.

updated_at.description: When the Session record last changed.

user_id.description: The ID of the User the Session belongs to.

SessionListResponse.description: One page of the collection in its stable order.

items.description: The current User's active Sessions on this page, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass this back as cursor to get the next page. Left out on the last page.

archived_at.description: When the Session record was archived. Left out when it has not been archived.

authenticated_at.description: When the Session was first signed in.

authentication_method.description: How the Session was signed in: password for a local password, or the external provider's protocol, such as oidc or cas.

authentication_strength.description: single_factor when the Session was signed in with one factor, or multi_factor when it also passed two-step verification.

client_type.description: The kind of client the Session was created for.

desktop_architecture.description: The processor architecture the Desktop was built for. Present only for a desktop Session.

desktop_build_id.description: The Desktop build identifier recorded when the Session was created. Present only for a desktop Session.

desktop_platform.description: The operating system the Desktop runs on. Present only for a desktop Session.

desktop_realtime_protocol.description: The realtime protocol version the Desktop speaks. Present only for a desktop Session.

desktop_registration_id.description: The ID of the Desktop Registration the Session is bound to. Present only for a desktop Session.

desktop_release.description: The Desktop release version recorded when the Session was created. Present only for a desktop Session.

device_id.description: The device identifier the client sent when it signed in. Left out when it sent none.

device_name.description: The readable device name the client sent when it signed in. Left out when it sent none.

expires_at.description: When the Session ends no matter how often it is used.

info.description: The reviewed public HTTP and WebSocket contract for one Proctor installation. Operations are grouped by stable product areas, declare authentication and idempotency requirements explicitly, and return RFC 9457 Problem Details for documented failures. The routing kernel also answers any operation with route.not_found (404), route.method_not_allowed (405), or request.too_large (413) Problem Details for an unknown path, an unsupported method, or a request body over the operation's limit. JSON request bodies require one Content-Type of application/json, optionally with charset=utf-8. Unsafe browser requests must use the configured public origin; conflicting Origin or Fetch Metadata headers are rejected before authentication. Native clients may omit browser headers. Cookie-authenticated mutations also require their signed CSRF proof. CAS and OIDC GET callbacks retain their purpose-specific state and browser-binding checks.
info.title: Proctor Server API

post.description:
Applies one operation to 1 to 200 existing Users in a single request. Each item runs on its own, with the same authorization, audit, mail and retry behavior as the matching single-item endpoint, so one failed item does not stop the others. The response reports every item's outcome in request order.
Item keys must be unique within the request; repeated keys fail those items with `request.invalid`. An item that would make the same change as another item in the request fails with `onboarding_batch.duplicate`. Role Binding operations, `user.enable`, `user.disable` and `user_sessions.revoke` also need a strong, recent Session.
post.summary: Run one bounded typed existing-User academic administration batch

post.description:
Previews one academic administration operation applied to every existing User that a User directory filter matches. The filter takes the same fields as the User directory, with the same validation and visibility rules, including the fields only an Institution-wide viewer may use. A filter the directory would refuse is refused here too.
Nothing changes yet. A background Job applies the filter with your visibility at that moment, saves the ordered list of matching Users, and puts each row in `will_change`, `no_op` or `skipped`, with a reason for each skipped row. Your own account is always skipped, and a disable or Session revocation also skips System Administrators. If more than 10,000 Users match, the preview fails with `academic_administration_preview.too_many_users`; narrow the filter and try again.
Poll the preview until it is `preview_ready` or `failed`. `class.transfer` is not offered, because a transfer must name the exact enrollment it replaces; a Student Progression does that instead. Requires a strong, recent interactive Session.
post.summary: Preview one academic administration operation over the Users a directory filter matches

get.description:
Reads one of your own previews: its state, operation, filter, digest and revision and, once it is ready, a `summary` of its rows by group, with skipped rows counted by reason. The summary counts only the rows whose User your User directory shows now, which are the rows the rows listing returns. After commit, the row counts report what happened when each row ran.
Only the User who created a preview can read it, and only while they can see onboarding batches at its scope. A caller without that access is denied, and any other User gets not found. If your directory would now refuse the preview's filter (for example an activity filter after you lose Institution-wide `user.view`, or a Role filter after you lose `role.view`), the read is refused with `academic_administration_preview.authorization_lost`.
get.summary: Read one academic administration preview and its counts

post.description: Cancels your own preview before it finishes. Rows that have not run yet are canceled. A row that is already running finishes, and rows that already completed are never undone.
post.summary: Cancel one unfinished academic administration preview

post.description:
Commits your own ready preview if its revision and digest still match, within 15 minutes of it becoming ready, measured by the server's database clock. After that the commit is refused with `academic_administration_preview.expired`, and you need a new preview. A preview another User created reads as not found, and the commit is refused with `academic_administration_preview.authorization_lost` once your User directory would refuse the preview's filter.
One background Job then runs the saved rows. It never runs the filter again, so a User who starts matching after the preview is not changed. Each row is authorized again when it runs. A row whose User your directory no longer shows fails with `authorization.denied`, and once your directory would refuse the filter, every remaining row fails the same way. The first commit records one audit entry for the whole batch, with the operation, filter, counts and preview ID. Each row also gets its own audit entry naming the preview and row, whether it succeeds or fails. The response is the preview as the commit recorded it, and repeating the request with the same Idempotency-Key returns that same commit. Requires a strong, recent interactive Session.
post.summary: Commit one exact academic administration preview

get.description: Pages through the saved rows of one group of your own preview, in row order. Each row names its User and, after commit, its outcome. A row appears only while your User directory still shows its User, so if your visibility has narrowed since the preview was made, you no longer see the Users you lost. Once your directory would refuse the preview's filter, the read is refused with `academic_administration_preview.authorization_lost`. A cursor only continues the group and reason it was issued for.

parameters.description: The group of rows to list.
parameters.name: group

parameters.description: Only with `group=skipped`. List only the rows skipped for this reason.
parameters.name: reason

get.summary: Show who is in one group of an academic administration preview

get.description: Lists the Academic Periods the caller can see through permissions on the Institution or on Academic Units, ordered by start time, then name, then identifier. An Academic Period is a span of academic time, such as a year or semester. Seeing one gives no access to its Classes or students.

parameters.description: Text to find in the Academic Period name or display name, matched literally and ignoring case.
parameters.name: q

get.summary: List or search Academic Periods visible through authorized owner scopes

post.description: Creates an Academic Period owned by the Institution or by one Academic Unit. The caller needs permission on that owner itself. `start_at` is included in the Period and `end_at` is not. Both are RFC 3339 times. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retry after an unclear failure can't create a second Period.
post.summary: Create an Institution- or Academic-Unit-owned Academic Period

delete.description: Archives one Academic Period, but only when no active Class or enrollment still depends on it. Its history is kept. Archiving never deletes Classes, ends memberships or moves students on.
delete.summary: Archive an Academic Period with no active Classes or enrollments

get.description: Returns one Academic Period when the caller can see its owner. The response gives its owner and start and end times. It does not give access to the Classes that run in it.
get.summary: Get an Academic Period

patch.description: Changes some of an Academic Period's display fields or its start and end times. Its owner stays the same. Proctor rejects new times that would break the Classes and memberships that depend on the Period or that conflict with its current saved state.
patch.summary: Update an Academic Period without changing its owner

delete.description: Ends one Academic Unit membership that is in effect, after checking that you may manage members of its Academic Unit. The membership keeps its dates and audit history. Ending it does not remove the member's Affiliations, Roles or Role Bindings.
delete.summary: End organizational membership while retaining history

get.description: Without `q`, lists the top-level Academic Units of the Institution. With `q`, searches every active Academic Unit in the Institution whose name or display name contains the text, ignoring case. Both need academic_unit.view on the Institution. Seeing an Academic Unit does not let the caller change it. Results come in pages ordered by name and then by identifier, at most `limit` per page.

parameters.description: Text to find in the name or display name, matched literally and ignoring case. Without it, only top-level Academic Units are listed.
parameters.name: q

get.summary: List or search Academic Units

post.description: Creates a top-level Academic Unit in the Institution. The caller needs academic_unit.manage on the Institution. Send an Idempotency-Key to make retries safe: a retry with the same key and body returns the first result, and the same key with a different body is a conflict. The server sets the new Unit's identifier, timestamps and Institution.
post.summary: Create a root Academic Unit

x-codeSamples.source:
curl --fail-with-body \
  --request POST \
  --url 'https://proctor.example.edu/api/v1/academic-units' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <access-token>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Idempotency-Key: docs-academic-unit-001' \
  --data '{"name":"computer-science","display_name":"Computer Science","description":"Teaching and research in computing."}'

delete.description: Archives one empty Academic Unit and keeps its place in the hierarchy and its audit history. Proctor does not archive anything beneath it: if the Unit still has active child Units, Programmes, memberships or permission grants, the request fails instead.

get.description: Returns one Academic Unit when the caller holds academic_unit.view on it. The response names its Institution and parent. It does not include the Units beneath it or any permission grants.
get.summary: Get an Academic Unit

patch.description: Changes some of an Academic Unit's fields and can move it under another parent. A move needs management permission on both the Unit and its new parent, or on the Institution when it becomes top-level. Proctor rejects the whole change if it would create a cycle, cross Institutions, rely on out-of-date data or break the hierarchy in any other way. Nothing is applied in that case.
patch.summary: Update or reparent an Academic Unit

get.description: Lists the active Academic Units directly under one Academic Unit, ordered by name and then by identifier. The caller needs academic_unit.view on the parent. Units further down are not included. List each child's children to walk the tree.
get.summary: List an Academic Unit's direct children

post.description: Creates an Academic Unit directly under the Academic Unit in the path. The parent always comes from the path. The caller needs academic_unit.manage on the parent, checked before the Unit is created.
post.summary: Create a child Academic Unit

get.description: Searches the active Classes under the active Programmes this Academic Unit owns directly. The caller needs class.view on the Academic Unit. Results describe the Classes only: they never enroll students or give the caller permission on a Class. Items are ordered by name, then by identifier, in the `dir` direction. The first page, read without a cursor, also reports `total`, the number of Classes the filters match across every page. It is exact below 10,000. At 10,000 counting stops and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. Later pages carry no total, so keep the first page's. Each item carries `student_count`, the Class's current members counted up to 10,000, with `student_count_is_lower_bound`, but only when the caller holds class.members.view on this Academic Unit. Otherwise both are omitted.

parameters.description: Text to find in the Class name or display name, matched literally and ignoring case.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Sort by name, then by identifier, ascending (`asc`, the default) or descending (`desc`). A cursor works only with the direction that produced it.
parameters.name: dir

get.summary: Search Classes owned by an Academic Unit

post.description: Invites an existing User, by email address, to one Role scoped to the Academic Unit in the path. Acceptance cannot widen the Role, scope or dates the Invitation records. The claim is only ever sent by email and used to accept.

requestBody.description: The existing User's address, the Role to grant, and an optional start and end at the Academic Unit in the path.

201.description: The Invitation was issued. The response contains neither the claim nor mailbox details.

post.summary: Invite an existing User to one exact Academic Unit Role package

post.description: Invites a teacher into one Academic Unit with one Role you may delegate. The request checks the recipient address, whether the Role can be delegated, the start and end, and your authority as the inviter. Once issued, the Invitation's terms cannot change. The one-time claim is sent by email and never returned to you.

requestBody.description: The recipient, the Role to delegate, an optional start and end, and suggested profile fields for the new teacher account.

201.description: The Invitation was issued. The response contains neither the claim nor mailbox details.

post.summary: Invite a teacher into one exact Academic Unit with one delegated Role package

get.description:
Lists the memberships of one Academic Unit that you may see: either those in effect at one instant, or the full history. A membership records a relationship only. It never grants permissions by itself.
Pages are ordered by `sort` and `dir`, by default by membership start (`since`), oldest first, then by ID. The first page also reports `total`, the number of memberships the filter matches across all pages. It is exact below 10,000; at 10,000 counting stops and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. A cursor keeps the first page's instant or history filter and its order, but every page reads current data, so memberships added or changed between requests can change later pages.
Each item names the member in `user`. `email` is included only if you hold Institution-wide user.view. If you hold role_binding.view on this Academic Unit, each item also lists the member's current Role Bindings scoped exactly to it, in `roles_here`.

parameters.description: Return the memberships in effect at this instant. Defaults to now. It cannot be combined with `history=true`. When following a cursor you may omit it, because the cursor keeps the first page's instant.
parameters.name: active_at

parameters.description: When true, return the full membership history instead of only the memberships in effect at one instant. It cannot be combined with `active_at`.
parameters.name: history

parameters.description: The page order, each key followed by membership ID: `since` (the membership start, the default) or `name` (the member's display name, or their username when there is none, compared case-insensitively on its first 64 characters). A cursor only continues the sort and direction that produced it, so repeat both when following it.
parameters.name: sort

parameters.description: Ascending (`asc`, the default) or descending (`desc`) by the `sort` key.
parameters.name: dir

get.summary: List effective-dated organizational members

post.description: Adds an existing User to the Academic Unit in the path, from an optional start time. The request rechecks your authority over the Academic Unit and refuses a membership that overlaps another one. It creates no Role or Role Binding.
post.summary: Create organizational membership without granting permissions

get.description: Lists the active Programmes this Academic Unit owns directly, optionally narrowed by `q`. Programmes of Units further down are not included. List them through those Units. The first page, read without a cursor, also reports `total`, the number of Programmes the filters match across every page. It is exact below 10,000. At 10,000 counting stops and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. Later pages carry no total, so keep the first page's.

parameters.description: Text to find in the Programme name or display name, matched literally and ignoring case.
parameters.name: q

get.summary: List or search Programmes owned by an Academic Unit

post.description: Creates a Programme owned by the Academic Unit in the path. The caller's management permission is checked again when the request is handled. Creating a Programme does not create Programme Levels, Classes, enrollments, Roles or Role Bindings.
post.summary: Create a Programme owned by an Academic Unit

get.description: Returns the installation's whole current Access Policy, the deployment facts an administrator needs to edit it, and up to 100 of its most recent changes. Provider secrets and mail settings are never included.
get.summary: Get the revisioned Access Policy and bounded transition history

put.description: Replaces the whole Access Policy. Send the `revision` you read as `expected_revision`. If the policy has changed since, the request fails and nothing changes. Proctor checks again, as it saves the change, that the deployment supports the new settings and that a system administrator can still sign in. When you ask it to, Proctor signs out Sessions that used a sign-in method you are turning off. If the change starts requiring two-step verification for role holders, it also signs out their Sessions that have not proved a second factor. When a Session length gets shorter, running Sessions get the earlier deadline. The request needs a recent, strongly authenticated interactive Session and an Idempotency-Key.
put.summary: Revision-fenced replacement of the installation Access Policy

post.description: Checks a proposed Access Policy without saving it. Proctor compares it with the current revision and checks the configured providers, Invitation mail delivery, two-step verification support and whether a system administrator could still sign in. It also counts the role holders without two-step verification and their Sessions that have not proved a second factor. Nothing is saved and the revision is not held for you, so the replacement runs every check again.
post.summary: Evaluate an Access Policy replacement without mutating it

get.description: Returns the counts shown as badges in administration navigation. `pending_invitations` counts pending Invitations that have not expired. `failed_jobs` counts operator-visible Jobs that failed in the last seven days. `failed_mail_deliveries` counts mail deliveries that ended in the `failed` state. Suppressed and canceled deliveries are not failures. `open_onboarding_imports` counts unexpired administrative onboarding imports that are still uploading, parsing, waiting to be committed or running, not counting student progressions. Each count applies the same permission and visibility checks as its resource's own list, and records the permission decision the same way, so it counts only what the caller could list. A count the caller may not list is left out, together with its `_is_lower_bound` flag. If a count can't be read, the request fails rather than reporting zero. Counting stops at 1,000: the count is then 1,000 and its flag is true. Only an interactive Session may read the counts.
get.summary: Summarise administration work waiting on the caller

delete.description: Ends one Affiliation that is in effect, after checking that you may manage the User. The User's other Affiliations stay in effect, and ending this one never revokes credentials or permissions.
delete.summary: End an Affiliation while retaining history

get.description: System administrators manage immutable assistant profiles. Creation requires a configured provider. Retirement preserves the recipe used by published exams; transcripts are available only through exam review.

parameters.description: Whether retired profiles are listed too.
parameters.name: include_retired

get.summary: List the assistant profiles

post.description: System administrators manage immutable assistant profiles. Creation requires a configured provider. Retirement preserves the recipe used by published exams; transcripts are available only through exam review.

requestBody.description: The complete profile. Every member is required.

post.summary: Create an assistant profile

parameters.description: The assistant profile to retire.
parameters.name: assistant_profile_id

post.description: System administrators manage immutable assistant profiles. Creation requires a configured provider. Retirement preserves the recipe used by published exams; transcripts are available only through exam review.
post.summary: Retire an assistant profile

get.description: System administrators read counters for retained attempts, including outstanding reservations. No candidate identity or transcript is returned. Counters fall when histories are retired.

parameters.description: The assistant profile to retire.
parameters.name: assistant_profile_id

get.summary: Read aggregate assistant profile usage

get.description: Lists the audit Events you can see through Institution-wide or Academic Unit audit permissions, newest first unless `order=asc` asks for oldest first. Events never include the raw request parameters, earlier state, results, credentials, protected content or internal error details. The first page (read without a cursor) also has `total`, the number of matching Events across all pages. It is exact up to 10,000. Above that it shows 10,000 and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. Later pages have no total, so keep the one from the first page. Each Event also has a `summary` sentence, written from its codes, in the language `Accept-Language` picks. It falls back to the installation language and then English. It names the actor, the User the Event is about, and a User, Academic Unit or Class resource by their current names only if you could see that record now, through `user.view` or `class.members.view`, `academic_unit.view` or `class.view`. Otherwise it uses a general phrase such as "a user" or "a class". For an Academic Unit auditor the summary names only the action, never the recorded operation or the User the Event is about.

parameters.description: Maximum number of audit Events to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page, sent back unchanged with the same filters.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Return only Events where this User performed the action.
parameters.name: actor_id

parameters.description: Return only Events about this User, such as a change to their account.
parameters.name: subject_user_id

parameters.description: Return only Events with one of these actions. Repeat the parameter for up to 32 actions. An Academic Unit auditor still sees only the academic actions they are allowed to, so any other action matches nothing.
parameters.name: action

parameters.description: Return only Events with this outcome: `attempt` (no outcome recorded yet), `success` or `fail`.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Return only Events whose action changes something (`change`: a mutation, a sign-in or other authentication, a credential issued or revoked, mail sent) or only looks (`read`: a view, a search, a list, or an export). Every audit action is one of the two. It only narrows `action` and what you can see, so an Academic Unit auditor still sees only their own academic actions.
parameters.name: kind

parameters.description: Return only Events about resources of this type. Send it together with `resource_id`.
parameters.name: resource_type

parameters.description: Return only Events about the resource with this ID. Send it together with `resource_type`.
parameters.name: resource_id

parameters.description: Return only Events recorded at or after this RFC 3339 time.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Return only Events recorded before this RFC 3339 time. It must be later than `created_after`.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Read newest first (`desc`, the default) or oldest first (`asc`). A cursor works only with the order that produced it.
parameters.name: order

get.summary: List authorized institution or Academic Unit audit history

post.description: Exchanges a one-time Invitation claim for a short-lived browser handle tied to that Invitation and its purpose, without using up the Invitation yet. The response does not repeat the claim, so the claim never has to appear in later browser URLs or logs. It names the address the Invitation was sent to, which acceptance uses and the browser cannot change. For a student Class Invitation only, it also gives the Class display name; Academic Unit and Role names are never returned.
post.summary: Exchange an Invitation claim for a purpose-bound browser acceptance transaction

post.description: Creates the invited account and applies what the Invitation grants, using one browser handle. The password and profile are validated, the handle is used up in the same step, and no claim or credential is ever returned.
post.summary: Accept an account-creating Invitation through its browser transaction

post.description: Applies a Role Invitation to the signed-in User the browser handle is tied to. It never moves the Invitation to another User, and the handle is used up in the same step.
post.summary: Accept a scoped-role Invitation with the current browser Session

post.description: Starts a Desktop sign-in that finishes in the system browser, using version 1 of the handoff. Proctor stores the loopback callback address, state, S256 PKCE challenge, public key, build details and device details for this request, and none of them can change later. The Desktop then opens the returned authorization page in the browser, where the person chooses how to sign in. The request must pass the Desktop compatibility policy, and the Access Policy must allow at least one way to sign in.
post.summary: Create a purpose-bound Desktop browser authorization transaction

post.description: Forgets which account signed in for this request, so the same browser tab can sign in another way. The Desktop's request details stay as they were.
post.summary: Return the same hosted transaction to account selection

post.description: Approves the request after an account has signed in for it. The state must match the one the Desktop sent. Proctor issues one short-lived code and returns the loopback address that hands it to the Desktop. The browser never sees Session credentials. The response also clears the browser's authorization cookie, and the approval is recorded in the audit log.
post.summary: Explicitly approve the authenticated Desktop transaction

post.description: Checks a local username or email address and password, plus a two-step verification code when the account needs one, for this Desktop request only. It does not create a Web Session and does not approve the request.
post.summary: Prove a local account for only this Desktop transaction

get.description: Starts a sign-in with an external provider that can only finish this Desktop request, then redirects the browser to the provider. It does not start an ordinary Web sign-in.

parameters.description: The state value the Desktop sent when it started this request, passed through unchanged.
parameters.name: state

get.summary: Begin provider authentication bound to this Desktop transaction

post.description: Uses the browser's current Web Session to show which account is signing in for this Desktop request. It does not approve the request and does not create another Session.
post.summary: Bind the current Web Session identity without approving the Desktop

post.description: The hosted page sends the request handle, the browser proof from the page address fragment and the state. This works once. Proctor then sets a host-only HttpOnly cookie that ties this browser to the request. The response body is empty, so the page's own scripts never see a credential.
post.summary: Exchange the one-time fragment proof for an HttpOnly browser binding

post.description: Checks the browser's authorization cookie and the state, then cancels the request for good. Every remaining browser proof and code for it stops working, and the response clears the cookie.
post.summary: Terminally cancel the browser-bound Desktop transaction

get.description: Uses the browser's authorization cookie to return what the hosted page needs to show. That is the device name, when the request started, the allowed sign-in methods, when it expires and, once known, the account. The account and its email address appear only after this browser has signed in as that account for this request.
get.summary: Read the safe current hosted-journey context

post.description: Starts confirming, in the system browser, that the person using a Desktop Session is still its account holder. Only a Desktop Session can call this, with a valid DPoP proof from its registered key. Web Sessions and Personal Access Tokens are refused. Proctor stores the loopback callback address, state and S256 PKCE challenge, ties the request to the calling Session, Desktop Registration, key and User, and returns the hosted reauthentication page. The page accepts only the sign-in method the Desktop Session itself used. The request lasts at most five minutes.
post.summary: Start confirming the Desktop Session's account in the system browser

post.description: Needs the browser's reauthentication cookie, the same state the Desktop sent, a successful proof and a Desktop Session that is still active. Proctor then issues one single-use code that expires within a minute. It returns the loopback address to send the browser to, which carries only that code and the state.
post.summary: Hand the confirmed proof back to Proctor Desktop

post.description: Checks the password of the Desktop Session's own User. It works only when the Desktop Session was signed in with a password. It creates no Web Session. When the Desktop Session is single_factor and the User has active Proctor two-step verification, the browser must also prove a code. The Desktop Session is updated only when Desktop calls the complete operation.
post.summary: Prove the Desktop Session account's password

get.description: Accepts only the Desktop Session's own identity provider. Proctor asks the provider for a new sign-in and then returns to the hosted reauthentication page. The provider must confirm the same linked identity the Desktop Session uses. If it confirms any other account, the request is denied and the denial is recorded in the audit log. No User is created and no Session is created.

parameters.description: The state value the Desktop sent when it started this reauthentication, passed through unchanged.
parameters.name: state

get.summary: Begin fresh provider authentication for this Desktop reauthentication

post.description: Uses the Desktop reauthentication cookie and verifies an authenticator code or one unused recovery code. The authenticated browser context can then be approved to finish confirming the Desktop Session.
post.summary: Verify the code for Desktop reauthentication

post.description: The hosted page sends the request handle, the browser proof from the page address fragment and the state. This works once. Proctor then sets a host-only HttpOnly cookie that is sent only to the Desktop reauthentication routes. The response body is empty, so the page's own scripts never see a credential.
post.summary: Exchange the one-time fragment proof for an HttpOnly reauthentication binding

post.description: Checks the browser's reauthentication cookie and the state, then cancels the reauthentication for good. Every remaining browser proof for it stops working.
post.summary: Terminally cancel the browser-bound Desktop reauthentication

post.description: The Desktop redeems the code. The request must carry a DPoP proof from the same Desktop Session and registered key that started the reauthentication. Proctor checks the PKCE verifier, the state, that the code has not expired and has not been used, and checks the proof and the Session again. It then records the new proof time on that Session and saves the audit record with it. No Session is created, the Desktop Registration stays the same and the current access credentials keep working.
post.summary: Redeem the reauthentication code as recent authentication

get.description: Uses the browser's reauthentication cookie to return the Desktop Session account's display name, the one sign-in method this request accepts and when the request expires. The method is either a password or the Desktop Session's own identity provider. A Web Session already open in the browser is never accepted as proof.
get.summary: Read the hosted Desktop reauthentication context

post.description: The Desktop trades the one-time code for a Desktop Session. The code is used up in a single step, and only when the state matches, the code_verifier matches the earlier code_challenge, and no active Attempt is holding the account's Session lock. The public key and build details must match the ones sent at the start, and the DPoP header must carry a proof signed by that key. The response returns DPoP-bound tokens in the body.
post.summary: Exchange one Desktop code and S256 verifier for a Desktop Session

post.description: Uses up the one-time undo token that Proctor emails to an account's previous address when its email changes. Within the configured undo window, it restores that address as the account's verified email, cancels pending verification and password-reset links, signs out every Session of the account and records an audit event. An invalid, expired or already used token reveals no account details. If another account now uses the previous address, the undo is refused.
post.summary: Undo an email change from the previous address

post.description: For one active undo token, returns the previous address it would restore, the account's current address masked as in the warning email, and when the change happened. It never uses up, extends or reissues the token, and it records no audit event. It shares the rate limits of the undo, counted per token and per source address. A token that is unknown, malformed, expired or already used gets the same generic invalid-token error as the undo itself. The token is sent in the body so it stays out of URLs and logs. Only the undo itself checks whether the previous address is still free.
post.summary: Read the email change an undo credential would reverse

post.description: Uses up one valid verification token and marks the email address it was issued for as verified. A token works once and can't verify any other address. An invalid or expired token reveals no account details.
post.summary: Consume an email-verification credential

post.description: Returns the address an active verification token was issued for, so the hosted page can show it before the person confirms. It never uses up, extends or reissues the token, and it records no audit event. It shares the rate limits of completion, counted per token and per source address. A token that is unknown, malformed, expired, replaced or already used gets the same generic invalid-token error as completion. The token is sent in the body so it stays out of URLs and logs. The result is for display only: completion checks the token again.
post.summary: Read the address an email-verification credential would confirm

post.description: Emails a new short-lived verification link to the signed-in User's current email address when it is not yet verified. The response is the same in every case, so it reveals nothing about the account. A new link may replace any earlier link that still works.
post.summary: Request an email-verification message

get.description: Uses the HttpOnly external second-factor cookie set by the provider callback. Returns the account and provider display names and the challenge deadline.
get.summary: Read the pending sign-in verification

post.description: Uses the HttpOnly external second-factor cookie. Accepts an authenticator code or an unused recovery code. A Web sign-in sets the Session cookies and returns the checked original continuation. Desktop authorization returns its authenticated browser context without creating a Web Session. Success clears the verification cookie.
post.summary: Verify a code and finish signing in

post.description: Checks a local username or email address and password, then creates an interactive Session for the declared client type. Web and Desktop clients receive their credentials as host-only cookies, and the response body leaves out tokens. A CLI client receives the access and refresh tokens in the body. An account with two-step verification turned on must also send a current authenticator code or one unused recovery code. A failed sign-in does not say which value was wrong. Every attempt that passes the rate limit is recorded in the audit log, whether it succeeds or fails. If that audit record can't be written, the sign-in fails with audit.unavailable and no usable Session is issued. The request must use Content-Type application/json, optionally with charset=utf-8. A cross-origin browser request or a wrong media type returns request.invalid before the password is checked or any cookie is set. Native clients may omit browser origin headers.
post.summary: Create an interactive session

post.description: Signs out the interactive Session that the current access credential belongs to. If the request used browser cookies, the response clears them. The User's other Sessions stay signed in.
post.summary: Revoke the current session

post.description: Uses up one valid reset token, sets the new password and signs out every Session of the account. The new password must meet the password rules. When the server keeps a password history, it must not match a recent password. A token that has expired, was already used or was replaced by a newer one is rejected without revealing anything about the account. The response also clears any browser authentication cookies.
post.summary: Consume a password-reset credential

post.description: Emails a short-lived password-reset link to the address when it belongs to an active account that has a local password and local sign-in is allowed. The response is the same whether or not such an account exists, so it can't be used to discover accounts.
post.summary: Request a password-reset message

get.description: Lists the external sign-in providers that the current Access Policy allows, sorted by provider ID. Each entry has only what a sign-in page needs to show. Provider secrets, discovery settings and disabled providers are left out. The list can change at any time, so don't cache it as fixed.
get.summary: List external authentication providers selected by current Access Policy

get.description: Checks the provider's callback and uses up the one-time sign-in state. It then creates or updates only the account link that this sign-in was started for, and redirects to the checked return path. A single-factor provider sign-in for a User with active Proctor two-step verification instead sets a separate HttpOnly binding and redirects the browser to the verification page. The original return path is used after the code succeeds.
get.summary: Complete external authentication

get.description: Starts a short-lived sign-in with the chosen provider and redirects the browser to it. Proctor ties the sign-in to a one-time state value so the callback can only finish this attempt. It checks the return path and device details before issuing any redirect.
get.summary: Begin external authentication

post.description: Starts an external sign-in tied to one Invitation claim. The identity that comes back from the provider can then accept only that Invitation, whose contents can't change. The claim is never put in the provider redirect or returned to another account. It works only when the provider requires an Invitation and Invitation sign-up is turned on for it.
post.summary: Begin invitation-bound external authentication

post.description: Starts a new sign-in with the provider that the current Web Session originally used. The callback is accepted only for the same User, external identity, Session and credential. For OIDC, Proctor sends max_age=0 and prompt=login and requires a new auth_time. For CAS, it sets renew on both sign-in and ticket validation. On success, the Session records the time of this new proof, and its original sign-in and two-step verification times stay as they were. The task picks one of a fixed set of hosted pages to return to. That page still asks for the sensitive action as a separate request.
post.summary: Refresh the current Session's original provider proof

post.description: Checks the current User's password again and records the time of this new proof on a Session that was signed in with a password. The Session keeps its ID, credentials and expiry times, and its original sign-in and two-step verification times stay as they were. A Session that was signed in through an external provider must reauthenticate with that provider instead. This call doesn't perform the sensitive action itself: the client sends that as its own request afterwards. The call is rate limited. A successful proof is saved together with its audit record, so neither is kept without the other.
post.summary: Refresh the current Session's password proof

post.description: Replaces the current Session's refresh credential with a new one in a single step and returns a new access and refresh token pair. If the request used the refresh cookie, the new credentials are set as cookies and the body leaves out tokens. A Desktop refresh credential must use the DPoP authorization scheme with a new proof signed by the Desktop's registered key and carrying the server's current nonce. Each refresh credential works once. Sending a used one again is treated as a replay and revokes the Session it belongs to.
post.summary: Rotate refresh credentials

post.description: Creates one local account with an unverified email address, but only when the current Access Policy allows public registration and local sign-in. The first and last names are what the person says they are called. They are shown on the profile and do not prove identity. Registering does not make the account a member of any Institution or grant it any access. Proctor emails a verification link to the address. The response returns no credentials.
post.summary: Register one unverified local account when current policy permits

get.description: Returns whether the current User has a local password, and the name and type of each linked external identity. Password hashes, provider subject IDs, tokens and other credentials are never returned.
get.summary: List the current User's authentication methods without credential material

delete.description: Removes the current User's local password. The interactive Session must have passed two-step verification and must have signed in or reauthenticated recently. If removing it would leave the User no way to sign in, the request is refused and nothing changes. On success, every Session that was signed in with the password is revoked and outstanding password-reset links stop working.
delete.summary: Remove the current User's local password while preserving another usable method

put.description: Adds a local password to the current User. This works only when the Access Policy allows local passwords and the interactive Session has passed two-step verification and has signed in or reauthenticated recently. Proctor stores only a hash of the password and never returns it.
put.summary: Enroll a policy-permitted local password after strong recent authentication

post.description: Replaces the current User's local password. This works only when the Access Policy allows local sign-in and the interactive Session has passed two-step verification and has signed in or reauthenticated recently. The new password must meet the password rules. It must fit the configured length limits and must not be a common password or a simple pattern. It must not contain the username, the part of the email address before the @, or the person's name, and it must not match one of the account's recent passwords. The calling Session stays signed in. Every other Session of the User is revoked, outstanding password-reset links stop working, and the account's email address receives a password-changed notice.
post.summary: Replace the current User's local password after strong recent authentication

delete.description: Unlinks one of the current User's external identities. The interactive Session must have passed two-step verification and must have signed in or reauthenticated recently. If this identity is the User's last way to sign in, the request is refused and nothing changes. On success, every Session that was signed in through this identity is revoked.
delete.summary: Unlink one exact provider identity while preserving another usable method
