parameters.description: The ID of the linked external identity to remove, as listed in providers[].id. It is not the provider's subject ID or any credential.
parameters.name: external_identity_id

post.description: Starts a short-lived connection to an external provider for the current User and returns the address to send the browser to. The interactive Session must have passed two-step verification and must have signed in or reauthenticated recently. When the provider sign-in finishes, the identity can be linked only to this User.
post.summary: Begin a proof-bound provider connection for the exact current User

get.description: Reports whether this installation has been set up yet. The response holds only that flag, so a client can choose between the setup screen and the normal sign-in page without learning anything about the Institution or its administrators.
get.summary: Get installation bootstrap status

post.description: Sets up a new installation in one step. It creates the single Institution, the first administrator, the built-in System Administrator Role and its Role Binding, and the first Access Policy. The bootstrap secret from the operator works only before setup. Once one request succeeds, later or simultaneous requests can't replace the installation.
post.summary: Bootstrap the installation

delete.description: Ends one Class enrollment and keeps its Academic Period history. It does not delete the User, the Class, past participation or audit records, and it never enrolls the student in another Class.
delete.summary: End an enrollment while retaining history

delete.description: Archives one Class, but only when it has no active members or Role Bindings. Past enrollment and audit records are kept. Archiving never ends a membership or Role Binding for you.
delete.summary: Archive a Class with no active members or role bindings

get.description: Returns one active Class. Proctor checks the caller's permission on this Class itself. Being able to list Classes elsewhere is not enough. The response names its Programme Level and Academic Period and does not include its students.
get.summary: Get a Class using exact Class scope authorization

patch.description: Changes some of a Class's fields. It can also move the Class to another Programme Level or Academic Period when the caller is allowed to and the target can take it. The Class's membership history is kept, and Proctor checks again that its members' Academic Period rules still hold.
patch.summary: Update a Class and optionally move its parent references

post.description: Invites a student into the Class in the path, with an account and a Class enrollment, after checking your authority over the Class roster and the start and end. Once issued, the Invitation's terms cannot change. The claim is sent by email and never appears in the response.

requestBody.description: The recipient, an optional enrollment start and end, and a suggested profile for the student account.

201.description: The Invitation was issued. The response contains neither the claim nor mailbox details.

post.summary: Invite a student into one exact Class

get.description:
Lists the student enrollments of one Class that you may see: either those in effect at one instant, or the full history. Each item describes the enrollment only. It never includes the student's credentials, answers or other profile data.
Pages are ordered by `sort` and `dir`, by default by enrollment start (`enrolled`), oldest first, then by ID. The first page also reports `total`, the number of enrollments the filter matches across all pages. It is exact below 10,000; at 10,000 counting stops and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. A cursor keeps the first page's instant or history filter and its order, but every page reads current data, so enrollments added or changed between requests can change later pages.

parameters.description: Return the enrollments in effect at this instant. Defaults to now. It cannot be combined with `history=true`. When following a cursor you may omit it, because the cursor keeps the first page's instant.
parameters.name: active_at

parameters.description: When true, return the full enrollment history instead of only the enrollments in effect at one instant. It cannot be combined with `active_at`.
parameters.name: history

parameters.description: The page order, each key followed by enrollment ID: `enrolled` (the enrollment start, the default) or `name` (the student's display name, or their username when there is none, compared case-insensitively on its first 64 characters). A cursor only continues the sort and direction that produced it, so repeat both when following it.
parameters.name: sort

parameters.description: Ascending (`asc`, the default) or descending (`desc`) by the `sort` key.
parameters.name: dir

get.summary: List active or historical student enrollments for a Class

post.description: Enrolls an existing User in the Class in the path. If the student already has an enrollment in effect in another Class of the same Academic Period, and a transfer or progression is allowed, that enrollment is ended in the same step. Every earlier enrollment keeps its dates.
post.summary: Enroll, transfer, or progress a student transactionally

get.description: Returns the Institution's whole Desktop Compatibility Policy. This server release ships with a fixed list of verified Proctor Desktop builds, and the policy can only narrow that list: it can't allow a build the server doesn't know. It holds no update feed and no download location.
get.summary: Get the Institution Desktop Compatibility Policy

put.description: Replaces the whole policy. Send the `revision` you read as `expected_revision`. If the policy has changed since, the request fails and nothing changes. The request needs a recent, strongly authenticated interactive system administrator Session and an Idempotency-Key, and it fails if the change can't be audited. Revoked build IDs and the administrator message are left out of ordinary audit records.
put.summary: Replace the Institution Desktop Compatibility Policy

x-codeSamples.source:
curl --fail-with-body \
  --request PUT \
  --url 'https://proctor.example.edu/api/v1/desktop-compatibility-policy' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <interactive-system-administrator-session>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Idempotency-Key: docs-desktop-policy-001' \
  --data '{"expected_revision":3,"minimum_desktop_release":"1.4.0","revoked_desktop_build_ids":["desktop-build-2026-08-17"],"administrator_message":"Update Proctor Desktop before your next exam.","availability":"maintenance","retry_at":"2026-08-28T11:00:00Z"}'

get.description: Returns what a client needs to know before anyone signs in: which registration and sign-in paths are open, which providers to offer and which Proctor Desktop protocol versions the server accepts. No sign-in is needed, and the document is served from the installation's own origin with Cache-Control: no-store. It holds only details that are safe to show anyone, and it never stands in for a permission check. Two operator settings appear both before and after the installation is set up: the optional support mailbox that hosted pages offer as a contact, and the minimum length for new passwords.
get.summary: Get safe same-origin access and desktop compatibility discovery

get.description: Lists the environment profiles that are not retired, and with include_retired=true the retired ones too, ordered by name. An environment profile is the recipe an Exam's execution environments are created from: the execution image, resources, network, idle window and the most terminals one Attempt may open. A Session with environment_profile.manage is required; Personal Access Tokens cannot read it.

parameters.description: Whether retired profiles are listed too.
parameters.name: include_retired

get.summary: List the environment profiles

post.description: Saves a new environment profile. Requires a strong recent interactive system-administrator Session, an Idempotency-Key, and durable audit. A profile is never edited: to change one, create a new profile and retire the old. Its name is unique among the profiles that are not retired.

requestBody.description: The complete profile. Every member is required.

post.summary: Create an environment profile

parameters.description: The environment profile to retire.
parameters.name: environment_profile_id

post.description: Retires one environment profile so that new Exam Revisions can no longer name it. Revisions already published keep using it. Retiring a retired profile changes nothing. Requires a strong recent interactive system-administrator Session, an Idempotency-Key, and durable audit.
post.summary: Retire an environment profile

parameters.description: The tool call that waits for the candidate's approval.
parameters.name: call_id

post.description: Answers an exam_attempt_assistant_approval_requested event. When the Exam asks for approvals, each command and each edit waits for the candidate; an unanswered request is declined after five minutes. The answer is recorded once: a second answer, or one after the expiry, fails with exam.attempt.assistant_approval_conflict.

requestBody.description: Accept or decline this pending command or edit.

post.summary: Approve or decline an assistant command or edit

get.description: Downloads the candidate's own sealed assistant transcript and the inventory that verifies it as one JSON attachment. A current candidate Session is required. The download is unavailable before sealing or after retirement.

Content-Disposition.description: Instructs the client to download the JSON document.

get.summary: Download the sealed assistant transcript

post.description: Records the candidate's message and starts the assistant's reply, which streams to the candidate's originating session as exam_attempt_assistant_* events and is recorded in the transcript. The answer is 202 with the turn the message started; a retry with the same Idempotency-Key and text returns the same turn without starting another. One turn runs at a time per Attempt: while one runs the request fails with exam.attempt.assistant_busy. The request also fails when the Exam Revision does not offer the assistant, when the installation has it off, and when the Attempt's allowance of turns or tokens is spent. The assistant acts only while the candidate's own access holds: a seal or the end of the participation ends a running turn, which the transcript records.

example.text: Why does my loop never end?

requestBody.description: The candidate's message, 1 to 16 KiB of text.

202.description: The message was recorded and the reply started

post.summary: Ask the assistant

get.description: Returns the candidate’s live and recently ended assistant sessions after checking process state.
get.summary: List assistant sessions

get.description: Returns the current screen of a running assistant session as text. The caller needs current access to the Attempt.
get.summary: Read an assistant session screen

parameters.description: The process tag allocated by the assistant.
parameters.name: tag

parameters.description: The process tag allocated by the assistant.
parameters.name: tag

post.description: Stops the candidate’s assistant session and returns its recorded outcome, even if its environment is stopped or frozen. Repeating the request returns the same session.
post.summary: Stop an assistant session

get.description: Pages the candidate's own assistant transcript in record order: each message, reply, tool call, approval and output check, as recorded. Realtime deltas are hints; this is what a client keeps, and it reloads from here after a dropped socket. It needs only the candidate's Session, so the transcript stays readable after submission. The inventory covers the whole transcript, and at the seal its digest is bound to the Submission.
get.summary: Read the assistant transcript

parameters.description: The running turn to stop.
parameters.name: turn_id

post.description: Stops the running turn wherever it runs: the model call ends, any assistant command is killed, and the transcript records the turn as canceled. Tokens already spent stay spent.
post.summary: Stop the assistant's turn

get.description: Returns up to 49 browser activity source statuses for one Participation you own, in the order the sources started. The response is at most 1 MiB. You need a Session for the registered key that owns the Participation. If any source is still live, you also need the current Connection headers. Use this to recover sources after a lost response. It gives no access to Browser Activity history.

parameters.description: ID of the Participation you own whose browser activity sources you want.
parameters.name: participation_id

get.summary: List owned Participation Browser sources

get.description: Returns the status of one browser activity source: who owns it, its counters and whether it has been closed. Use it when a start or reset response was lost. You must be the User who owns the source, with a current Session for the registered key. A live source also needs the current Connection headers. Owning a closed source does not let you interact with the Attempt. The response is at most 16 KiB.
get.summary: Recover an owned Browser source

post.description: Uploads stored events for a browser activity source that is already closed. You need the registered key that owns the source, and the events must use the policy revision and digest the source started with. Candidate Connection headers are rejected. Each event keeps its receipt even if it is sent again in a different batch. Receipt progress is reported separately from positions settled by declared gaps. The upload deadline and any declared final position can't change.
post.summary: Upload retained events for a closed Browser source

post.description: Declares sequence numbers of a browser activity source that the client can never deliver. The server always checks that the registered key still owns the source. A live source also needs the current Connection headers. Repeating the same declaration returns the same result. Declared gaps never create event receipts. For a closed source, the request must arrive before the upload deadline, which can't change.
post.summary: Declare permanent missing Browser positions

get.description: Returns up to 64 stored event receipts in ascending sequence order. Missing positions are skipped. next_cursor continues at the next stored receipt and is left out on the last page. The response is at most 16 KiB. The same ownership and live Connection rules apply as for the source status.

parameters.description: Largest number of stored receipts to return on this page.
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: Read bounded per-event Browser receipts

post.description: Declares the last sequence number of a closed browser activity source. The server always checks that the registered key still owns the source. Repeating the same declaration returns the same result. The request must arrive before the upload deadline, which can't change.
post.summary: Declare a closed Browser source final boundary

post.description: Reports how many browser activity events the client produced but could not deliver. The server always checks that the registered key still owns the source. A live source also needs the current Connection headers. Repeating the same summary returns the same result. For a closed source, the request must arrive before the upload deadline, which can't change.
post.summary: Update cumulative unretained Browser delivery counts

put.description: Records that the candidate has read the oldest correction still waiting for acknowledgement. The server first checks the current Revision, the active Participation and its generation, the registered desktop Session, the Attempt credential and the open Attempt connection. Repeating the request with the same Idempotency-Key returns the saved acknowledgement and changes nothing else.
put.summary: Acknowledge one required live correction for an active Attempt

get.description: Returns the delivery usage of one Participation you own, together with the lifetime counters of the Attempt across every Participation Generation. The response is at most 8 KiB. You need a current Session for the registered key that owns the Participation. Retiring records or deleting the client's local spool never gives quota back. The snapshot doesn't allow interaction or raise any limit.

parameters.description: ID of the Participation you own whose delivery limits you want.
parameters.name: participation_id

get.summary: Read current delivery limits

post.description: Stops detailed delivery for one family, native or browser, for the current Participation, because the client has run out of room to track lost records. You need the live registered Desktop Connection and an Idempotency-Key. The stop can't be undone. It fixes the reserved positions where they are and marks the rest as permanently missing, without making up receipts. The response holds the current budget and the affected statuses: at most one native stream or 49 browser sources, within 1 MiB. A retry with the same key checks live authority again and never affects a later Participation Generation. No quota is given back. This request alone never creates an Integrity Flag, a Suspension or a block on interaction.
post.summary: Stop detailed delivery for a Participation

get.description: Returns what the Attempt's execution environment does and the sync status of its files in both directions. A Workspace entry whose last journal change is past projection_cursor is not in the machine yet, which a client can mark as not yet synced. A guest change waits about a second at most before it is saved; paths lists the guest paths the environment did not save, each ignored (by the Workspace's .proctorignore, the default patterns, or a parent directory that is not saved) or refused with the Workspace's reason, such as a quota or a conflict the Workspace won. Every other guest path is synced. The list keeps the latest status of at most 256 paths, the newest last, and a path leaves it once a later change to it is saved or the guest removes it.
get.summary: Read the Attempt's execution environment

get.description: Lists TCP listeners bound to loopback or a wildcard address in the candidate's running Attempt environment. Each entry shows whether the published Exam policy permits opening a preview.

200.description: Listening ports reported by the execution host

get.summary: List the listening ports in the Attempt environment

get.description:
Upgrades to a binary WebSocket carrying one TCP connection to a guest listener. Proctor checks live
candidate access and the frozen policy and dials the guest before it upgrades. Each connection goes
to the execution host from the node handling the request.

The first byte of each binary message is its type. Clients send `0x01` followed by 1 to 32,768 bytes
of data, or `0x02` with no payload to close their write side. The server sends `0x81` followed by
up to 32,768 bytes, `0x82` with no payload for EOF from the guest, or `0x86` followed by a public
UTF-8 error code. Each direction can close independently. When the guest resets a connection,
Proctor sends `exam.attempt.preview_connection_ended` and closes that WebSocket normally.

Proctor rechecks access every 15 seconds. Close code 4003 indicates lost access, a freeze or a seal.
A connection closes after 10 minutes without bytes in either direction. The local limit is 32
connections per Attempt. Candidate content travels only in binary frames.

101.description: Switching Protocols to the preview socket

get.summary: Upgrade to a preview port socket

get.description: Lists the candidate's terminals on the Attempt's current machine, running or exited, in number order, with where each one's output and input stand. A client reconnecting after a restart reads it to reattach. A new machine, after the old one was lost or replaced, starts with no terminals.
get.summary: List the terminals in the Attempt's execution environment

post.description: Starts a terminal running the image's login shell on the Attempt's current machine and answers with its number and tag. Terminals are numbered in the order the machine opened them, terminal:1, terminal:2 and so on, and a number is never reused on that machine. At most the Exam's number of terminals run at once; past it the request fails with exam.attempt.terminal_limit_reached. The environment must be running: while it starts, waits for capacity or is frozen the request fails with exam.attempt.environment_not_running. A request whose response was lost may have opened a terminal, so a client lists the terminals before opening another. Every command a terminal runs is in the Attempt's command log, and when the Exam records terminal input the input is kept too; output never is.
post.summary: Open a terminal in the Attempt's execution environment

post.description: Sends the terminal an interrupt, as Ctrl+C does in a terminal that reads its keys. A candidate may only interrupt; the server ends terminals itself when the machine ends. An exited terminal fails with exam.attempt.terminal_exited, and a number the current machine never opened with exam.attempt.terminal_not_found.
post.summary: Interrupt what a terminal runs

get.description:
Upgrades to a binary WebSocket attached to one terminal. Any Proctor node serves it by reaching the execution machine itself, so a reconnect may land on another node and resume exactly. The terminal is attached before the upgrade: a refusal answers as a problem.

Every message is one binary frame whose first byte is its type; integers are big-endian. The client's first message is ATTACH or SCREEN.

Client frames:
- `0x01` ATTACH `offset:u64`: stream output from offset. A reconnecting client sends the output offset it holds, and output still in the terminal's history is replayed, so full-screen programs come back intact.
- `0x02` SCREEN: answer with the screen. As the first message, also stream output from the screen's offset; a client with no screen of its own draws it, then continues.
- `0x03` INPUT `offset:u64` `data` (1 to 16,384 bytes): input written at offset. Bytes the terminal already took are dropped, so after a lost connection the client resends everything after the last INPUT offset it saw, and nothing types twice.
- `0x04` RESIZE `cols:u16` `rows:u16`: the terminal's new window, 1 to 1,000 each way.

Server frames:
- `0x81` OUTPUT `offset:u64` `data`: output bytes at offset, at most 32 KiB.
- `0x82` TRUNCATED `from:u64` `to:u64`: output from to to that the history no longer holds.
- `0x83` EXIT `code:i32` `signal:i32`: the terminal exited; the socket then closes normally.
- `0x84` INPUT `offset:u64`: the terminal's input offset after an INPUT, accepted or not.
- `0x85` SCREEN `offset:u64` `cols:u16` `rows:u16` `cursor_row:u16` `cursor_col:u16` `flags:u8` `data`: the screen as of offset; flag bit 0 is the alternate screen, bit 1 a hidden cursor, and data redraws it on a blank terminal of that size.
- `0x86` ERROR `code`: a refused frame, by its public error code in UTF-8, such as exam.attempt.invalid for input past the terminal's input offset; the socket stays open.

Several sockets may read one terminal, such as the candidate's two windows; they share one input offset. The socket closes normally after EXIT or a malformed frame, with 4003 once the Attempt is sealed, its Participation ends, or its machine ends or is replaced, and with 1011 on a server failure. Access is checked again every 15 seconds while the socket is open. Terminal bytes never travel between Proctor nodes, and output is never recorded.

101.description: Switching Protocols to the terminal socket

get.summary: Upgrade to a terminal's binary socket

get.description: Returns what the active candidate Attempt may see: the Exam title, the Markdown instructions, the capacity limits that apply, and the ordered list of Exam Resources. The server checks the Attempt credential bound to the Session and the open Connection again. The response contains no answers and nothing meant only for Exam Managers. Capacity limits come from the Exam Revision the Attempt was admitted with. They don't change when Institution policy changes or a live correction is published. Instructions and resources follow the current Exam Revision of the Sitting.
get.summary: Get the protected current presentation for one candidate Attempt

get.description: Sends one current Exam Resource inline to the candidate. The request needs the active Attempt credential bound to the Session and an open Connection. This is not a public or export URL.

parameters.description: One or more entity tags from an earlier protected-content response. A match returns 304 without a body.
parameters.name: If-None-Match

get.summary: Render a current protected Exam resource inline

get.description: Returns the candidate's result once a manager has finalized the review and released it. Until then the result is not available. The result never includes private notes, manager reasons, integrity evidence, decisions or unreleased grading data.
get.summary: Get only the explicitly released candidate result projection

get.description: Lists, newest first, the screen clip requests waiting for the candidate's Desktop, after validating the Session-bound Attempt credential and open Connection. Requests queued while the Attempt was suspended appear once the candidate resumes. Each item carries the range to cut; never who asked or why.
get.summary: List the screen clip requests the candidate's Desktop has not taken

post.description: Records that the candidate's Desktop took a request and is recording what remains of its range. The request then belongs to the Participation that took it. Taking it again through the same Participation returns it unchanged.
post.summary: Take one screen clip request

get.description: Returns the clip and the numbers of the chunks that arrived, so Desktop resumes an interrupted upload with the rest.
get.summary: Read where a screen clip upload stands

post.description: Declares a taken clip's media type, exact size and the SHA-256 of every chunk in order. Every chunk is chunk_bytes long except the last, which holds the rest. The clip's content digest is the SHA-256 of that manifest. A clip that would take the Attempt's clips past 6 GiB is refused. Declaring the same clip again returns it unchanged. Once the Participation that took the clip has closed, as at submission, Desktop continues the upload without the Attempt credential and Connection headers until that Participation's upload deadline; a clip not complete by then fails with upload_deadline.
post.summary: Declare the screen clip about to be uploaded

parameters.description: The chunk's number, from 1.
parameters.name: chunk

put.description: Streams one chunk as the raw request body, with its exact Content-Length. The bytes are checked against the hash the clip declared for that chunk and kept only if they match. Sending a stored chunk again changes nothing, so a chunk whose response was lost can be sent again.

requestBody.description: The chunk's raw bytes, exactly the size the declared upload gives that chunk: 8 MiB (8388608 bytes) for every chunk but the last.

put.summary: Upload one chunk of a screen clip

post.description: Makes a clip whose every chunk arrived ready to play. The body carries the clip's content digest and the installation key's ES256 signature over the exact bytes of that digest (its 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters), raw r and s in unpadded base64url. The signature must verify with the key of the Desktop registration uploading the clip; it is stored with the clip so a reviewer can check the clip later from the clip and its record alone. Completing it again returns it unchanged.
post.summary: Finish a screen clip upload

post.description: Atomically accepts one closed batch under its original verified release, matrix, policy, source instances, and Participation generation. Live delivery requires exact Connection continuity; closed streams use current owning registered-key authentication until the fixed upload deadline. Exact retries preserve the submitted prior acknowledgement and recover the original receipt. Out-of-order records wait behind recoverable holes; terminal gaps preserve unresolved openers. The server evaluates the policy's rules on the facts in stream order; an enforce rule that stops being met raises its native Flag and, for a flag_and_suspend family, suspends the Attempt. Observe rules, unknown status and gaps never flag. Lifetime quotas include pending bytes, envelopes, receipts and bounded metadata. Repair has reserved headroom. Native append is limited across Sessions and transports to two requests per second with burst eight; replay consumes allowance. A 429 response supplies Retry-After.
post.summary: Append minimized native security evidence

get.description: Returns the exact active Participation binding and original frozen configuration to its owning registered Desktop Session after transport ambiguity. Checks current Session, key, compatibility, eligibility and lease. An open transport Connection is not required. Ready reentry uses a fresh preflight. This read creates no authority and never renews the lease.
get.summary: Recover the active Desktop security receipt

get.description: Requires the owning User and a currently valid Session for the registered key bound at admission. Live sources also require exact Connection continuity. After server-owned closure, historical delivery never revives interaction or extends the upload deadline. Exact replay rechecks ownership. Receipts attest only stored batches; terminal omissions advance settlement without fabricating content. Source status is bounded at 16 KiB.
get.summary: Read native delivery settlement

post.description: Requires the owning User and a currently valid Session for the registered key bound at admission. Live sources also require exact Connection continuity. After server-owned closure, historical delivery never revives interaction or extends the upload deadline. Exact replay rechecks ownership. Receipts attest only stored batches; terminal omissions advance settlement without fabricating content. At most 8 KiB, 1..32 disjoint nonadjacent ranges within the current 1024-position receive window. Declaration revision and exact canonical metadata charge commit atomically.
post.summary: Declare permanently unavailable native batches

get.description: Requires the owning User and a currently valid Session for the registered key bound at admission. Live sources also require exact Connection continuity. After server-owned closure, historical delivery never revives interaction or extends the upload deadline. Exact replay rechecks ownership. Receipts attest only stored batches; terminal omissions advance settlement without fabricating content. Source status is bounded at 16 KiB.
get.summary: Recover an exact native batch receipt

post.description: Requires the owning User and a currently valid Session for the registered key bound at admission. Live sources also require exact Connection continuity. After server-owned closure, historical delivery never revives interaction or extends the upload deadline. Exact replay rechecks ownership. Receipts attest only stored batches; terminal omissions advance settlement without fabricating content. At most 2 KiB. Only after closure. The final tail is bounded by known-at-close plus 1024 and remaining lifetime positions.
post.summary: Declare the final boundary of a closed native stream

post.description: Requires the owning User and a currently valid Session for the registered key bound at admission. Live sources also require exact Connection continuity. After server-owned closure, historical delivery never revives interaction or extends the upload deadline. Exact replay rechecks ownership. Receipts attest only stored batches; terminal omissions advance settlement without fabricating content. At most 2 KiB. Changed summaries at most once per five seconds except the one final summary; incomplete counts never become complete.
post.summary: Report cumulative unretained native records

post.description: Submits an active Attempt. In one step the server seals the Workspace as the client last saw it acknowledged and records the final integrity position. It checks the Session's Attempt credential and connection, and that the candidate is still in the Class. Repeating the request with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same 201 receipt without repeating realtime notifications or other side effects.
post.summary: Seal one active Exam Attempt and return a candidate-safe receipt

get.description: Lists one page of the files and directories in the candidate's active Attempt Workspace. The request needs the Attempt credential bound to the Session and an open Connection. Every page is tied to the Workspace Cursor of the first page. If the Workspace changes while you page through it, the response tells you to start again from the first page.

parameters.description: Largest number of Workspace entries to return on this page.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Cursor from next_cursor of the previous page. Send it back unchanged. Don't build or parse it yourself.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List one protected candidate Workspace page

post.description: The one way the candidate's Attempt Workspace changes. A batch holds 1 to 128 mutations, applied in order and all or nothing: create a file or directory, replace a file, move or rename an entry, or delete one. Each mutation keeps its own fence, so unrelated entries commute; a recursive directory delete also fences the batch on expected_workspace_cursor. The body is multipart: a strict JSON manifest first, then one content part for each create_file and replace_file mutation, in manifest order. Access is checked once for the whole batch against the Session-bound Attempt credential, open Connection and active Participation generation. When one mutation refuses the batch, nothing changes and the problem's item field names it by its position. One audit record and one realtime hint cover the whole batch. Each Attempt may change its Workspace only so fast, by mutations and by bytes, whoever writes; a faster writer gets 429 with Retry-After and nothing is staged.

requestBody.description: A strict JSON manifest part first, then exactly one content part per create_file and replace_file mutation, in manifest order, and no other part. The manifest and every body together are bounded by the hard API limit; each file is also bounded by the admitted Revision. The Attempt credential and Connection remain headers, never form fields.

200.description: Every mutation of the batch was acknowledged

post.summary: Apply one atomic batch of Workspace changes

get.description: Returns the Workspace changes the server accepted after workspace_cursor, in order, for the candidate's active Attempt. If the server no longer keeps enough history to continue from that cursor, the response tells the client to reload the full file list instead.

parameters.description: List only changes made after this Workspace Cursor. Zero, or leaving it out, starts at the oldest change the server still keeps. Leave it out when you continue a listing with cursor.
parameters.name: workspace_cursor

get.summary: List ordered acknowledged Workspace changes

get.description: Streams one file from the active Workspace. Before it sends anything, the server checks the Session, the Attempt credential, the open Connection, the current Participation, and that the Attempt can still be read. The response never reveals where the file is stored. Responses are private and not cached (no-store), use nosniff, carry an ETag, and return 304 when the content has not changed.

parameters.description: One or more entity tags from an earlier protected-content response. A match returns 304 without a body.
parameters.name: If-None-Match

get.summary: Render a protected candidate Workspace file inline

get.description: Resolves the Sitting's current native policy, under the same eligibility checks as preparing a preflight, for the overview a candidate's Desktop shows before Start: the capabilities it activates, the rules it checks, the recorder switch and the disclosure. It creates no preflight, records nothing and grants nothing, so the overview may hold it for as long as it is open. At Start, compare readiness_digest with the one the prepared preflight returns; if they differ, refresh the overview.

200.description: The policy the readiness overview checks the machine against

get.summary: Read the policy for the readiness overview

post.description: Requires an eligible registered Desktop Session and an exact admitted build, capability registry and configuration manifest. Stores one pending 120-second challenge per Session and Sitting; a successor supersedes it. Does not create an Attempt, Workspace or Participation. Ready rejoin returns frozen configuration; active and suspended Attempts cannot obtain a replacement preflight. Unavailable Institution catalogs, or a family enforced where the release does not certify enforcement on the candidate's platform, fail closed.
post.summary: Prepare a secure Desktop admission challenge

get.description: Returns one row for each Exam you can see, most recently updated first. When you filter by Sitting state or schedule, an Exam is included only if at least one of its Sittings matches every Sitting filter you gave. To get the next page, send next_cursor back unchanged. A cursor does not give access to anything you could not already see.

parameters.description: Return only Exams owned by this Academic Unit. You still see only the Exams you are allowed to see.
parameters.name: academic_unit_id

parameters.description: Return only Exams whose current Draft title contains this text. Matching ignores case, and wildcard characters are treated as plain text.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Return active Exams, archived Exams, or all of them. Defaults to active.
parameters.name: archive_state

parameters.description: Return only Exams with a Sitting in one of these states. Repeat the parameter for several states. With ends_after and starts_before, the same Sitting must also fall in that time range.
parameters.name: sitting_state

parameters.description: Return only Exams with a Sitting scheduled to end after this time. Send it together with starts_before.
parameters.name: ends_after

parameters.description: Return only Exams with a Sitting scheduled to start before this time. Send it together with ends_after, and make it later than ends_after.
parameters.name: starts_before

parameters.description: The most Exams to return in one page, from 1 to 200. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The next_cursor value from the previous page, sent back unchanged. Omit it for the first page. Don't parse it or store it as an ID.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List Exams visible to the current principal

post.description: Creates an Exam in the Academic Unit you choose, together with its first Draft. You become its creator, owner and first Manager. You need permission to author Exams in that Academic Unit. Send an Idempotency-Key. Retrying with the same key and body returns the original result. Reusing the key with a different body is rejected as a conflict.
post.summary: Create an Exam and its initial Draft

x-codeSamples.source:
curl --fail-with-body \
  --request POST \
  --url 'https://proctor.example.edu/api/v1/exams' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <access-token>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Idempotency-Key: docs-exam-001' \
  --data '{"academic_unit_id":"q4nzk1xwe7rbdg3cyjoth5mupa","title":"Algorithms — final examination","instructions_markdown":"Read every question before you begin."}'

get.description: Returns the Exam, its current Draft, its owner and how many Managers it has. You must currently be allowed to manage the Exam. Published Revisions can't change, and you read them through the Revision operations.
get.summary: Get one bounded Exam authoring view

post.description: Archives an active Exam. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Exam's current revision, so a Manager working from an old copy can't hide newer work. Archiving keeps the Draft, published Revisions, Manager history, Sittings, Attempts and audit history.
post.summary: Archive an active Exam

patch.description: Changes the Draft title, its Markdown instructions, or both. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision, so you never overwrite someone else's newer edit. A field you leave out or send as null stays as it is. Proctor stores the Markdown exactly as you wrote it and renders it safely when it is shown.
patch.summary: Edit authored title or Markdown instructions on the active Exam Draft

put.description: Replace the assistant policy behind the Draft revision fence. The profile must be active and permit the requested level and budgets. Publication checks installation availability.

requestBody.description: The complete replacement assistant policy.

put.summary: Configure the Draft assistant

put.description: Replaces the whole Browser Policy on the Draft. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision. A disabled policy has no rules. An enabled policy lists the sites candidates may open, and Proctor matches pages against them by host and path in a fixed order.
put.summary: Replace the Browser Policy on the active Exam Draft

put.description: Replaces the execution policy on the mutable Draft at the expected revision: whether Attempts get an execution environment, the environment profile they are created from, whether terminal input is recorded, how many terminals a candidate may open, and which ports a candidate may preview. An enabled policy must name a profile that exists, is not retired and allows that many terminals, or the change fails with exam.execution.profile_unusable. A disabled policy names no profile, records nothing and opens no terminal. Publication checks the profile again and requires the installation to allow execution.

requestBody.description: Supplies the expected Draft revision and the complete replacement execution policy.

put.summary: Replace the execution policy on the active Exam Draft

put.description: Replaces the whole Focus Loss rule on the Draft. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision. The minimum duration, incident count, window and outcome are checked together, so every published Revision carries a rule that makes sense as a whole.
put.summary: Replace the Focus Loss policy on the active Exam Draft

put.description: Replaces the complete ten-family native policy at the expected Draft revision. The mandatory desktop_candidate baseline cannot be disabled. Publication freezes these selections; live Participation native selections cannot be changed by a Draft edit. Catalog IDs must refer to server-admitted catalogs when resolved for admission.
put.summary: Replace native security selections on the active Exam Draft

get.description: Returns every Resource on the Draft, in order, with its name, description, content revision, media type, size and SHA-256 digest. It does not return the file content. Read the content through the separate content operation, which checks your access again.
get.summary: List the ordered protected resources in an Exam Draft

post.description: Adds one Resource to the end of the Draft's Resource list. The upload is accepted only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision, the metadata is valid, the content matches the size and digest you declared, the media type is allowed, and the Draft has room under its Resource limits. Send the metadata part first, then the content. The Resource and its content are saved together, or not at all. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retry can't add the Resource twice.

requestBody.description: A metadata part followed by a content part. The size and SHA-256 digest in the metadata must match the uploaded bytes.

post.summary: Upload and append a protected resource to an Exam Draft

x-codeSamples.label: Append a protected PDF resource
x-codeSamples.source:
curl --request POST \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $PROCTOR_TOKEN" \
  --header "Idempotency-Key: exam-resource-create-001" \
  --form 'metadata={"expected_revision":3,"display_name":"Formula sheet","description_markdown":"Reference formulas for this examination.","media_type":"application/pdf","size":2048,"sha256":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"};type=application/json' \
  --form 'content=@./formula-sheet.pdf;type=application/octet-stream' \
  https://proctor.example.edu/api/v1/exams/ybndrfg8ejkmcpqxot1uwisza3/draft/resources

put.description: Sets a new order for all of the Draft's Resources. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision. List every current Resource ID exactly once. If the list is out of date or incomplete, the request fails and no Resource moves.
put.summary: Replace the complete order of active Exam Draft resources

delete.description: Removes one Resource from the Draft. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision. The Resources after it move up to fill the gap in the same step. Revisions you already published keep their copy of the Resource.
delete.summary: Remove one resource from the active Exam Draft

patch.description: Changes the display name, the Markdown description, or both, for one Resource on the Draft. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision. The content, its digest and the Resource's position stay the same. A field you leave out stays as it is.
patch.summary: Edit one Exam Draft resource's authored metadata

get.description: Returns the Resource's content for display inside the application, after checking your access. It is not a public link and not a download or export, and it never reveals where the file is stored.

parameters.description: The ETag from an earlier response for this content. If it still matches, the server returns 304 with no body.
parameters.name: If-None-Match

get.summary: Render protected Exam resource content inline

put.description: Replaces the content of one Resource. The upload is accepted only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision, and the media type, size and digest you declared match the upload. Send the metadata part first, then the content. The display name, description and position stay the same, and the Resource gets a new content revision. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retry is safe.

requestBody.description: A metadata part followed by a content part. The media type, size and SHA-256 digest in the metadata must match the uploaded bytes.

put.summary: Replace an Exam Draft resource's protected content

get.description: Returns every file and directory in the Draft's Starter Workspace, sorted by path. When the Draft is published, these entries become the starting files of each candidate's Workspace. Files include their content version, size and digest. Read the content through the separate content operation.
get.summary: List the complete Starter Workspace manifest for an Exam Draft

post.description: Creates one empty directory at the path you give. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision. The parent directory must exist, nothing may already use the path, and the Starter Workspace must have room for another entry.
post.summary: Create an empty directory in an Exam Draft Starter Workspace

delete.description: Removes one file or directory from the Starter Workspace. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision. To remove a directory that isn't empty, set recursive to true. The directory and everything in it are then removed in one step, and the Draft revision goes up by one. Revisions you already published keep their copy of the Starter Workspace.
delete.summary: Remove a Starter Workspace entry or guarded directory subtree

patch.description: Renames or moves one file or directory to a new path in a single step. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision. The request fails, and nothing changes, if the new parent doesn't exist, the path is taken, a directory would move inside itself, or the path is the same as before.
patch.summary: Rename or move one Starter Workspace entry by logical path

post.description: Adds one file at the path you give. Send the metadata part first, then the content. The upload is accepted only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision, the parent directory exists, the content matches the digest and any size you declared, and the Starter Workspace stays within its limits. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retry can't add the file twice.

requestBody.description: A metadata part followed by a content part. The path, size and SHA-256 digest are checked before the file is saved.

post.summary: Upload a file into an Exam Draft Starter Workspace

get.description: Returns the file's content for display inside the application, after checking your access. It is not a public link and not a download or export, and it never reveals where the file is stored. Content that a browser would run as an active page is served as plain text.

parameters.description: The ETag from an earlier response for this file. If it still matches, the server returns 304 with no body.
parameters.name: If-None-Match

get.summary: Render protected Starter Workspace file content inline

put.description: Replaces the content of one file. The upload is accepted only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision and expected_content_version still matches the file's current content version. Send the metadata part first, then the content. The entry must be a file, and the content must match its digest and fit the size limits. The file then gets a new content version.

requestBody.description: A metadata part followed by a content part. expected_content_version stops you from overwriting someone else's newer upload.

put.summary: Replace one Starter Workspace file's content

get.description: Lists the Users who currently manage the Exam, newest first. Each entry shows who made that User a Manager and whether they are the creator or the current owner. The response contains no User profile or credential data.

parameters.description: The most Managers to return in one page, from 1 to 200. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The next_cursor value from the previous page, sent back unchanged. Omit it for the first page.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List bounded Exam Manager relationship provenance

post.description: Makes an eligible User a Manager of the Exam, with the same management rights as the other Managers. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Exam's current revision. Proctor records who added the Manager and when. Adding a Manager never changes the owner, and belonging to the Academic Unit alone never makes someone a Manager.
post.summary: Grant an eligible User equal Exam management responsibility

delete.description: Removes one User as a Manager of the Exam. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Exam's current revision. The record of who added them, and the audit history, are kept. You can't remove the current owner. Transfer ownership to someone else first.
delete.summary: Revoke an Exam Manager relationship while preserving provenance

put.description: Makes an existing, eligible Manager the owner of the Exam. The change is made only if expected_revision still matches the Exam's current revision. The previous owner stays a Manager, and the creator does not change. Ownership changes only through this audited operation, never because of someone's membership alone.
put.summary: Transfer Exam ownership to an eligible current Manager

get.description: Needs a Session and `exam.records.hold`, held through current Exam Manager status and membership of the exact Academic Unit, or through its scoped override. Lists holds on the requested scope or below it, together with the higher-level holds that cover it. Holds never expire on their own. The retired counts recorded when each hold was created show content the hold can't bring back. The cursor is tied to the requested scope.

parameters.description: Return only holds for this Sitting. Exam holds that cover it are included.
parameters.name: exam_sitting_id

parameters.description: Return only holds for this Submission. Needs `exam_sitting_id`. Holds on the Sitting and Exam that cover it are included.
parameters.name: submission_id

parameters.description: Set to `true` to include released holds. Only `true` and `false` are accepted.
parameters.name: include_released

parameters.description: Maximum number of holds to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` value from the previous page, sent with the same scope and `include_released`. Pass it unchanged and don't try to read it.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List preservation holds

post.description: Needs a Session and `exam.records.hold`, held through current Exam Manager status and membership of the exact Academic Unit, or through its scoped override. A hold on an Exam, Sitting or Submission covers its current content and anything added to that scope later, until someone releases it. It stops pending retirement but can't bring back content that was already retired. A hold on a single Submission that is fully retired is rejected. Broader holds still protect whatever remains below them. The retired counts recorded at creation show any partial retirement. The hold, its critical audit record and the retry result are saved together after authority is checked again.
post.summary: Preserve examination records

post.description: Needs `retention_hold.release` on a protected system-administrator Session with a strong, recent sign-in. The release is audited and idempotent. Authority and the sign-in proof are checked again inside the transaction and on replay. The private release reason isn't written to the ordinary audit log. Releasing a hold doesn't restore data already retired, and records must still become eligible and pass a new grace period before cleanup.
post.summary: Release a preservation hold

get.description: Lists the Exam's published Revisions, newest first. Each entry includes digests of the policy and content, the capacity limits, Resource and Starter Workspace counts, and who published it and when. It does not return Resource content or the current Draft.

parameters.description: The most Revisions to return in one page, from 1 to 200. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The next_cursor value from the previous page, sent back unchanged. Omit it for the first page.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List bounded immutable Exam Revision metadata

post.description: Checks the whole current Draft and publishes it as a new Revision, which can't change afterwards. Publishing happens only if expected_revision still matches the Draft's current revision, so you never publish edits you haven't seen. Send an Idempotency-Key: if the response is lost, retrying with the same key returns the same result. The Revision captures the text, policies, capacity limits, Resources and Starter Workspace together.
post.summary: Publish the complete validated Draft as an immutable Exam Revision

get.description: Returns one published Revision. It checks that the Revision belongs to this Exam and that you can currently manage the Exam. The response holds publication details and digests, not the current Draft or any file content.
get.summary: Get bounded immutable Exam Revision metadata

get.description: Lists the Sittings of one Exam, latest scheduled start first. You can filter by Class, by state, and by a time window the Sitting overlaps. The response never includes candidate credentials, private reasons, answers or integrity evidence.

parameters.description: Return only Sittings for this Class.
parameters.name: class_id

parameters.description: Return only Sittings in these states. Repeat the parameter to match several states; duplicates are ignored.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description: Return only Sittings that end after this time. Send it together with `starts_before`, and make it earlier than `starts_before`.
parameters.name: ends_after

parameters.description: Return only Sittings that start before this time. Send it together with `ends_after`. The two together select Sittings that overlap the window.
parameters.name: starts_before

parameters.description: Maximum number of Sittings to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged and do not parse or build it yourself.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List bounded Exam Sittings ordered by scheduled start and identity descending

post.description: Schedules a published Exam Revision for one Class, within the Class's Academic Period. Before saving, the server checks that the Revision belongs to this Exam, that the Class is eligible, and that the window is in the future.
post.summary: Schedule one immutable Exam Revision for one Class

get.description: Returns one Sitting of the Exam, including its lifecycle times and current revision. Private manager reasons and candidate details are not included.
get.summary: Get one bounded Exam Sitting

patch.description: Changes the Exam Revision, Class or schedule of a Sitting that has not opened yet. Send the Sitting's current revision; the request fails if the Sitting changed since you read it. After the Sitting opens, these values can't change here. Use live corrections or the lifecycle operations (pause, resume, extend, close) instead.
patch.summary: Change the pre-open Exam Revision, Class, or schedule

get.description: Lists the Attempts of one Exam Sitting, after checking again that the caller may manage it. You can filter by Attempt state. Rows contain no candidate credentials, answers, private Integrity Evidence or internal lease data.

parameters.description: Return only Attempts in these states. Repeat the parameter for each state, at most three, without duplicates.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description: Largest number of Attempts to return on this page.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Cursor from next_cursor of the previous page. Send it back unchanged. Attempts are listed newest first.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List bounded candidate Attempts for one Exam Sitting

get.description: Returns one Attempt, after checking that it belongs to the Exam and Sitting in the path and that the caller may manage it. The response shows the Attempt's operational state. It contains no candidate credentials, answers or private evidence.
get.summary: Get one manager-safe Exam Attempt projection

get.description: Returns one page of top-level browser navigation records for an Attempt, with only the details the review needs. The server checks that the caller is currently an Exam Manager of this Exam and holds the separate Browser Activity view permission, and it checks again on every page. Administrator, teacher, integrity review and general export permissions don't replace it. Responses are not cached. They contain no Session, Connection, Desktop Registration, credentials, page content or private Submission Review state.

parameters.description: Largest number of browser activity records to return on this page.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Cursor from next_cursor of the previous page. Send it back unchanged. Don't try to read browser locations from it.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List privacy-minimized Browser Activity for one managed Attempt

post.description: Ends one active, ready or suspended Attempt on behalf of the candidate. The candidate's last acknowledged Workspace state is sealed as a Submission in the same step. Your reason is kept for audit and is never shown to the candidate. Once the Sitting deadline is reached, scheduled closure seals the Attempt instead.
post.summary: End and seal one unfinished Exam Attempt

post.description: An Exam Manager's repair for an execution environment that misbehaves. Names the incarnation the manager saw on the candidate-status board; the environment's owner then replaces that machine with a new incarnation built from the Attempt Workspace and records the restart as an execution.gap. Nothing the candidate saved is lost; processes, terminals and ignored files that only the old machine held are. Repeating the request for the same incarnation changes nothing; a newer incarnation fails with exam.attempt.environment_changed and an ended environment with exam.attempt.environment_ended. Like a kick, it is refused once the Sitting is closing.
post.summary: Replace a candidate's execution environment with a new machine

post.description: Ends the given active Suspension and returns the Attempt to Ready. Integrity Evidence is kept. No continuity credential, Participation, Session binding or Connection is created, so the candidate must enter again and pass every admission check.
post.summary: Re-allow one exact suspended Exam Attempt

get.description: Lists, newest first, every clip requested for the Attempt, manager and incident alike, with its state: requested, recording the future part of its range, uploading, ready or failed. Managers' reasons are never returned.
get.summary: List an Attempt's screen clips

post.description: An Exam Manager's request for part of the screen Desktop records on the candidate's device, for an Exam whose native policy turns the screen recorder on. The range is either from the start of the session or an explicit start and end of at most six hours; it may end up to ten minutes after the request, and Desktop waits for that part before cutting the clip. A request made while the Attempt is suspended waits until the candidate resumes. The manager's reason is required, audited as an attempt, and stored with the request; it is never returned. An Attempt takes at most ten manager requests. Requests stop once the Attempt has ended.
post.summary: Request a range of a candidate's recorded screen

get.description: Streams a ready clip to one of the Sitting's Exam Managers, or once the Attempt is submitted to someone allowed to review its Submission, whole or by one byte range so a player can seek. Each playback, a request from the clip's first byte, is audited. Multiple ranges, or a range past the clip's end, are refused.

parameters.description: One byte range, such as bytes=0-1048575, bytes=1048576- or bytes=-4096.
parameters.name: Range

get.summary: Play a ready screen clip

get.description: Returns the summary of one sealed Submission: what was sealed, its size, and the state of its integrity data. You must currently manage the Exam. If the Submission does not belong to the Exam, Sitting and Attempt in the path, the request fails as not found.
get.summary: Get one protected immutable Submission header

get.description: Returns the exact bytes of one sealed file, whether it came from the Starter Workspace or was written during the Attempt. The bytes are served by Proctor itself. This is not a public link or an export, and it reveals no storage location.

parameters.description: The `ETag` from an earlier response for this file. If it still matches, the server returns 304 with no body.
parameters.name: If-None-Match

get.summary: Render one protected immutable Submission file inline

get.description: Lists the files and directories sealed in one Submission, one page at a time. The page cursor never contains a file path or storage location.

parameters.description: Maximum number of manifest entries to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged and do not parse or build it yourself.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List one protected immutable Submission manifest page

post.description: Lets an Exam Manager suspend an Attempt at once. It ends the active Participation Generation as kicked, closes its open Connection and opens one manual Suspension, with no Integrity Flag. While suspended, the Attempt refuses connections, Workspace and Exam material access, and Submission until someone allowed to re-allows it. The candidate sees only the reason manager_suspended. The manager's private reason is kept only in the Suspension record. Database time decides the outcome. Once the Sitting's scheduled end has passed, the request fails with exam.attempt.sitting_not_open. If the Participation Lease had already run out, the server records that Connection Loss (Integrity Flag, evidence and policy Suspension) and fails with exam.attempt.connection_lost instead.
post.summary: Suspend (kick) one exact active Exam Attempt

post.description: Cancels a Sitting that has not opened yet. Send the Sitting's current revision; the request fails if it changed since you read it. Your private reason is kept for audit. Canceling never creates Attempts or Submissions, and a Sitting that has already opened can't be canceled.
post.summary: Cancel a Scheduled Exam Sitting with a private manager reason

get.description: Returns one row for each candidate of the Sitting, after checking that the caller currently holds exam.sitting.view. Presence comes from the Participation Lease as it stands at server_time. Rows contain no Sessions, credentials, Connections, evidence, private reasons or Submission Review decisions.

parameters.description: Largest number of candidate rows to return on this page.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Cursor from next_cursor of the previous page. Send it back unchanged.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List the minimized candidate-status board for one Exam Sitting

post.description: Closes an open or paused Sitting before its deadline. Send the Sitting's current revision; the request fails if it changed since you read it. Candidates can't join or change their Workspaces from that moment. Unfinished Attempts are sealed as Submissions, not discarded, so the Sitting can stay in `closing` for a short time before it is `closed`.
post.summary: Close an open or paused Exam Sitting early with a private manager reason

post.description: Uploads the content for one resource that a live correction will add or replace. Send a multipart body with the `metadata` part first and the `content` part second. Then pass the returned `stage_id` in the correction's `resources`. The response describes the ready stage only; storage and upload details stay private.

requestBody.description: Two multipart parts in this order, the stage metadata and then the resource file.

post.summary: Stage one purpose-bound Exam Resource upload for a live Sitting correction

post.description: Publishes a corrected Exam Revision to an open or paused Sitting and switches the Sitting to it. The new Revision can't change afterwards. `resources` is the full list of resources you want, in order. A resource you leave out is removed, and its position in the array becomes its position in the Exam. A resource without `stage_id` keeps its current content. A resource with `stage_id` takes the content you uploaded to that stage. Leave out `instructions_markdown` to keep the current instructions, or send an empty string to clear them. You can't change the policy, the Starter Workspace, the Exam's default for future Sittings or the schedule here.
post.summary: Create an immutable live correction and retarget one open or paused Sitting

post.description: Needs an interactive Session and the separate `exam.records.export` permission, held through current Exam Manager status and membership of the exact Academic Unit, or through its scoped override. The caller also needs ordinary view access to every selected Submission, and a Sitting export also needs Sitting view access. An integrity export also needs current Exam Manager status on this exact Exam and the dedicated Browser Activity view permission. These are checked when the export is created, replayed, read and downloaded, and the general export override can't bypass them. Candidates can't export their own records. Personal Access Tokens are rejected. Choose work, integrity or both explicitly. The whole selected scope is captured at once, so a Sitting archive is never partial. The limits are 200 Submissions, 50,000 workspace entries, 50,000 structured records, 8 GiB of original files and 64 MiB of structured JSON. A request over any limit is rejected. The policy's export lifetime must be set to 1 to 7 days. While it is 0, exports can't be created until someone changes it. The expiry counts from when the request is made, and the archive must be built within 24 hours. The audit record, the build Job and the protection of the selected source records are saved together. A retry returns the same export and never extends its expiry. The archive holds the original workspace files, structured records, a manifest and SHA-256 hashes. Archives can't be imported back.
post.summary: Create a Sitting export

get.description: Needs an interactive Session and the separate `exam.records.export` permission, held through current Exam Manager status and membership of the exact Academic Unit, or through its scoped override. The caller also needs ordinary view access to every selected Submission, and a Sitting export also needs Sitting view access. An integrity export also needs current Exam Manager status on this exact Exam and the dedicated Browser Activity view permission. These are checked when the export is created, replayed, read and downloaded, and the general export override can't bypass them. Candidates can't export their own records. Personal Access Tokens are rejected. Only the User who requested the export can read it. Credentials, ordinary read access and the exact scope are checked again on every read. The state is `queued`, `ready`, `failed` or `expired`. An expired export never returns its content hash or anything that could fetch the archive. The expiry shown is fixed, even if the policy changes later. No storage keys or public download URLs are returned.
get.summary: Get a Sitting export

get.description: Needs an interactive Session and the separate `exam.records.export` permission, held through current Exam Manager status and membership of the exact Academic Unit, or through its scoped override. The caller also needs ordinary view access to every selected Submission, and a Sitting export also needs Sitting view access. These are checked when the export is created, replayed, read and downloaded, and the general export override can't bypass them. Candidates can't export their own records. Personal Access Tokens are rejected. Only the User who requested the export can download it, while it is ready and unexpired, with current credentials and ordinary read access. The response is an `application/zip` attachment with private, no-store caching and a safe file name. No presigned or public URL is issued. The `ETag` header and the `archive_sha256` field give the SHA-256 of the whole ZIP, and `manifest.json` lists the size and SHA-256 of each data file. Hashes detect changes but aren't a signature. Expiry blocks new downloads but doesn't cut off a download already in progress. Cleanup later checks that the archive is gone from current storage. It can't certify secure erasure of the storage media, or removal from backups, earlier object versions or replicas that operators manage.
get.summary: Download a Sitting export

post.description: Moves the deadline of an open or paused Sitting to a later time. Send the Sitting's current revision; the request fails if it changed since you read it. The server checks again that the Class is eligible and that the new deadline fits its Academic Period. You can't shorten a Sitting or reopen a closed one.
post.summary: Extend the deadline of an open or paused Exam Sitting

get.description: Lists the candidates who were members of the Class when the Sitting actually opened and who never started an Attempt. Absence never creates an Attempt or Submission. The list is available only while the Sitting is `closing` or `closed`; in any other state the request fails with a conflict.

parameters.description: Maximum number of no-show candidate identities to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged and do not parse or build it yourself.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List candidates who were Class members at actual start but never created an Attempt

post.description: Pauses an open Sitting and records your private reason. Send the Sitting's current revision; the request fails if it changed since you read it. The pause is saved before realtime notifications go out, and those notifications can be missed. After a disconnect, read the Sitting over HTTP to confirm its state.
post.summary: Pause an open Exam Sitting with a private manager reason

get.description: Needs a Session and the separate `exam.records.complete` action, held through current Exam Manager status and membership of the exact Academic Unit, or through its scoped override. Returns the completion history and counts only. Records completion is separate from closing the Sitting, and a stale completion blocks retention. Integrity categories that were already retired don't need their Reviews recreated.
get.summary: Inspect Sitting records completion

post.description: Needs a Session and the separate `exam.records.complete` action, held through current Exam Manager status and membership of the exact Academic Unit, or through its scoped override. The Sitting must be Closed, and every remaining Submission Review must be finalized or marked unnecessary for the Submission's current inventory. The revision and the integrity evidence revision you send must match the current ones. Newly accepted evidence, or an edit to a waived Review, makes the completion stale. You then acknowledge the change and complete again, which restarts the retention clock. An exact retry, or completing when the completion is already current, doesn't restart the clock. The completion, the fresh credential and permission checks, the audit record and the retry result are saved together. Completing doesn't turn on cleanup or release Retention Holds.
post.summary: Complete Sitting records

post.description: Resumes a paused Sitting. Send the Sitting's current revision; the request fails if it changed since you read it. The server checks the Exam and the delivery window again first. post.summary: Resume a paused Exam Sitting with a private manager reason

get.description: Returns the one Institution this Proctor installation serves, to a caller allowed to see it. An installation always serves exactly one Institution. The response contains no deployment secrets or infrastructure settings.

patch.description: Changes some of the Institution's name and display fields or its Exam capacity limits. The caller needs permission on the whole Institution. The update can't change the installation's identity, add another Institution or change the identifiers of anything the Institution owns.

Acceptance cannot narrow or widen the Role and scope the Invitation records, and the one-time claim is kept secret.

One failed item does not stop the others. Item keys must be unique within the request; repeated keys fail those items with `request.invalid`.

get.description: Returns one Invitation, what it grants and its state, if you may see its scope. The response never includes the one-time claim, the email contents or any credential.
get.summary: Get one Invitation within the caller's authorized scope

post.description: Replaces a pending Invitation with a new one that has the changes you ask for. If the revision you send still matches, the request revokes the Invitation and issues a new one with a new one-time claim. The old claim cannot accept the new Invitation, and the history links the two.

post.description: If the revision you send still matches, replaces the pending Invitation's one-time claim with a new one and queues the same Invitation to be emailed again. Any earlier claim stops working. The purpose, scope, Role and dates stay the same.
post.summary: Rotate the claim and resend an unchanged pending Invitation

post.description: If the revision you send still matches, revokes the pending Invitation, so its claim and any browser acceptance in progress can no longer be used. The Invitation's terms and audit history are kept. Revoking does not undo an Invitation that was already accepted.

A Job that has already finished, or whose type doesn't support cancellation, is rejected and its history is left unchanged.

A delivery addressed to a User carries `recipient_display_name` only when the caller can see that User right now. The names are looked up once for the whole page. The first page, read without a cursor, also reports `total`: the number of deliveries that match the filters and that the caller may see, across all pages. The count is exact below 10,000. At 10,000 it stops and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. Later pages carry no total, so keep the one from the first page.

Queue figures come from the most recent check by its mail maintenance monitor. Metrics never include recipients, message content, payload IDs, credentials or raw provider errors.
