Only one rotation can run at a time, and a key counts as safe to retire only when the finished Job shows that no payload uses it any more.
post.summary: Start a durable fenced mail payload-key rotation

get.description: Returns the progress of one mail key rotation Job. After the Job succeeds, it also returns the final counts that show whether the retiring key is safe to remove. Payload content, key bytes, recipients and worker diagnostics are never included.
get.summary: Inspect safe progress and final retirement proof for one mail rekey Job

parameters.description: ID of the mail key rotation Job, as returned when it was started.
parameters.name: job_id

post.description: Queues the built-in test message to the caller's own verified email address. The caller's address must be able to receive mail. The server chooses the recipient and the content, and applies its own rate limit to this endpoint. The response holds the new delivery's status, with the address masked.
post.summary: Enqueue a controlled test message to the operator's verified address

get.description: Returns the ID of the primary key this server node uses to encrypt new authenticator secrets, and the primary key the last rekey made required on every node. For each encryption key still in use, it also returns how many live authenticator secrets it encrypts and whether this node has the key configured. Use it to plan a key rotation, and to confirm that a key you are retiring encrypts nothing before you remove it from configuration. Key IDs are not secret. No key bytes, encrypted data or account details are returned.
get.summary: Inspect the MFA key ring and the live secrets each key seals

post.description: Makes this node's configured primary key the required primary key for every node, then starts one background Job. The Job re-encrypts every live authenticator secret that uses another key with the primary key, one at a time. Each secret is replaced only if it still uses the key the Job read, so a change made in the meantime is never overwritten. The Job saves its place as it goes and picks up from there after a crash or after it loses its lease. A rekey is refused while another one is queued or running. The required primary key can change to a different key only after the previous rekey proved that no live secret still needs another key. From the moment it starts, every node must encrypt new secrets with the required primary key.
post.summary: Start a durable fenced rotation of the MFA secret key

get.description: Returns the progress of one MFA rekey Job. After the Job succeeds, it also returns the counts of live secrets that prove the retiring key encrypts nothing and can be removed from configuration. The ID of a Job of any other type returns not found. No secrets, encrypted data, account details, key bytes or worker diagnostics are returned.
get.summary: Inspect safe progress and final retirement proof for one MFA rekey Job

parameters.name: file_name

requestBody.description: The UTF-8 CSV file to validate, at most 10 MiB. Uploading only creates a preview; it changes no accounts or memberships.

post.summary: Upload a bounded onboarding CSV for asynchronous validation

get.description: Returns the state, preview digest and row outcomes of one onboarding import you may read. It never includes claims, passwords, email contents, internal Job data or raw parsing diagnostics.
get.summary: Get one authorized immutable onboarding preview or final report projection

post.description: Asks to cancel the import's validation or commit Job while it can still be canceled. The work stops at its next safe point. Rows that already committed are not undone, and the uploaded file, preview and Job history are kept.
post.summary: Cooperatively cancel an onboarding parse or execution

post.description: Starts applying the preview you reviewed, but only if its revision and digest still match and the commit policy you chose allows it. Each row is applied on its own and gets its own outcome. A file that was not validated, or that changed since, is never applied. The work runs in the background; poll the import to follow it.
post.summary: Commit one exact validated onboarding preview

get.description: Downloads the preview or final row report of one import as CSV. Values a spreadsheet would run as formulas are neutralized, so they show as plain text. The report never contains credentials, one-time claims, email contents or internal worker diagnostics.
get.summary: Download the authorized formula-safe onboarding report

get.description: Lists every permission a custom Role can hold, sorted by `name`, with its title and description in the request's language, the area it belongs to, and the scopes a Role Binding can grant it at. The list is the same for every Institution and changes only with the server version. An override permission names the permission it widens in `override_of`. Permissions kept for the protected System Administrator role, and capabilities that come only from a person's relationships, are not listed. Requires role.view.
get.summary: List the permissions a Role can hold

get.description: Lists every plugin compiled into the server, ordered by name, with its state on the serving node, whether it should run, its saved settings and the JSON Schema an administration UI draws its settings form from. A Session with plugin.manage is required; Personal Access Tokens cannot read it. Plugin secrets never appear: they stay in the configuration file. A plugin nobody configured shows its default and revision 0.
get.summary: List the plugins compiled into the server

put.description: Turns one plugin on or off and replaces its settings document, under an optimistic revision fence. Requires a strong recent interactive system-administrator Session, an Idempotency-Key, and durable audit; the audit records the plugin and whether it is enabled, never setting values. Use expected_revision 0 for a plugin nobody has configured. The plugin checks the settings before they are saved and may refuse them with plugin.invalid. A required plugin cannot be turned off. A saved change applies on every node within about five seconds, without a restart, and plugin_settings_changed tells administrators' clients to refetch. A no-op keeps the revision.
put.summary: Save a plugin's settings

delete.description: Archives one Programme Level, but only when it has no active Classes. Its history is kept. Archiving never archives Classes, ends enrollments or removes Role Bindings.
delete.summary: Archive a Programme Level that has no active Classes

get.description: Returns one active Programme Level when the caller can see the Programme and Academic Unit above it. The response does not include its Classes and gives no access to their rosters.
get.summary: Get a Programme Level

patch.description: Changes some of a Programme Level's name and display fields. The Programme that owns it stays the same. Its Classes keep pointing to it, and a change that would break their structure is rejected.
patch.summary: Update a Programme Level without changing its Programme owner

get.description: Lists the active Classes of one Programme Level. Each item describes the Class itself and leaves out its roster, candidate Attempts and permission grants. Items are ordered by name, then by identifier, in the `dir` direction. The first page, read without a cursor, also reports `total`, the number of Classes across every page. It is exact below 10,000. At 10,000 counting stops and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. Later pages carry no total, so keep the first page's. Each item carries `student_count`, the Class's current members counted up to 10,000, with `student_count_is_lower_bound`, but only when the caller holds class.members.view on this Programme Level. Otherwise both are omitted.

parameters.description: Sort by name, then by identifier, ascending (`asc`, the default) or descending (`desc`). A cursor works only with the direction that produced it.
parameters.name: dir

get.summary: List Classes for a Programme Level

post.description: Creates a Class, a group of students, under the Programme Level in the path and in the Academic Period named in the body. Proctor checks the Programme Level and the Academic Period before creating it. No student is enrolled automatically.
post.summary: Create a Class for a Programme Level and Academic Period

delete.description: Archives one Programme, but only when it has no active Programme Levels. Its history is kept. Archiving never changes Programme Levels, Classes, enrollments or permissions.
delete.summary: Archive a Programme that has no active Programme Levels

get.description: Returns one active Programme when the caller can see the Academic Unit that owns it. The response does not include its Programme Levels or Classes.
get.summary: Get a Programme

patch.description: Changes some of a Programme's name and display fields. The Academic Unit that owns it stays the same. Its Programme Levels keep belonging to it and are not changed.
patch.summary: Update a Programme without changing its Academic Unit owner

get.description: Lists the active Programme Levels this Programme owns, ordered by name and then by identifier, optionally narrowed by `q`. The list does not include Classes, and seeing it does not give access to Class rosters or permissions. The first page, read without a cursor, also reports `total`, the number of Programme Levels the filters match across every page. It is exact below 10,000. At 10,000 counting stops and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. Later pages carry no total, so keep the first page's.

parameters.description: Text to find in the Programme Level name or display name, matched literally and ignoring case.
parameters.name: q

get.summary: List or search Programme Levels owned by a Programme

post.description: Creates a Programme Level owned by the Programme in the path. The caller's management permission is checked again when the request is handled. It does not create Classes, Academic Periods, enrollments or permission grants.
post.summary: Create a Programme Level owned by a Programme

get.description: Returns the Institution's retention settings. The caller needs `retention_policy.view` through a Session. Personal Access Tokens can't read it. Examination and audit periods start at zero, which means no expiry is configured, never immediate deletion. `automatic_deletion_enabled` reflects a separate cleanup approval for the current revision. Saving settings never turns cleanup on. Examination periods start at the current Sitting Records Completion. Retention Holds, supporting integrity evidence and exports being built can protect individual records. Temporary exports need a lifetime of one to seven days. Backups and earlier object versions that operators keep are outside cleanup.
get.summary: Get the Institution Retention Policy

put.description: Replaces the whole policy. Send the revision you read as `expected_revision`. The caller needs a strong, recent interactive system-administrator Session and an `Idempotency-Key`, and every change is audited. The policy, its audit record and the idempotent result are saved together. Every write, including one that changes nothing and an exact retry, checks again at write time that the caller's credential, protected administrator Role and strong recent sign-in are still valid. A stale revision fails with `retention_policy.revision_conflict` and reports `current_revision`. An exact retry returns the recorded result after authorization is checked again. A write that changes nothing keeps the revision and timestamps. All periods are required integers. Export retention accepts 0 when it isn't configured, or a lifetime of 1 to 7 days. Other periods accept 0 to 36500. That upper limit is a technical limit, not a recommended period. A day means 24 hours. Zero leaves a period unconfigured, and no export can be created while the export lifetime is unconfigured. A real change to the settings pauses approved cleanup and cancels pending grace. A new Retention Preview and a new approval are needed before cleanup schedules anything again. `candidate_notices` defaults to false when omitted, and null is rejected.
put.summary: Replace the Institution Retention Policy

get.description: Returns whether recurring cleanup is approved. The caller needs `retention_policy.view`. Approval is kept apart from the policy settings. While the control is `disabled` or `paused`, nothing is scheduled for retirement.
get.summary: Get cleanup approval

put.description: Turns recurring cleanup on or pauses it. The caller needs `retention_cleanup.manage` and a strong, recent system-administrator sign-in. Enabling ties the approval to a fresh Retention Preview of the exact policy revision, and the policy's grace period must be above zero. Every change to the control cancels existing grace. Eligible records get a new grace period when scheduling resumes. Pausing can't undo retirement that already happened, and doesn't stop the removal of stored files for records already retired. An exact retry returns the recorded result after authorization is checked again.
put.summary: Enable or pause institution cleanup

post.description: Creates a Retention Preview for the given current policy revision. The caller needs `retention_policy.view`, and the request is written to the critical audit log. The preview lasts one hour and holds counts only, never content. The counts show records that are incomplete, waiting for their deadline, held, needed as supporting integrity evidence, protected by an export or already retired. Creating a preview never schedules anything for deletion.
post.summary: Preview retention eligibility

get.description: Returns a Retention Preview as it was created, with its expiry. The caller needs `retention_policy.view`. Records may have changed since, which can change what is eligible. Every scheduling and final retirement step checks the live records again.

parameters.description: ID returned when the preview was created. Reading the preview doesn't extend its expiry.
parameters.name: retention_preview_id

get.summary: Get a retention preview

get.description: Lists the retention status of each Submission's records. The caller needs `retention_policy.view`. File names, answers, evidence and remarks are never included. `limit` counts Submissions, and each Submission adds four items: work, integrity, Browser Activity and security operational. The cursor only works with this listing. A retired category stays retired even after its detailed receipt expires. `purge_verified` counts come from a separate check that the stored objects are gone from current storage. They don't certify secure erasure of the storage media, or removal from backups, earlier object versions or downloads already in progress.

parameters.description: Maximum number of Submissions to include. Each one adds a work, an integrity, a Browser Activity and a security operational item.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` value from the previous page. Treat it as an unreadable token and pass it unchanged.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List retention eligibility and retirement status

get.description: Lists Role Bindings you can see, filtered in exactly one of three ways. Combining them fails with `request.invalid`. `user_id` lists one User's current and past Bindings inside your role_binding.view scopes. `scope_type` with `scope_id` lists every Binding at one scope you can view. Both return the whole history, newest first. `role_id`, repeated for up to 16 Roles, lists who holds those Roles now: Bindings of any listed Role that are in effect at the time of the request, on a Role and scope that are not archived, inside your role_binding.view scopes. They are sorted newest first by `created_at`, then `id`. You need Institution-wide role.view to name Roles. Without it, or for a Role that does not exist or is archived, the request fails with `request.invalid` on `role_id`. Its cursor works only with the same set of Roles. A Binding grants a Role for a period of time. Memberships and Affiliations on their own are not listed here. The first page (read without a cursor) also has `total`, the number of matching Bindings across all pages. It is exact up to 10,000. Above that it shows 10,000 and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. Later pages have no total, so keep the one from the first page.

parameters.description: Return only Bindings for this User.
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: Return only Bindings at this kind of scope, `institution`, `academic_unit` or `class`. Send it with `scope_id`.
parameters.name: scope_type

parameters.description: Return only Bindings at this Institution, Academic Unit or Class. Send it with `scope_type`.
parameters.name: scope_id

parameters.description: Return the current Bindings of any listed Role inside your role_binding.view scopes. Repeat the parameter for up to 16 Roles. A repeated Role counts once. You need Institution-wide role.view, and every Role must exist and not be archived, or the request fails with `request.invalid` on `role_id`. You can't combine it with `user_id`, `scope_type` or `scope_id`.
parameters.name: role_id

get.summary: List Role Bindings by user, scope, or Role

post.description: Grants a Role to a User at one scope, for a period of time. You must have signed in recently with a strong method. The server checks again that you may grant this Role here. The System Administrator Role can only be granted at the Institution scope.
post.summary: Create a Role Binding

delete.description: Ends a Role Binding now by setting its `end_at`. The Binding and its audit history are kept. The server refuses to end the last System Administrator's Binding. The User, Role, memberships and Affiliations are not changed.

get.description: Lists the built-in and custom Roles you can see, sorted by `name` and then `id`. A Role only names permissions. A User gets them only through a current Role Binding at a scope, and each request still checks access at that moment. Each item has `holders`, counting the current Role Bindings of that Role you can see through role_binding.view, all read at the same moment for the whole page. `holders` is left out if you hold role_binding.view nowhere.
get.summary: List Roles

post.description: Creates a custom Role with a machine name and a set of known permissions. A new Role is granted to nobody. It has no effect until you create a Role Binding for it.
post.summary: Create a custom Role

delete.description: Deletes a custom Role, unless Role Bindings that are kept still depend on it. Built-in Roles can't be deleted, and neither can a Role whose removal would break the record of current grants.

get.description: Returns one built-in or custom Role you can see, with its permissions and whether it is built in. `holders` counts the current Role Bindings of the Role you can see through role_binding.view. It is left out if you hold role_binding.view nowhere. A Role existing does not mean anyone holds it.
get.summary: Get a Role

patch.description: Changes the display name, description or full permission list of a custom Role, after checking your permission again. Built-in Roles can't be changed. A permission change can be refused when existing grants would make it unsafe.

get.description: Finds Exams by Draft title, Classes by name or display name, and Users by directory fields. Each match contains the trimmed `q` as literal text, ignoring case. Each type is checked, audited and limited exactly as its own list is: active Exams the caller may see in the Exam catalog, unarchived Classes within the caller's class.view scope, and enabled Users visible in the User directory. A requested type the caller may not list adds no items. The request is denied only when the caller may list none of the requested types. Items are grouped by type in the order exam, class, user. Each group keeps its own list's order and holds at most `limit` items. Search returns a single page and never continues: `next_cursor` is always omitted and `cursor` is rejected. Email addresses are never returned, and the search text is kept out of logs and audit records.

parameters.description: The text to find, 2 to 100 characters after surrounding spaces are removed. It is matched literally, ignoring case.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: The result types to search, repeated once per type, such as `types=exam&types=user`. Leave it out to search every type. A type may appear only once.
parameters.name: types

parameters.description: The most items to return for each type.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Not accepted. Search returns a single page and never issues `next_cursor`, so any cursor is rejected with `request.invalid`.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: Search Exams, Classes, and Users

post.description: Rechecks the same registered Session, candidate, build, Sitting and policy before storing the bounded report and its canonical digest. The server evaluates every readiness rule on the reported facts; each enforced and baseline rule must be met, and an unknown status blocks. Observed rules never block. A blocked report creates no Attempt or misconduct Flag. Retry preserves the original receipt time; Connect must consume a current eligible report within 30 seconds.
post.summary: Report minimized privileged preflight results

get.description:
Lists the student progressions that have not expired and that you could read one by one, newest first. Reading a progression needs progression authority over both its source and its destination Class, so a progression appears only when your current Institution, Academic Unit or Class progression authority covers both. Items are summaries without rows, each naming its source and destination Classes. Read one progression to see its preview or result rows.
The first page, read without a cursor, also reports `total`: the number of progressions the filters and your authority match across all pages. It is exact below 10,000; at 10,000 counting stops and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. Later pages carry no total, so keep the first page's.

parameters.description: Return only progressions in these lifecycle states. Repeat the parameter to select several; omit it for all.

parameters.description: Return only progressions from this exact source Academic Period.

parameters.name: destination_period_id

parameters.description: Return only progressions into this exact destination Class.

x-codeSamples.label: List progressions into one Class awaiting review

post.description: Starts a background Job that checks the source and destination Classes and Academic Periods without changing any enrollment. When it finishes, the progression holds a preview of each student's outcome and a digest of that preview. Review the preview, then commit it.
post.summary: Create an asynchronous dry-run for one exact student progression

get.description: Returns the preview or final result of one progression you may read. It contains no credentials, student answers or internal worker diagnostics.
get.summary: Get one authorized student progression preview or result

post.description: Asks to cancel one progression while its dry-run or commit work can still be canceled. The work stops at its next safe point. The preview and Job history are kept, and enrollment changes that already completed are not undone.
post.summary: Cooperatively cancel a student progression

post.description: Applies the dry-run preview you reviewed, but only if its revision and digest still match the current source Class, destination Class and students. For every affected student, enrollments are ended and created together in one step, and earlier enrollments keep their history. The work runs in the background; poll the progression to follow it.
post.summary: Commit one exact student progression preview

get.description: Downloads the report for one progression preview or result as CSV. Values a spreadsheet would run as formulas are neutralized, so they show as plain text. The report holds the progression's rows and no internal Job data, credentials or database selectors.
get.summary: Download the authorized formula-safe student progression report

get.description: Requires the same Submission integrity-view authorization as Attempt evidence. Returns the candidate's assistant conversation in record order: messages, replies, tool calls with their arguments and results, approvals and output checks. A command's call names its assistant:N process, whose commands are in the Attempt evidence; an edit's call is the author of the Workspace changes it made. Read it as a timeline beside the candidate's own work. The inventory is the one the seal bound. Assistant use the Exam allows raises no Flag. No-store.
get.summary: Read the assistant transcript sealed with a Submission

get.description: Requires the same Submission integrity-view authorization as Attempt evidence. Counts the sealed transcript: messages and replies, tokens, the tools used, commands, edits proposed and applied, approvals and output checks. It is descriptive only and never a score or a Flag; estimated marks token figures the server estimated. No-store.
get.summary: Summarize how the candidate used the assistant

get.description: Requires the same current Submission integrity-view authorization as detailed evidence. Returns the append-only records the core kept for the Attempt, such as the execution environment's command log, in identity order. They raise no Flag and carry no decision: a record of kind `execution.gap` says coverage was missing. Each item names its kind, the author that produced it, the author's stream sequence, and its bounded detail object, which the server stores as given. The Submission seal fixed the set, whose inventory the Review response carries. Pages contain at most 100 records. Integrity retirement removes them. No-store; cursors are purpose-specific opaque keysets.

parameters.description: Maximum number of Attempt evidence records to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Opaque continuation from the preceding Attempt evidence page.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: Inspect the Attempt evidence sealed with a Submission

get.description: Lists the Discrepancies of one Submission: integrity records that arrived after collection ended, and gaps the server could not close. They are kept separately and never change a Review that was already finalized or released.

parameters.description: Maximum number of Discrepancies to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged and do not parse or build it yourself.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List bounded late records retained after integrity collection ended

get.description: Lists the integrity Flags raised for one sealed Submission. Each summary gives the Flag's state and evidence counts. It does not include the evidence itself, private decisions, accusations or grades.

parameters.description: Maximum number of integrity Flags to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged and do not parse or build it yourself.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List bounded integrity Flag summaries for one sealed Submission

get.description: Lists the evidence kept for one Flag of the Submission. Evidence records are integrity signals, not findings of guilt and not academic judgments. Only authorized reviewers can see them.

parameters.description: Maximum number of evidence records to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged and do not parse or build it yourself.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List bounded purpose-specific evidence for one Submission Flag

get.description: Requires the same current Submission integrity-view authorization as detailed evidence. Returns every change of a native rule's status as the server evaluated it on the facts Desktop reported, with the delivery position that caused it (batch 0 is the state reported at Start), original receipt and interpretation times, and immutable stream and policy provenance. An occurrence opens when a rule becomes not met and closes when it is met again; an enforce occurrence that opens also raises its capability's native Flag. The facts themselves are not returned. Pages contain at most 100 records. Integrity retirement removes this material independently of native operational retention. No-store; cursors are purpose-specific opaque keysets.

parameters.description: Maximum number of native condition transitions to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Opaque continuation from the preceding native condition page.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: Inspect the native rule status changes of a Submission

get.description: Requires the same Submission view authorization as Attempt evidence. Reports one row per guest port used before the seal, including completed connections, byte counts and times. Preview content is never recorded. The summary raises no Integrity Flags.

200.description: Preview usage bound to the sealed Submission

get.summary: Read sealed preview usage

get.description: Returns the Review of one Submission as a manager sees it: the Review itself, the current decision for each Flag, counts and the integrity state. It includes private review fields. Candidates see only the released result, never this response.
get.summary: Get the authorized manager Review snapshot

put.description: Creates the Review, or replaces its private manager notes and the remarks approved for the candidate. Send the Review's current revision; the request fails if it changed since you read it. A finalized Review can't change. Repeating the request with the same Idempotency-Key does not repeat audit records or notifications.
put.summary: Create or revise private notes and approved student remarks

put.description: Creates or replaces the one current decision for a Flag. Send the decision's and the Review's current revisions; the request fails if either changed since you read them. The outcome is an integrity decision, not an academic one: never a grade or a verdict of guilt. The rationale stays private.
put.summary: Create or revise the one current decision for a Flag

post.description: Finalizes a Review at its current revision. Every required decision must be made and the integrity data must be complete first. Finalizing freezes the Review's private content and records a digest of the evidence it covered. Records that arrive later become Discrepancies and can't change what was finalized.
post.summary: Freeze the complete Review and bounded evidence inventory

post.description: Releases the result of a finalized Review to the candidate. The candidate sees only the remarks you approved. Manager notes, rationales, Flags, evidence, Discrepancies and other private review data stay hidden.
post.summary: Explicitly release the approved candidate result projection

get.description: Tells a Proctor Desktop build whether the server is available and whether that build can work with it. When the server can't decide, the answer is not compatible. The build details are what Desktop reports about itself, and the server does not verify the binary. Every well-formed request gets 200, even for an unsupported build or while the server is unavailable. Malformed parameters get a Problem Details error. The response never reveals the installation's identity, sign-in settings, identity providers, build details or update locations.

parameters.description: Desktop's semantic version, such as `1.4.2`, without a leading `v`.
parameters.name: desktop_release

parameters.description: The build ID of this signed Desktop build.
parameters.name: desktop_build_id

parameters.description: Desktop's operating system, such as `darwin`, `win32` or `linux`. Any other well-formed value gets `unsupported_target`.
parameters.name: platform

parameters.description: Desktop's processor architecture, such as `arm64` or `x64`. Any other well-formed value gets `unsupported_target`.
parameters.name: architecture

parameters.description: The realtime protocol version Desktop speaks, 1 or higher.
parameters.name: realtime_protocol

get.summary: Check product availability and Desktop compatibility

get.description: Lists the optional features compiled into the server that are active on the serving node, ordered by name, so a client can show only what this server supports. A plugin that is turned off, failed to activate, or has since failed is not listed. The response carries no plugin settings or diagnostics.
get.summary: List the plugins active on this server

get.description: Returns the version and build details of the server node that answers. It contains no configuration, credentials, service addresses or installation identity.
get.summary: Get build and version information

get.description: Searches the Users you can see through your Institution-wide or scoped permissions. Results are sorted by username, then ID, unless `sort` and `dir` say otherwise. Disabled Users are hidden unless you hold Institution-wide user.view and ask for them. Each item has a `summary`: the User's current Affiliations with the current Academic Units you can see and, if you hold role_binding.view, their current Role Bindings inside your scopes. Each list is short and ends with a count of the rest. The first page (read without a cursor) also has `total`, the number of matching Users across all pages. It is exact up to 10,000. Above that it shows 10,000 and `total_is_lower_bound` is true. Later pages have no total, so keep the one from the first page.

parameters.description: Text to find, case-insensitively, anywhere in the User fields you can see. It is matched literally.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: With `true`, also returns disabled Users. It works only with Institution-wide user.view. With scoped permissions, disabled Users are always left out.
parameters.name: include_disabled

parameters.description: Keeps Users who have a current Affiliation of any listed kind. Repeat the parameter for several kinds, each kind at most once. Filters only narrow what you can already see.
parameters.name: affiliation

parameters.description: Keeps Users who are current members of this Academic Unit or any unit below it. A unit outside your user.view scope returns an empty page, not an error.
parameters.name: academic_unit_id

parameters.description: Keeps Users who hold a current Role Binding of any listed Role inside your role_binding.view scopes, so it matches only Bindings the `summary` could show. Without role_binding.view you get an empty page. Repeat the parameter for up to 16 Roles. You need Institution-wide role.view to name Roles. Without it, or for a Role that does not exist or is archived, the request fails with `request.invalid` on `role_id`. Filters only narrow what you can already see.
parameters.name: role_id

parameters.description: Keeps only `active` or only `disabled` accounts. As with `include_disabled`, only Institution-wide user.view can see disabled Users, so with scoped permissions `disabled` returns an empty page. You can't combine it with `include_disabled=true`.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description: With `true`, keeps Users who have never signed in. Activity is first recorded when a User gets a Session. Only Institution-wide user.view can filter on activity; anyone else gets `request.invalid`. You can't combine it with `last_active_after` or `last_active_before`.
parameters.name: never_signed_in

parameters.description: Keeps Users last active at or after this RFC 3339 time. A User who was never active does not match. Only Institution-wide user.view can filter on activity; anyone else gets `request.invalid`.
parameters.name: last_active_after

parameters.description: Keeps Users last active before this RFC 3339 time. It must be later than `last_active_after`. A User who was never active does not match. Only Institution-wide user.view can filter on activity; anyone else gets `request.invalid`.
parameters.name: last_active_before

parameters.description: Sort order, with User ID breaking ties: `username` (the default), `name`, `created` or `last_active`. `name` is the display name, or the username when there is none, compared case-insensitively on its first 64 characters. `last_active` puts Users who were never active as least recent, and only Institution-wide user.view can use it; anyone else gets `request.invalid`. A cursor works only with the sort and direction that produced it.
parameters.name: sort

parameters.description: Ascending (`asc`, the default) or descending (`desc`) by the `sort` key.
parameters.name: dir

get.summary: Search the authorized User directory

get.description: Returns your own User profile. It never includes password data, identity-provider claims, Session or Personal Access Token secrets, or your Role Bindings.
get.summary: Get the authenticated User profile

get.description: Returns one page of the current Session User's own account history, newest first unless `order=asc` asks for oldest first. The first page, read without a cursor, also carries `total`: the number of events the filters match across every page, exact below 10,000 and reported as 10,000 with `total_is_lower_bound` at that limit. Later pages carry no total, so keep the first page's. Reading the first page oldest first reaches the end of the history without counting pages. The history holds events about the User's account, whoever performed them, and account-relevant events the User performed on anything else. Each item carries an `event` name from a fixed list that can grow, and clients write their own labels for it. Records outside that list and unfinished attempts are never returned. No item carries another person's identity: the actor is only `self`, `administrator`, or `system`, and the IP address and user agent appear only on the User's own actions. A resource identity appears only when the resource is the User, the Institution, or an Academic Unit or Class the User has or had a membership or Role Binding at. Each item also carries a `summary` sentence in the language `Accept-Language` selects, falling back to the installation language and then English. It keeps the same mask: the actor is "you", "an administrator", or "the system", and whoever acted on the User is never named. When the User acted on another User, the sentence names that User only while the User can see them now through the User directory's visibility, as the institution audit list does, and otherwise says "a user". It names an Academic Unit or Class only where the resource identity appears, and a Role only when the event bound it to the User. Otherwise it uses a generic noun such as "a class". The page also carries `runs`: each stretch of two or more consecutive items on the page with the same actor kind, event, recorded operation, status, and relation, with a plural `summary` such as "You changed 5 profile pictures". Items stay unchanged and individually addressable. A run never reaches past the page, so a stretch the page edge cuts reads as two runs, or the client fetches the next page before folding the last one. Each run's count is exact for the items it covers. Events that cannot follow one another, such as turning on two-step verification, never form a run. Personal Access Tokens cannot read this history. Reading it records no authorization decision.

parameters.description: Return only events recorded at or after this RFC 3339 time.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Return only events recorded before this RFC 3339 time. It must be later than `created_after`.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Return only these events. Repeat the parameter to select several, or leave it out for all.
parameters.name: event

parameters.description: Return only events with this outcome.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Return only events about the User's account (`subject`) or only events the User performed on anything else (`actor`). Omit it for both.
parameters.name: relation

parameters.description: Read newest first (`desc`, the default) or oldest first (`asc`). A cursor continues only the order that produced it.
parameters.name: order

get.summary: List the current User's own account history

get.description: Returns what a client needs to build navigation for the current Session: the product areas you can open, up to 20 scopes you manage, and any Attempt you have not finished. It contains no Roles, permissions, identity-provider claims, credentials or Exam content. It does not prove you may do anything, and it must never be cached.
get.summary: Get the signed-in User's bounded product context

get.description: Lists the current User's Desktop Registrations, newest first, including revoked ones. Each entry has its name and the Desktop build details. Public keys, key thumbprints, proofs and Session IDs are never returned.
get.summary: List the current User's Desktop Registrations

delete.description: Revokes one Desktop Registration for good. It needs an interactive Session that has passed two-step verification and has signed in or reauthenticated recently. In the same step, every Session bound to the registration is revoked, along with its access and refresh credentials.

patch.description: Gives one of the current User's active Desktop Registrations the name they chose. The name is trimmed, loses bidirectional and invisible formatting code points, and must be 1 to 128 characters without control characters. It labels the device in the User's own registration and Session lists, and a later Desktop sign-in with the same key keeps it instead of the device name the Desktop reports. Renaming changes no key, Session or credential, so any interactive Session can do it without a recent sign-in. A Personal Access Token can't. Sending the same name again gives the same result. A revoked registration is kept as security history and can't be renamed. Another User's registration returns not found. Every rename is audited and appears in the User's own account history.

get.description: Lists your own Exam Sittings with their current state and what you can do now, for a Web or Desktop Session. Review results are hidden until they are released. The actions are hints for navigation only: each destination checks your access again. Personal Access Tokens can't use this operation.

parameters.description: Maximum number of Sittings to return in this page.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page, sent back unchanged. If the server rejects it, start again from the first page.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List the signed-in candidate's Exam activity

get.description: Returns the current User's two-step verification status. It says whether two-step verification is on, whether a setup is waiting to be finished, and how many of the User's recovery codes are still unused. It also says when the User's own password last changed, how long the recent sign-in window is and, while this Session is inside that window, when it ends. Authenticator secrets, recovery codes and passwords are never returned here.
get.summary: Get current-user MFA status

post.description: Checks a current authenticator code against the pending setup, turns on two-step verification and returns a new set of recovery codes. The codes are shown only in this response. A setup that has expired or was replaced by a newer one can't be activated.
post.summary: Activate pending MFA setup

post.description: Checks a current authenticator code or one unused recovery code, then marks the current interactive Session as having passed two-step verification. A recovery code is used up as part of the same step and can't be used again.
post.summary: Upgrade the current session with MFA

post.description: Turns off two-step verification for the current User and cancels any pending setup and all recovery codes. It needs an interactive Session that has passed two-step verification and has signed in or reauthenticated recently. The change is recorded in the audit log. It is refused with mfa.required_by_policy when the Access Policy requires the User to use two-step verification.
post.summary: Disable current-user MFA

post.description: Cancels the current recovery codes and returns a new set, each usable once. The codes are shown only in this response, so store them safely. It needs an interactive Session that has passed two-step verification and has signed in or reauthenticated recently. A Personal Access Token can't be used.
post.summary: Regenerate MFA recovery codes

post.description: Starts setting up an authenticator app for two-step verification. It creates a short-lived pending setup, replacing any earlier one, and returns its secret and provisioning URI once so the app can be set up. Two-step verification is not on until a valid code is sent to the activate operation.
post.summary: Begin MFA setup

get.description: Returns the signed-in User's own notices about records entering deletion grace, with each notice's cancellation and delivery status. A notice grants no access to examination records. Reading it doesn't acknowledge delivery or change cleanup. Responsible Exam Managers and Institution operators get notices by default. Candidates get them only when the policy turns candidate notices on. When grace is canceled, the dates a notice gave no longer apply. Each notice names the Exam title and the Sitting's scheduled times so the recipient can tell which records it covers. It includes no candidate, answer or evidence content.

parameters.description: Maximum number of notices to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` value from the previous page. Treat it as an unreadable token and pass it unchanged.
parameters.name: cursor

get.summary: List my retention notices

get.description: Lists the current User's active Sessions, newest first, with their device, sign-in, activity and expiry details. Access tokens, refresh tokens, provider subject IDs and other credentials are left out.
get.summary: List the current user's sessions

post.description: Revokes one Session, but only when it belongs to the current User. It can be a Session on another device. If it is the Session making this request, that Session stops working right away.
post.summary: Revoke one current-user session

post.description: Revokes every active Session of the current User, including the Session making the request, so the caller is signed out too. Afterwards, clients must throw away cached credentials and sign in again. To stay signed in on this device, use revokeOtherCurrentUserSessions instead.
post.summary: Revoke all current-user sessions

post.description: Revokes every active Session of the current User except the Session making the request. That Session stays signed in, and its cookies and credentials are left in place. The response says how many Sessions were revoked, which is zero when no other Session was active. A Personal Access Token has no Session to keep, so it is refused.
post.summary: Sign out every other current-user session

patch.description: Sets the device name of one of the current User's live browser or CLI Sessions. The name is trimmed, loses bidirectional and invisible formatting code points, and must be 1 to 128 characters without control characters. A Desktop Session is named by its Desktop Registration, so renaming one is refused with session.desktop_named_by_registration, whose fields.desktop_registration_id names the registration to rename through renameDesktopRegistration instead. Renaming changes no credential, so any interactive Session can do it without a recent sign-in. A Personal Access Token can't. Sending the same name again gives the same result. A Session of another User, or one that is revoked or expired, returns not found. Every rename is audited and appears in the User's own account history.

get.description: Returns your settings document exactly as it was saved, with its format version, revision and whether you can replace it. The server does not rewrite the document or add fields to it. The response is private and must not be stored by shared caches.
get.summary: Get the signed-in User's exact settings.json source

put.description: Checks and replaces your whole settings document. `expected_revision` must match the current revision, so an update from another client is never overwritten: a stale revision fails with `user_settings.revision_conflict`. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first result.
put.summary: Conditionally replace the signed-in User's exact settings.json source

get.description: Lists the current User's Personal Access Tokens, newest first, with their scopes, expiry and whether they are disabled or revoked. The secret token value is shown only once, when the token is created, and never appears in this list.
get.summary: List current-user Personal Access Tokens

post.description: Creates a Personal Access Token with limited scopes and a fixed expiry. The interactive Session must have signed in or reauthenticated recently. The response shows the secret token value once, and Proctor never shows it again. Proctor checks that the current User may grant every requested scope at the requested Academic Unit, or across the Institution when no Academic Unit is given, and that the expiry is within the allowed lifetime.
post.summary: Create a Personal Access Token

get.description: Returns the Personal Access Token scopes the current User may grant right now, each with a title and description in the request's language. A scope with `institution_wide` set can be granted without an Academic Unit limit, or limited to any Academic Unit. Any other scope can be granted only when limited to one of its `academic_unit_ids` or to a unit below one of them. `academic_units` lists at most 50 of those top Academic Units, sorted by display name, and `academic_units_has_more` says whether there are more. Scopes the User can't grant anywhere are left out. Creating a token checks the User's permissions again.
get.summary: List grantable Personal Access Token scopes

x-codeSamples.label: List grantable Personal Access Token scopes

delete.description: Revokes one of the current User's Personal Access Tokens for good. The revocation is saved and recorded in the audit log. The token can't be restored or swapped for a replacement.

post.description: Disables one of the current User's Personal Access Tokens, so requests that use it stop working until it is enabled again. The token record and its audit history are kept, so it can be reviewed or enabled later.
post.summary: Disable a Personal Access Token

post.description: Enables a disabled Personal Access Token that has not expired. The interactive Session must have signed in or reauthenticated recently, and Proctor checks again that the User may still grant the token's scopes. A revoked token can't be enabled.
post.summary: Enable a Personal Access Token

get.description: Returns one User's profile if you can currently see that User through Institution-wide or scoped permissions. Unrelated Users, and disabled Users when you have only scoped permissions, stay hidden.
get.summary: Get a contextually visible User profile

patch.description: Changes some profile fields of a User, after checking your permission on that User. It changes only names, locale and time zone. Email, sign-in methods, account state, memberships and Role Bindings each have their own operations.

get.description: Lists the current and past Affiliations of one User that you may see. A User can hold several Affiliations at once. Affiliations describe the person and are never used in place of Role Bindings to check permissions.
get.summary: List a User's effective-dated Affiliations

post.description: Adds one student, teacher, staff or external Affiliation to an existing User, with optional start and end times. Other kinds of Affiliation can exist at the same time, and adding one grants no permissions or credentials.
post.summary: Create a non-exclusive effective-dated Affiliation

post.description: Disables a User and ends all their active Sessions in the same step. It checks your permission first, and refuses to disable the last System Administrator. The User's Affiliations, memberships, Role Bindings, Attempts, Submissions and audit records are kept. An optional `reason` goes only into the audit record. It is not stored on the User, and Academic Unit auditors never see it.

requestBody.description: An optional reason for the audit record. Send no body to disable without a reason.

post.summary: Disable a User account and revoke its active sessions

x-codeSamples.source:
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://proctor.example.edu/api/v1/users/wj3drgzdpnf54rxf5d8qd3dqne/disable' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  --header 'X-Proctor-CSRF-Token: <session-csrf-token>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"reason": "Left the institution"}'

put.description: Changes a User's email address. You must have signed in recently with a strong method. The new address starts unverified. The new address gets a verification link, and the old address gets a one-time link to undo the change, valid for the configured undo period. Changes to one account count against its account-recovery rate limit. Your administrator permissions are never taken as proof that the User owns the new address.
put.summary: Explicitly change a User email address and require verification

post.description: Marks a User's current email address as verified, as an administrator action. You must have signed in recently with a strong method. It does not change the address, enable a disabled account, bring back Sessions, or skip the usual permission checks.
post.summary: Privileged verification of a User email address

post.description: Enables a disabled User, after checking your permission. History is kept. It does not bring back ended Sessions, verify the email address, add sign-in methods, restart ended memberships or recreate Role Bindings.
post.summary: Enable a User account without restoring revoked sessions

post.description: Resets another User's two-step verification after the Institution has checked who they are. The caller needs the protected system-administrator action user.mfa.reset and an interactive Session that has passed two-step verification and has signed in or reauthenticated recently. An administrator can't reset their own two-step verification. The Institution checks the person's identity outside Proctor and records a short reference to that check here. In one step, Proctor cancels the User's old authenticator and recovery codes, revokes all their Sessions and Personal Access Tokens, and cancels unfinished access grants. The audit record and the security notice email are saved in the same step, and the reset fails if either can't be. When the User next signs in with their password or provider, they get a limited Web Session. Normal access returns once they set up a new authenticator app. Their linked provider identities and password stay as they were. The request fails when authenticator setup is not available, or when it would leave no administrator able to sign in. Each new reset starts a new recovery round.
post.summary: Reset another User's local MFA after institution verification

delete.description: Removes a User's custom picture so the default picture shows again, and returns the updated profile. If-Match must name the current custom picture, so you can't remove a newer upload by mistake. The stored files are deleted after the change is saved.

parameters.description: The ETag of the custom picture to remove, from any of its sizes.
parameters.name: If-Match

delete.summary: Remove the custom profile picture and return to the retained default

get.description: Returns the User's profile picture as a square WebP image, served directly rather than through a public or signed storage link. The response has an ETag and may be cached privately. Send If-None-Match to get 304 when the image has not changed. Every request checks again that you can see the User, so disabled Users stay hidden from scoped viewers.

parameters.description: Width and height of the image in pixels, 128, 256 or 512.
parameters.name: size

parameters.description: One or more ETags from earlier responses. If one matches, you get 304 with no body.
parameters.name: If-None-Match

get.summary: Get an authorized normalized profile-picture rendition

put.description: Uploads a new custom profile picture for a User. Proctor checks the image and converts it to WebP at 128, 256 and 512 pixels before saving it. When you replace an existing custom picture, send If-Match so you can't overwrite a newer upload by mistake.

parameters.description: The ETag of the current custom picture, from any of its sizes, when you replace it. Omit it for the first custom upload.
parameters.name: If-Match

requestBody.description: The image file as raw PNG, JPEG or WebP bytes. The server checks it and stores WebP copies at 128, 256 and 512 pixels.

put.summary: Upload and normalize a custom profile picture

get.description: Returns one page of the given User's Sessions, newest first, when the caller currently has the administrative permission to see them. Each entry describes the device, sign-in, activity and expiry of a Session. Revoked and expired Sessions are left out unless include_revoked asks for them. Access and refresh credentials are never returned.

parameters.description: Also return revoked Sessions, with their revocation time and reason.
parameters.name: include_revoked

parameters.description: Maximum number of Sessions to return.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The next_cursor value from the previous page. Leave it out to get the first page.
parameters.name: cursor

schema.description: A cursor from the previous page. Treat it as a token and don't read or change it.

get.summary: List a User's Sessions for administrative review

post.description: Revokes every active Session of the given User, after checking that the caller is allowed to. The revocation and its audit record are saved before the response reports success.
post.summary: Revoke every active Session for a User

x-codeSamples.label: Revoke all Sessions for a User

delete.description: Revokes one Session of the given User. Proctor first checks that the Session belongs to that User and that the caller is still allowed to do this. The operation never takes or returns Session credentials.
delete.summary: Revoke one Session belonging to a User

get.description: Opens a Proctor WebSocket connection for a signed-in Session. The first `hello` message gives the connection's ID and its starting sequence number, which goes up with every message. To reconnect, send the old `connection_id` and the last `sequence_number` you processed. If the same server node still has the missed messages, it sends them again. Otherwise it sends `resync_required`, and the client should reload its state.

parameters.description: The ID of an earlier connection to resume. Send it with `sequence_number`.
parameters.name: connection_id

parameters.description: The last sequence number you processed on that connection. Zero is allowed. Send it with `connection_id`.
parameters.name: sequence_number

get.summary: Upgrade to the WebSocket protocol

get.description: Reports whether this server process is running and can answer. It does not mean the services it depends on are ready, or that the node should get traffic.
get.summary: Check process liveness

get.description: Reports whether this node and the services it needs are ready for traffic. When it fails, stop sending traffic to the node, and use the liveness check to decide whether to restart it.
get.summary: Check service readiness
